calls.title: Under My Skin Issue #2 — Euphoria
calls.description: Second issue of Under My Skin, the magazine published by the California Aggregation for Gender Diversity, a nonprofit building community, resources and public education around Transgender, Genderqueer, Intersex and Nonbinary (TGIN+) history and art. The issue asks Transgender, Genderqueer, Intersex and Nonbinary artists how they experience euphoria — a counterpoint to the clinical framing of gender dysphoria, and an attempt to imagine what affirming care for gender euphoria might look like. Photography and all other forms of visual art are welcome alongside poems, essays and articles; music and film can be promoted even though they cannot be printed on paper. Submissions are especially encouraged from artists who are multiply marginalised, chronically ill, disabled, trans, intersex, undocumented, incarcerated or formerly incarcerated, low-income and otherwise systemically excluded, and contributors may use a pseudonym. Contributors receive a digital copy of the published issue, credit lines and artwork descriptions alongside their images, and promotion through the organisation's website and social channels.

calls.title: LSI 2026 Photography Grant
calls.description: Tenth edition of the Leica Society International's annual project-based grant, supported by the LSI Philanthropy Fund and Leica North America. Applications include a project description, a portfolio of 10 JPEG images from the project, a bio, and a CV. Entries are capped at 200 applications; the call closes on 4 September or when the cap is reached, whichever comes first.

calls.title: Tasweer Residency 2026–2027: As the Image Unfolds
calls.description: The second edition of the residency from Tasweer, Qatar's photo festival organised by Qatar Museums. Three emerging photographers and visual storytellers based in Qatar, aged 21+, are selected for a five-month residency (1 October 2026 – 1 March 2027) at Bayt Al Wakrah in historic Old Al Wakrah City. Built around the concept of 'athar' — an Arabic word for traces, imprints and legacies — residents develop a project across documentary, conceptual, or experimental image-making. Each receives studio space at Bayt Al Wakrah, mentorship and professional development, access to local networks, and a monthly stipend of 4,000 QAR. Completed projects are presented in the exhibition 'As the Image Unfolds — The Language of Athar' during the 2027 Tasweer Photo Festival, accompanied by an online zine documenting the process. Apply with a cover letter, artist bio and statement, CV, a 15–20 image portfolio (PDF), a residency statement of intent, and 1–2 recommendation letters. Free to apply.

calls.description: The 10th edition of the Singapore Young Photographer Award (SYPA), organised by DECK Photography Art Centre, the non-profit behind the Singapore International Photography Festival. This year's theme, "Echoes of Home", asks young photographers to reflect on what defines home — exploring the stories, history and heritage of place and the relationships between people, their environments, and their origins. Two age categories: Junior (13–18) submit a portfolio of 5–7 images drawn from at least three of five subjects (architecture, nature, landscape, portrait, still life); Youth (19–25) submit a connected photo series of 7–10 images. Finalists' work is exhibited during the Singapore International Photography Festival in October 2026. Free to enter; open to photographers aged 13–25 based in Singapore.

prose: The Singapore Young Photographer Award (SYPA) is an annual award organised by DECK Photography Art Centre, a registered Singapore charity and the organiser of the Singapore International Photography Festival. Now in its 10th edition, the award nurtures the next generation of Singapore-based image-makers aged 13 to 25.

The 2026 theme, "Echoes of Home", invites entrants to reflect on what home means to them and to those around them — the stories, history and heritage of place, and the interrelationships between people, their environments, and their origins. Submissions are made in two age categories: Junior (13–18), a portfolio of 5–7 images drawn from at least three of five subjects (architecture, nature, landscape, portrait, still life); and Youth (19–25), a connected photo series of 7–10 images.

Over $8,000 in prizes is awarded across the categories, including cash, Nikon cameras, rental vouchers and certificates. Finalists are announced in August 2026, winners in September, and the finalist works are exhibited at an awards ceremony during the Singapore International Photography Festival in October 2026. Entry is free, with submissions made through Judgify.

All accepted works are professionally printed at around 40 inches wide at no cost to the artist, sponsored by Fort Worth Camera, the Print Refinery and Red River Paper. Open internationally to photographers 18 and over; submit up to 12 images. Works previously exhibited in a TPS show are not eligible.

calls.description: 14th biennial juried exhibition from PhotoMidwest, the Madison, Wisconsin photography nonprofit, presented in collaboration with Promega Art Showcases. Juror Karen Irvine, Chief Curator and Deputy Director of the Museum of Contemporary Photography at Columbia College Chicago, awards a $1,000 Best of Show and three $250 Images of Distinction. The exhibition runs September 17, 2026 – February 26, 2027 across Promega's Art Showcase gallery, PhotoMidwest Studio and UW–Madison's Pyle Center. calls.title: Penland Resident Artist Program
calls.description: Penland School of Craft's long-running residency for professional craft artists at a pivotal moment in their practice, on its campus in the North Carolina mountains. Two options are offered: a 1-year project-based residency and a 3-year career-transition residency, both beginning March 15, 2027. Photography is among the accepted media alongside books, clay, drawing and painting, glass, iron, letterpress, metals, paper, printmaking, textiles and wood (hot glass excluded this cycle). Residents receive a private studio and apartment with utilities included, meals while school is in session, one tuition-free workshop annually and studio representation at the Penland Gallery — no housing or studio rental fees. No prior connection to Penland is required; reduced application fees are available on request.
calls.summary: 1-year and 3-year residencies at Penland School of Craft — private studio, housing and meals; photography included.

calls.title: Penland Winter Residency 2027
calls.description: A self-directed project residency during Penland's quiet winter season, offering artists two- or four-week sessions of studio time and equipment access with no classes, assignments or critiques. Residents work independently in one of Penland's teaching studios — photography is among the available studios, alongside books, clay, drawing and painting, glass, iron, letterpress, metals, papermaking, printmaking, textiles and wood — with studio assistants on hand for orientation and equipment help. Sessions run January 3–15 and January 17–29, 2027; the residency fee is $500 for two weeks (more for flameworking and hot shop) plus housing, and limited fellowships cover the residency fee and partial housing, with preference given to first-time applicants and artists from underrepresented backgrounds. Open to artists at any career stage who are comfortable working independently.
calls.summary: Self-directed 2- or 4-week winter residency at Penland with studio and equipment access; photography included. Fellowships available.
jury: National panel of artist peers, curators & Penland staff

calls.description: Public art exhibition on bus shelter advertising space in Miami, FL, curated by Miami-based artist Hermes Berrío. calls.summary: Miami bus-shelter public art show curated by Hermes Berrío. Theme: the beauty and weight of everyday life.

Open to artists of all ages and backgrounds; photography welcome. Selected works are displayed on NYC billboards for at least one month starting July 24, 2026. SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has run public art billboard exhibitions since 2015; fees are structured as tax-deductible donations supporting exhibition production.
calls.summary: NYC billboard public art show on immigrant experience — making home in unfamiliar places and building new community.
prose: SaveArtSpace is a non-profit that has placed artists' work on commercial billboard and transit advertising space since 2015, giving artists a public platform far larger than a gallery wall.

"Home Is Where I Make It" takes as its theme the various experiences of making homes in places unknown, celebrating how immigrants and their children build new rituals and communities far from where they began.

The call invites artists of all ages and backgrounds, with photography welcome. Selected works are displayed on billboard advertising space in New York City for at least one month starting July 24, 2026.
Submission is $35 for one to three images and $10 for each additional image, structured as a tax-deductible donation supporting exhibition production. The deadline is June 8, 2026.

calls.title: The Open Road: Endless Horizons
calls.description: International photography competition from the International Photography Hall of Fame and Museum (IPHF) marking the 100th anniversary of Route 66. Photographers worldwide are invited to reflect on the spirit of the open road — wanderlust, resilience, and discovery — in their own environments. Selected works are featured in an online exhibition at iphf.org. Awards: Grand Prize $1,000, First Place $500, Second Place $250, Third Place $100. Jurors: Susan Hacker Stang (photographer/educator), Shellee Graham (photographer and Route 66 ambassador), and Jim Ross (Route 66 historian). Open internationally to artists 18+; work must be original and not previously exhibited at IPHF. AI-generated or significantly AI-altered work is not eligible.
calls.summary: IPHF international competition marking Route 66's centennial — the spirit of the open road. Online exhibition + cash prizes.
prose: The International Photography Hall of Fame and Museum (IPHF) is a St. Louis institution that honors the medium's most influential practitioners and runs exhibitions and competitions open to photographers worldwide. "The Open Road: Endless Horizons" is its themed call marking the 100th anniversary of Route 66, America's iconic "Mother Road."

The brief asks photographers to reflect on the enduring spirit of the road as a symbol of history, movement, and possibility — wanderlust, resilience, and discovery — interpreted in their own environments anywhere in the world, not just along Route 66 itself.

Selected works are presented in an online exhibition at iphf.org. Awards are Grand Prize $1,000, First Place $500, Second Place $250, and Third Place $100, with one prize per person. The jury is Susan Hacker Stang, a photographer and educator; Shellee Graham, a photographer and Route 66 ambassador; and Jim Ross, a Route 66 historian.

Eligibility is international for artists 18 and older. Work must be two-dimensional photography from traditional or digital processes, original, and never before exhibited at IPHF or on its website. Three-dimensional work and photographs created primarily with or significantly altered by generative AI are not eligible.

Entry is via CaFÉ (CallForEntry.org). The first three images are free for IPHF Photographer's Circle members and above; non-members pay $35 for the first three, with additional images $10 each up to ten total. The deadline is June 21, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. CDT.

calls.title: forgotten
calls.description: Online juried exhibition exploring the forgotten — abandoned, buried, erased, lost, repressed, bygone, neglected, vanished. Juror Ann Mitchell, a Southern California artist, curator, and educator (BFA Art Center College of Design, MFA Claremont Graduate University) whose work explores landscape, memory, and transformation. Up to 47 images selected; 27 featured in the hardbound "The 27" exhibition book. Awards: Juror's Award (online solo exhibition, book, blog feature), Directors' Award (book, blog feature), Visitors' Award ($100 for most Instagram likes). Exhibition July 31 – September 10, 2026 online, with reception August 29 at 3pm CST.
calls.summary: Themed online juried show on the forgotten — lost, buried, neglected, vanished. Juror Ann Mitchell. 47 images selected.
prose: A Smith Gallery is a Texas Hill Country photography gallery in Johnson City, Texas. "forgotten" is the gallery's themed call exploring what has been abandoned, buried, erased, lost, repressed, neglected, or vanished — a wide field of bygone, suppressed, and discarded subjects.

Up to 47 images are selected for the online exhibition; 27 of those are featured in a hardbound exhibition book, "The 27." The exhibition runs July 31 through September 10, 2026, presented online with a reception on August 29 at 3pm CST posted in the gallery's ASG Conversations.

The juror is Ann Mitchell, a Southern California–based artist, curator, and educator who holds a BFA in Photography from Art Center College of Design and an MFA from Claremont Graduate University. She taught at Long Beach City College for over twenty years; her own work explores landscape, memory, and transformation.

Awards: the Juror's Award includes an online solo exhibition, the hardbound book, and a blog feature. The Directors' Award includes the book and a blog feature. The Visitors' Award is $100 cash for the most Instagram likes during the exhibition.

Eligibility is open globally. Images are submitted at 1800 pixels on the longest side, JPEG, 72 ppi, with no watermarks. AI-generated images are not accepted. Entry fee is $40 for the first 5 images, $5 per additional image, with no submission limit. The 2026 deadline is July 6.

calls.title: Personality: The Face and Its Absence
calls.description: Curated international group photography exhibition exploring personality and portraiture beyond the traditional face — through the body, objects, spaces, traces, absence, or symbolic associations. All creative photographic interpretations welcome, including AI-generated photo-based images. Curated by Zsolt Bátori (PhD; founder/director PH21 Gallery; Photolucida board member) and Borbála Jász (art historian; Photolucida juror). Curator's choice receives three free entries for future PH21 exhibitions; honorable mentions also recognized. Special rate for students, unwaged, and low-income economies (€15–20). Early bird deadline June 15 at reduced rates; final deadline June 30. Exhibition at PH21 Gallery in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter, August 22 – September 15, 2026.
jury: Zsolt Bátori, Photographer & Philosophy of Art
Borbála Jász, Art Historian & Philosophy of Art
calls.summary: Curated group show on personality and portraiture beyond the face. Exhibition in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter, Aug–Sep. Student rates.
prose: PH21 Gallery is a curatorial gallery operating from Barcelona's Gothic Quarter. "Personality: The Face and Its Absence" is the gallery's themed call inviting photographers to explore personality and portraiture beyond traditional facial depiction — through the body, objects, spaces, traces, absence, or symbolic association.

All creative photographic interpretations are welcome, from traditional portraits and selfies to photomontages and AI-generated photo-based images. The brief favors work in which personality surfaces by indirect means as readily as by the face itself.

The 2026 exhibition runs August 22 through September 15, 2026 at PH21's Barcelona gallery in the Gothic Quarter. The Curator's Choice winner receives three free entries for future PH21 themed group exhibition calls (up to 15 images each); honorable mentions are also recognized.

Selection is by curators Zsolt Bátori (PhD, founder and director of PH21 Gallery, Photolucida board member) and Borbála Jász (art historian, Photolucida juror). Acceptance is competitive — curators have final selection authority.

Entry fees are tiered. Standard rates run €25–€45 for 3 to 15 photos at early bird (closing June 15, 2026), rising to €30–€50 at final deadline (June 22, 2026). Discounted rates of €15 (early bird) or €20 (final) are available for students, unwaged persons, and applicants from low-income economies. A series may contain up to 5 photographs. Submissions are made by email. Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18 and over.

calls.title: DECAY, CORROSION, RUST
calls.org: New York Center for Photographic Arts
calls.description: Themed juried call for photography of decay, corrosion, and rust — abandoned buildings, rusted vehicles, peeling paint, junkyards — in any photographic medium. Cash prizes total $4,000 across ten awards: $1,100 Grand Prize, three First Prizes of $400, three Second Prizes of $325, three Third Prizes of $250, plus 20 Juror Selections and 20 Honorable Mentions. Juried by Darren Ching, co-owner of Klompching Gallery, New York. Winners featured in the NYC4PA online gallery and catalog with certificates; the winning image appears on the NYC4PA homepage. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers; 2-D work only.
calls.summary: Decay, corrosion, and rust in any photographic medium. $4,000 cash prizes, online gallery, catalogue. New York.
prose: The New York Center for Photographic Arts (NYC4PA) runs themed juried exhibitions on a recurring schedule. DECAY, CORROSION, RUST invites photographers to capture deterioration and oxidation across subjects — abandoned buildings, rusted vehicles, peeling paint, junkyards — in any photographic medium, black and white, color, or abstract.

Cash prizes total $4,000 across ten awards: a Grand Prize of $1,100, three First Prizes of $400, three Second Prizes of $325, and three Third Prizes of $250. Beyond the cash awards, 20 Juror Selections and 20 Honorable Mentions are recognized — featured in the online gallery and catalog with certificates. The winning image is also featured on the NYC4PA homepage.
The 2026 cycle is juried by Darren Ching, co-owner of the Klompching Gallery in New York. All 2-D photographic work is accepted.

Entry fee is $40 for the first three images, with $10 each additional and unlimited submissions allowed. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Submissions go through SmarterEntry; the 2026 deadline is August 16 at midnight Pacific Time.

calls.title: 2026 Portrait Award
calls.description: The Independent Photographer's monthly themed competition cycle, this round dedicated to portrait photography. Total prize pool $2,700: 1st prize $1,000, 2nd $600, 3rd $400, plus seven $100 finalist prizes. Winners exhibited in London and featured to the platform's 970k+ Instagram following. All entrants receive a free online portfolio. Judge: Luisa Dörr, the Brazilian photographer known for her portrait work. Submissions are tiered: $15 for 1 image, $30 for 3, $45 for 6. AI-generated work not accepted; photography-based submissions only. JPEG or PNG, minimum 1200px longest side, maximum 10MB.
calls.summary: Portrait photography competition. $2,700 prize pool, London exhibition and feature to 970k+ followers. Judge: Luisa Dörr.
prose: The Independent Photographer (TIP) is a London-based online photography platform that runs themed monthly competitions and publishes editorial work, interviews, and book reviews. The 2026 Portrait Award is the platform's portrait-themed cycle, open to portraiture across any approach.

Total prize pool is $2,700: first place receives $1,000, second $600, third $400, and seven runners-up receive $100 each. Winners are exhibited in London and featured across The Independent Photographer's Instagram (970k+ followers). All entrants receive a free online portfolio on the platform.

Selection is by Luisa Dörr, the Brazilian photographer known for her portrait series, including her TIME magazine cover work. TIP's broader jury roster has historically included names like Steve McCurry, Ed Kashi, and Maggie Steber — useful context for emerging entrants weighing this competition.

Eligibility is open globally. Submissions are tiered: $15 for one image, $30 for three, $45 for six. JPEG or PNG, minimum 1200 pixels on one side, maximum 10MB per file. AI-generated work is not accepted — photography-based submissions only. The deadline is June 30, 2026.

calls.title: The Sweep of Time: Beyond the Horizon
calls.description: A call open to all traditional and non-traditional photographic and light-based media, including mixed media with a dominant lens-based component, presented as a participating venue project of the 2026 FotoFocus Biennial, The Long View. Invites work engaging time as subject, symbol, or environment; the horizon as literal landscape or conceptual threshold; and distance, duration, memory, or continuity. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 honorarium; one work each exhibition period receives a $1,000 Grand Jury Award. Artists receive 70% on sales. Submit up to 3 entries for $45, $5 per additional. Exhibition at Manifest Gallery in Cincinnati, September 25 – October 23, 2026, launching the gallery's 23rd season.
calls.summary: Lens-based work on time, memory, and the horizon — a 2026 FotoFocus Biennial venue project. Cincinnati gallery exhibition.
prose: Manifest Gallery is a Cincinnati-based nonprofit creative research gallery. "The Sweep of Time: Beyond the Horizon" launches the gallery's 23rd season and is presented as a participating venue project of the 2026 FotoFocus Biennial, The Long View.

The call is open to all traditional and non-traditional photographic and light-based media, including mixed-media work with a dominant lens-based component. Taking a phrase from Marcus Aurelius as its premise, it invites work that holds the immediate and the enduring in the same frame — engaging time as subject, symbol, or environment; the horizon as literal landscape or conceptual threshold; and distance, duration, memory, or continuity.

Selected work is shown at Manifest Gallery in Cincinnati, September 25 – October 23, 2026. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 honorarium — payment for selection, not just inclusion — and one work during each exhibition period receives a $1,000 Grand Jury Award. Artists receive 70% on sales.

Selection is by an anonymous multi-member jury of professional and academic advisors, whose recommendations pass to the exhibit curator for final selection. There are no restrictions on the date a work was made.

Submission is through the gallery's website with up to 3 entries for $45, $5 per additional entry, and no limit on number of entries. Eligibility is open internationally. The deadline was extended to July 19, 2026; notifications by August 17.

calls.title: Open 2026
calls.description: Open-themed international photography exhibition — any genre, any subject. Selected work is shown in a month-long gallery exhibition in Glasgow (7–31 October 2026), with work also appearing in an online gallery and exhibition catalogue. All participants are put forward for Photographer of the Month consideration. Prints are produced on photographic paper and framed in gallery frames; photographers retain all copyright. Open to emerging and established photographers, professional and amateur, Scottish and international. Submit up to 8 JPEGs (300ppi minimum, 3000 pixels on shortest side) via free file-transfer to the gallery email.
calls.summary: Open-themed photography exhibition — any genre. Glasgow gallery exhibition Oct 2026, plus online gallery and catalogue.
prose: Open 2026 is one of Glasgow Gallery of Photography's themed open calls — the gallery runs a roughly monthly schedule of themed group exhibitions across the year. As the name suggests, this call has no fixed subject: it is open to any genre or theme a photographer wants to explore, from documentary and street to portraiture, landscape, still life, and conceptual work.

The exhibition runs October 7 through 31, 2026 in the gallery's Glasgow space. The submission model is free to apply, pay-only-if-selected — a £48 participation fee covers all printing, installation, and de-installation. Photographers retain all copyright.

Selected work also appears in the gallery's online gallery and is included in the exhibition catalogue, and all participants are put forward for the gallery's Photographer of the Month consideration. Eligibility is open globally — emerging and established, professional and amateur.

Each photographer submits up to 8 JPEGs at minimum 300ppi and 3,000 pixels on the shortest side, named Firstname-Surname_#, sent via Smash, SwissTransfer, WeTransfer, or Dropbox to submissions@glasgowgalleryofphotography.com. The deadline is June 19, 2026, with acceptance notifications on June 24.

The exhibition runs October 7 through 31, 2026 in the gallery's Glasgow space. The submission model is free to apply, pay-only-if-selected — a £48 participation fee covers all printing, installation, and de-installation. Photographers retain all copyright.

calls.title: Guest Room: Sunyoung Kim & Shinwook Kim
calls.description: Open call curated by Sunyoung Kim (Senior Curator, Hanmi Museum) and artist Shinwook Kim, on the theme "Hyperobjects: Archipelagic Memories" — exploring how photographs circulate across digital and material networks, fragmenting and reshaping personal and collective histories. Selected work is featured on Der Greif's platform, and selected artists receive a face-to-face feedback session with the curators. One artist receives a €250 Guest Room scholarship. Open globally; works previously selected in past Der Greif opportunities are not eligible.
calls.summary: Theme: "Hyperobjects: Archipelagic Memories" — how photographs circulate across digital and material networks.
jury: Sunyoung Kim, Senior Curator, Hanmi Museum
prose: Guest Room is Der Greif's recurring curator-led open call format. Each edition is shaped by an external curator or curatorial duo who set the theme and selection criteria. This Guest Room is curated jointly by Sunyoung Kim, Senior Curator at the Hanmi Museum, and the artist Shinwook Kim.

The theme is "Hyperobjects: Archipelagic Memories." The brief considers how photographs circulate across digital and material networks — fragmenting, dispersing, and reshaping personal and collective histories — and invites work that reflects on memory as something scattered and reassembled rather than fixed.

Selected work is published on Der Greif's platform. Selected artists also receive a face-to-face feedback session with the curators, and one artist receives a €250 Guest Room scholarship. Eligibility is open globally; works previously selected in past Der Greif opportunities are not eligible.
Submission is through Picter and the fee is voluntary (pay-what-you-can). The deadline was extended to July 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM CET, with the resulting online presentation following on dergreif.org.

calls.title: Preus Museum Open Call 2026 — Passion
calls.description: Annual themed open call from Preus Museum, the National Museum of Photography in Norway, presented with the Oslo Negativ photo festival. The 2026 theme is "Passion." Open to all artists worldwide, professional or amateur, individually or as a collective. Submit single images or a series of up to 15 photographs exploring the theme, with a project description explaining how the work relates to it. One winner receives NOK 20,000, acquisition into the Preus Museum collection, and an exhibition at Oslo Negativ 2026, with production and travel costs covered by the museum. Entry fee €10; free for students and Norwegian photographers via voucher (email opencall@preusmuseum.no).
calls.summary: Preus Museum's themed open call with Oslo Negativ. Theme: Passion. Winner gets NOK 20,000, exhibition, and collection acquisition.
prose: Preus Museum is the National Museum of Photography in Norway, based in Horten. Its annual open call is run in partnership with the Oslo Negativ photo festival, and each edition is built around a single theme — "Passion" for 2026.

The call is open to everyone: all genders, ages, and nationalities, amateur or professional, applying individually or as a collective. Entrants submit a single image or a series of up to 15 photographs that respond to the theme, accompanied by a project description explaining the connection.

One winner is selected for an exhibition at Oslo Negativ 2026, receives a cash prize of NOK 20,000, and has the work acquired into the Preus Museum collection; production and travel costs for the exhibition are covered by the museum. The entry fee is €10, waived for students and Norwegian photographers who request a voucher code at opencall@preusmuseum.no. Submission is handled through Picter, with a deadline of August 15, 2026.

calls.title: Der Greif × Fondament — I Spy With My Little Eye
calls.description: Open call from Der Greif in collaboration with Fondament on the theme "Ich seh' etwas, was du nicht siehst" (I Spy With My Little Eye), exploring social life in Germany through photographs that tell more than one story and leave room for different readings. The brief asks for images that hold the tension between perception and interpretation rather than offering a single narrative. Three cash prizes of €1,000 each; selected work is presented online from October 2026, with a publication and exhibition under consideration. Free to enter via Picter.
calls.summary: Der Greif × Fondament call: photographs of social life in Germany that tell more than one story. Theme: I Spy With My Little Eye.
prose: This open call is a collaboration between Der Greif, the Germany-based contemporary photography platform, and Fondament, on the theme "Ich seh' etwas, was du nicht siehst" — the German equivalent of the children's game "I Spy With My Little Eye."

The brief centres on social life in Germany, inviting photographs that resist a single reading. Artists are asked to submit work that tells more than one story and leaves room for different interpretations, holding the tension between what is seen and how it is understood.

Three equal cash prizes of €1,000 each are awarded by an interdisciplinary jury, introduced gradually on Instagram, judging on perspective shift, societal relevance, visual language, and narrative depth. Selected works are presented online from October 2026 on both organizations' platforms, with a publication and exhibition under consideration. Submission is free and handled through Picter; the deadline is September 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM CET. Full details are shared by Der Greif (info@dergreif.org) and Fondament (kontakt@fondament.de).

calls.title: Pine Meadow Ranch 2027 Artist Residency
calls.org: Pine Meadow Ranch Center for Arts & Agriculture
calls.description: Two- or four-week residency at Pine Meadow Ranch in Sisters, Oregon, run by the Roundhouse Foundation on a working ranch in the high desert of central Oregon. The 2027 program theme is "Process and Material." Open to many disciplines — photography (digital) is explicitly eligible alongside painting, ceramics, printmaking, fiber, sculpture, mixed and digital media, writing, music, performance, and creative research. A cohort of two to four residents shares a historic home, each with a private bedroom and a private studio adapted to their medium; residencies run March through mid-November. Provides a $200/week stipend plus up to $300 travel reimbursement for residents living more than 1,000 miles away. No application or residency fees. Applications are evaluated by panels of external reviewers; finalist interviews in mid-August, decisions announced September 2026.
calls.summary: Funded 2–4 week multidisciplinary residency on a high-desert Oregon ranch. Photography eligible. $200/week stipend, no fee.
prose: Pine Meadow Ranch Center for Arts & Agriculture (PMRCAA) is a residency program of the Roundhouse Foundation, set on a working ranch in Sisters, Oregon, in the high desert of central Oregon about 20 miles from Bend. The program brings together artists, makers, and researchers around the intersection of art, agriculture, and the land.

Residencies run two or four weeks between March and mid-November. A cohort of two to four residents shares a large historic home, each with a private bedroom and a private studio adapted to one of nine medium-specific spaces. Residents receive a $200 per week stipend to offset living and travel costs, with up to $300 in additional travel reimbursement for those living more than 1,000 miles away. There are no application or residency fees.

The 2027 cycle is themed "Process and Material" and welcomes a wide range of disciplines, with photography (digital) explicitly listed as eligible. Applications are submitted through SlideRoom and evaluated by panels of external reviewers established in fields associated with PMRCAA's mission. The deadline is July 6, 2026 at midnight PST; finalist interviews take place in mid-August and residency decisions are announced in September 2026.

calls.title: Put a Pin(hole) In It
calls.description: Group show of pinhole photography at Blue Moon Camera & Machine in Portland, Oregon, open to long-time pinhole enthusiasts and recent converts alike. Each photographer may submit up to 5 images (series welcome; the jury may select single images from a series). 25 works are curated from all submissions. Selected images must be delivered matted — not framed — in 16×20 mats (horizontal or vertical), and can be any size within the mat. Submitted files should be at least 1000px and no more than 3000px on the long edge, and include the photographer's name, contact info, and which pinhole camera was used. The show opens August 1, 2026.
calls.summary: Free pinhole photography group show at Blue Moon Camera & Machine, Portland OR. Up to 5 images; opens August 1, 2026.

calls.title: Stove Works Artist Residency 2027
calls.description: One- to three-month residency in Chattanooga, Tennessee, open to artists across all disciplines including photography, as well as non-object-based practitioners such as writers, curators and academics. Eight residents are hosted between February and November 2027. Once accepted, the residency is free to attend: residents receive a private studio/bedroom with bathroom, shared kitchen, living space and laundry, and 24-hour access to on-site metal, wood and print shops plus a library. Programming includes visiting critics and open studios. Residents cover their own travel, materials and food. A $100 refundable security deposit and one inscribed book donation to the library are required on acceptance. International applicants welcome. The application fee is tiered: $10 (May 15–31), $20 (June 1–7), $30 (June 8–15).
calls.summary: Free 1–3 month residency in Chattanooga, TN for artists across all media incl. photography; 24-hr access to metal, wood & print shops.
prose: Stove Works is an artist residency and exhibition space in Chattanooga, Tennessee. Each year it invites eight artists to live and work on site between February and November, for stays of one to three months at a time. The program is open to all disciplines, explicitly including photography, and also accommodates non-object-based practices such as writing, curating and academic research.

Once accepted, the residency itself is free to attend. Residents receive a private studio/bedroom with a bathroom, shared kitchen, living space and laundry, and around-the-clock access to fully equipped metal, wood and print shops as well as a library. Programming over the residency period includes visiting critics and open studios. Residents are responsible for their own travel, materials and food, and on acceptance provide a $100 refundable security deposit and one inscribed book for the library.
Applications for 2027 residencies are open from 15 May to 15 June 2026, with a tiered fee of $10 (15–31 May), $20 (1–7 June) or $30 (8–15 June). International applicants are welcome.

calls.title: Form Photo Award / SCOPE Miami 2026
calls.description: Contemporary photography prize with an open theme, accepting single images and series. Top 4 winners exhibit at the SCOPE Art Fair in Miami in December 2026 during Miami Art Week; shortlisted artists are published in Form Magazine.
calls.summary: Contemporary photo prize; top 4 winners exhibit at SCOPE Art Fair Miami during Art Week, Dec 2026, plus a Form Magazine feature.
jury: Hayley Smith, Director, SCOPE Art Show
Blayne Planit, Artist, Curator & Creative Strategist
prose: Form is a Basel-based photography platform founded by Dimitri Bogachuk, spanning a gallery, publishing house and magazine. Alongside its photo basel edition each spring, Form runs a second annual award tied to the SCOPE Art Fair in Miami.

The premise is again positioning: the top four winners exhibit at SCOPE Art Fair Miami in December 2026, during Miami Art Week, reaching the collectors, curators and gallerists who travel for the fair.
Shortlisted artists are featured in Form Magazine, extending visibility beyond the fair. The theme is open, and both single images and series are accepted.
Eligibility is global, open to photographers 18 and over. Submission is through Picter with 1–8 images and a €35 fee. The deadline is July 31, 2026.

calls.title: Metamorfosi Residency 2026
calls.description: Artist residency in Prague run by the Italian Cultural Institute (IIC Prague) in collaboration with MUNAF — National Museum of Photography. One Italian artist is invited to develop a visual arts project under the theme Metamorphosis — reflecting on change and transformation across artistic practice and cultural context, with research open in theme and medium. The residency takes place at the IIC Prague guest house between autumn 2026 and spring 2027, lasting three to four weeks, structured in a planning phase and a production phase, and concluding with a public presentation. The total grant is €5,000 net, covering the artist's fee, all travel to and from the residency plus research travel, meals and accommodation at the guest house for the full stay, and production costs for the work delivered. Open to Italian artists with no age restriction. Apply by email with the application form, ID, CV and portfolio, a presentation of one completed project, a motivation letter, and the data-processing consent form.
calls.summary: Prague residency for Italian artists from IIC Prague & MUNAF. €5,000 grant covering travel, subsistence, and production. 3–4 weeks.
prose: Metamorfosi is an artist residency open call launched by the Italian Cultural Institute (IIC) in Prague in collaboration with MUNAF — the National Museum of Photography, Italy's first public national museum dedicated entirely to photography and technological imagery (known as MUFOCO until October 2025).

The residency invites one Italian artist to develop a visual arts project around the theme of Metamorphosis — a reflection on change and transformation, in both artistic practice and the cultural contexts artists work within. The scope is deliberately open in theme and medium, though a connection with the promoting institutions and the host territory is encouraged.

The residency runs at the IIC Prague guest house during a window agreed between autumn 2026 and spring 2027, lasting between three and four weeks. It is structured in two parts: a planning phase of meetings, site visits, and focus-setting, followed by a production phase, closing with a public presentation of the research.

The total grant is €5,000 net and covers the artist's fee, all travel to and from the residency (and any research travel), meals and accommodation at the guest house for the full stay, production costs for the delivered artwork including shipping, and any other activities the artist takes part in during the residency.

The call is open to Italian artists with no age restriction. Applications are submitted by email and must include the application form, a valid ID or passport, a signed CV and portfolio, a detailed presentation of one completed project, a motivation letter (which may outline the proposed residency project), and the data-processing consent form. The deadline is June 30, 2026 at 12:00 PM.

calls.title: Folk House Darkroom Residency 2026
calls.description: Darkroom residency at Bristol Folk House Darkroom, a community darkroom in central Bristol working towards more sustainable photographic processes. The residency is aimed at photographers and artists using or wanting to explore experimental, sustainable, and alternative processes — past residents have done work such as making developers from oats. Dates and length are flexible and chosen by the resident based on the darkroom's term schedule. Residents receive a stipend, darkroom training, darkroom space and equipment, and discounts in the Folk House café and programme. Open internationally; apply by email.
calls.summary: Free Bristol darkroom residency for experimental, sustainable and alternative processes. Stipend, darkroom training, and full access included.
prose: Bristol Folk House Darkroom is a community darkroom in central Bristol (40a Park St), run as part of the Bristol Folk House and working towards more sustainable photographic processes.

The 2026 residency is aimed at photographers and artists using or wanting to explore experimental, sustainable, and alternative photographic processes — for example, making developers from plant material or other low-impact darkroom approaches. The dates and length of the residency are flexible and decided by the resident based on the darkroom's term schedule.
Selected residents receive a stipend, darkroom training, darkroom space and equipment, and discounts in the Folk House café and programme.
Applications are open until 22 June 2026. To apply, email darkroom@bristolfolkhouse.co.uk for more information and an application.

calls.title: Solo Exhibition August 2026
calls.description: Monthly featured photographer showcase. Winner receives a full month online solo exhibition (August 1–31, 2026), permanent gallery presence, exclusive interview, social media promotion, newsletter feature, international press coverage, and commission-free sales. Submit a cohesive project or portfolio of 6–14 images.
jury: Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, Photographer & Founder, All About Photo
calls.summary: Monthly featured photographer showcase. Full month online solo exhibition, interview, and press coverage.
prose: All About Photo runs a monthly Solo Exhibition program — each month features a different photographer with a dedicated month-long online presentation. The August 2026 cycle is the next available slot.

The selected photographer receives a full month of online solo exhibition (August 1–31, 2026) featured on All About Photo's homepage, competition gallery, and showroom pages. Beyond the month, the work is permanently archived on the platform with a dedicated portfolio page, accompanied by an exclusive artist interview and social media promotion across the platform's Instagram, Facebook, and other channels.
Past winners have been featured in major international press outlets. Sales are commission-free — the artist retains 100% of the sale price.

Submission is open to photographers worldwide at any career level. Submissions are 6 to 14 cohesive images forming a project or portfolio. JPEG format, 72 dpi, no watermarks, flattened layers, file size under 2 MB, longest dimension max 1,200 pixels.
Selection is by Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, Founder & Editor of All About Photo. Entry fee is $45. The 2026 deadline is July 21; the selected photographer's solo exhibition opens August 1.

calls.title: BINNAR Festival 2026
calls.description: Multidisciplinary festival in Vila Nova de Famalicão, Portugal, running since 2016 with municipal support. Open call for the November 2026 edition welcomes photography and video for a collective exhibition with free theme. BINNAR handles all production: selected photos are printed and framed at no cost to the artist; videos must not exceed 2 minutes. Submissions are open internationally — artists send name, nationality, age, an artist statement and biography, plus a direct link to view the work, by email to info.binnar@gmail.com with subject line 'open call'.
calls.summary: Free open call for BINNAR Festival in Famalicão, Portugal. Free theme. Photos printed and framed by the festival; videos under 2 min.
prose: BINNAR is a multidisciplinary artistic festival and year-round platform based in Vila Nova de Famalicão, northern Portugal, founded in 2016 and run with municipal support under artistic director Filipe Miranda. The festival programs music, performance, photography, theatre, video, sculpture, and installation, with free admission to all events.

The 2026 open call is for a collective exhibition of photography and video taking place in November 2026. The brief is open theme — any subject or approach is accepted. Videos must not exceed two minutes; the photography component is shown as printed and framed work.

What distinguishes the call: there is no entry fee, and BINNAR covers the full production cost of selected works. Selected photographs are printed and framed by the festival; artists are not asked to provide prints or pay for production.

Submission is by email to info.binnar@gmail.com with subject line 'open call', including the artist's name, nationality, age (gender optional), a direct link to view the photos or video, an artist statement, and a biography. Selected artists are contacted directly by the organizers. The deadline is June 30, 2026.

calls.title: RED
calls.description: Themed exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe celebrating bold uses of red in photography — images where red commands the frame. Documentary, fine art, abstract, and experimental approaches all welcome. Juried by Dusk founder Holly Hart. Selected photographers receive complimentary professional printing and framing in 24×24 inch black museum-quality frames with matting; the artist supplies only the high-resolution JPEG (500KB–5MB, 4500px on the longest side). The gallery adjusts file dimensions for presentation without cropping. Exhibition runs August 7–28, 2026 in Santa Fe. Sales split 50/50; selected images retained in the gallery's flat files for six months post-exhibition. Open worldwide.
jury: Holly Hart, Fine Art Photographer & Founder, Dusk Gallery
calls.summary: Themed show on bold uses of red at Santa Fe's Dusk Gallery. Pro printing and 24×24 museum framing included. Juried by Holly Hart.
prose: Dusk Gallery is a Santa Fe, New Mexico photography gallery founded by fine art photographer Holly Hart, who also juries the gallery's calls. RED is a themed cycle built around a single color used as compositional force: images where red commands the frame rather than appearing as background or detail.

The brief is open across approach — documentary, fine art, abstract, and experimental work are all welcome. The gallery is interested in the use of red as a structural element of the photograph, not in subject matter alone.

What distinguishes Dusk's calls is the production model: the gallery covers professional printing and framing in 24×24 inch black museum-quality frames with matting at no cost to the artist. Photographers supply only a high-resolution JPEG (500KB–5MB, 4500px on the longest side); the gallery adjusts presentation dimensions without cropping the composition.

The exhibition runs August 7–28, 2026 at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe. Sales split 50/50 between gallery and artist, with selected images retained in the gallery's flat files for six months post-exhibition. The entry fee is $40 for 5 images or $45 for up to 10. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. The deadline is June 25, 2026.

calls.title: A Celebration of Contemporary Photography
calls.description: International juried exhibition at PhotoPlace Gallery in Middlebury, Vermont, programmed around World Photography Day (August 19). The call welcomes any subject, style, or process — landscape, portraiture, documentary, experimental, alternative process. Up to 35 images selected for the physical gallery exhibition, plus 40 additional images for the online exhibition; all 75 selected works appear in a printed catalog and remain permanently on the gallery's website. Awards include a Juror's Award ($300), Director's Award ($200), and three Honorable Mentions ($50 each). Juried by Paula Tognarelli (retired Executive Director, Griffin Museum of Photography) and Zach Hoffman (Gallery Owner/Director). Fully AI-generated work is not eligible. Exhibition runs August 7–29, 2026; prints due July 24.
jury: Paula Tognarelli, retired Executive Director, Griffin Museum of Photography
calls.summary: PhotoPlace's open-theme show around World Photography Day. 75 works selected for gallery, online and catalog. Paula Tognarelli juries.
prose: A Celebration of Contemporary Photography is PhotoPlace Gallery's annual broad-brief juried exhibition, programmed around World Photography Day (August 19). PhotoPlace Gallery is a photography gallery in Middlebury, Vermont, that runs themed calls on a rolling schedule alongside its own programming.

The brief is intentionally inclusive — any subject, any style, any photographic process. The gallery explicitly welcomes traditional landscape and portraiture alongside experimental and alternative-process work, framing the show as a panorama of contemporary photographic practice rather than a thematic exhibition.

Selection is by two jurors: Paula Tognarelli, retired Executive Director of the Griffin Museum of Photography, and Zach Hoffman, owner and director of PhotoPlace Gallery. They select up to 35 images for the physical exhibition in Middlebury and 40 additional images for an online companion exhibition. All 75 selected works are reproduced in a printed catalog and remain permanently accessible on the gallery's website.

Awards include a $300 Juror's Award, a $200 Director's Award, and three $50 Honorable Mentions. Fully AI-generated images are not eligible; AI-assisted editing tools applied to camera-originated work are acceptable. The fee is $39 for 5 images, $6 each additional. The deadline is June 8, 2026; the physical exhibition runs August 7–29, 2026, with prints due July 24.

calls.title: A Show of Hands
calls.description: Online exhibition organized by Blue Sky, Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts, as part of its 50th anniversary programming. The brief invites photographers to interpret the hand as a subject — symbols of connection, expression and care; intimate gestures or collective movements. Curated by a Blue Sky committee. The exhibition launches July 2, 2026 on the gallery's website. Submission via Google Form: up to three images per artist, max 1500 pixels on the long edge, filename format lastname_firstname_title.jpg. Membership not required. Accepted works display online only and are not available for sale. Free to enter.
calls.summary: Free online exhibition on hands — connection, expression, care — from Portland's Blue Sky, Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts.
prose: Blue Sky, the Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts, is a long-running Portland nonprofit photography gallery founded in 1975. A Show of Hands is one of its 50th anniversary online exhibitions.

The brief frames hands as both intimate and collective — symbols of connection, expression, and care, from quiet gestures to mass movements. Photographers are invited to bring their own approach: documentary, conceptual, staged or otherwise.

Selection is made by a Blue Sky committee. The chosen works are presented in an online exhibition launching July 2, 2026 on the gallery's website. Works are not offered for sale; this is a visibility-and-platform call rather than a commercial one.

Submission is free and open to all — Blue Sky membership is not required. Photographers send up to three images via Google Form, max 1500px on the long edge, named lastname_firstname_title.jpg. Deadline 12 June 2026, 4:59 PM Pacific.

calls.title: Encontros da Imagem Portfolio Reviews 2026
calls.description: Portfolio Review program of the 36th edition of Encontros da Imagem, one of Europe's longest-running photography festivals, held in Braga, Portugal. Two-stage process: an initial pre-selection via the Picter platform, then 32 photographers travel to Braga for in-person reviews on October 8–9, 2026. Each selected photographer gives a 10-minute public presentation followed by eight 10-minute one-on-one review appointments with the jury. The Portfolio Review Prize awards €3,000 cash, a solo exhibition at the 2027 edition of the festival, and publication in KATALOG magazine. Three Honorable Mentions are featured in a video projection during the 2026 festival. Submissions: up to 3 projects per applicant, 15–20 images per project plus synopsis. Fee structure: €30 application fee for the initial pre-selection; €80 second-stage fee for selected photographers attending the in-person review. Open globally. Festival theme: Territory and Identity.
jury: Awa Konaté, Curator & Founder, Culture Art Society
Emese Mucsi, Curator, Robert Capa Contemporary Photography Center
Gilles Cargueray, Editorial Director & Cultural Project Manager
Inês Grosso, Chief Curator, Serralves Foundation Museum of Contemporary Art
calls.summary: Two-stage portfolio review at Braga's Encontros da Imagem festival. €3,000 + solo 2027 show + KATALOG publication for the winner.
prose: Encontros da Imagem is one of Europe's longest-running photography festivals — a non-profit cultural association founded in 1987 that has run an International Photography and Visual Arts Festival in Braga, Portugal, every year since. The 2026 edition is the 36th, with the festival theme Territory and Identity.

The Portfolio Reviews program runs in parallel to the festival's main prize tracks and is structured in two stages. Stage one is an open online pre-selection through the Picter platform, requiring up to three projects per applicant with 15–20 images each. Stage two brings 32 selected photographers to Braga in person on October 8–9, 2026. Each gives a 10-minute public presentation followed by eight 10-minute one-on-one review appointments with the jury.

The top award — the Portfolio Review Prize — carries a €3,000 cash prize, a solo exhibition at the 2027 edition of the festival, and publication in KATALOG, the festival's magazine. Three Honorable Mentions are featured in a video projection during the 2026 festival.

Fees are tiered to the two stages: a €30 application fee for the open pre-selection, and an additional €80 second-stage fee paid only by selected photographers attending the in-person Braga review. Eligibility is open globally to photographers aged 18 or older. Deadline for the open stage: extended to 13 June 2026.

calls.title: ENDLESS SUMMER Photography Exhibit
calls.description: Themed exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson exploring summer's endless quality — golden hour on repeat, the weight of humid air, days that never seem to darken. Open to all photographic styles and approaches; not restricted to black-and-white. Twenty-six images are juried for the group exhibition by Decode founder Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson Ultra Premium Luster paper and museum-quality 22×22 inch framing with precut mats; the artist supplies only the high-resolution JPEG. Exhibition runs September 5–26, 2026. Sales split 50/50 between gallery and artist; selected prints retained in the gallery's flat files for six months post-exhibition for further promotion. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers.
jury: Holly Hart, Conceptual Fine Art Photographer & Decode Gallery Founder
calls.summary: Summer-themed photography exhibit in Tucson. 26 images juried by Holly Hart. Pro printing and 22×22 museum framing included.
prose: ENDLESS SUMMER is Decode Gallery's late-summer themed exhibition, framed around the sensory persistence of the season — golden hour repeating, humid air thick with weight, days that refuse to darken. The brief is open to interpretation across all photographic styles and approaches; the gallery clarifies that black-and-white is welcome but not a requirement.

Twenty-six images are juried by Decode founder Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer based in Tucson. The selected works are shown in a three-week physical exhibition at the gallery, running September 5–26, 2026, with high-resolution JPEGs due two days after acceptance notification.

What distinguishes Decode's open calls from typical fee-based group shows: the gallery covers professional printing on Epson Ultra Premium Luster paper and museum-quality 22×22 inch white framing with precut mats. The artist provides only the file. Sales split 50/50 between gallery and photographer, and selected prints remain in the gallery's flat files for six months after the show for continued promotion.

The entry fee is $40 per entry, which includes up to 5 images. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers; payment via PayPal or Square. The 2026 deadline is July 24; acceptance notifications go out within two weeks.

calls.title: 100 Book Award 2026
calls.description: Open call from Kult Books, an independent publishing project in Stockholm run by Janne Riikonen. One or two selected projects are produced as a published photobook in a limited edition of 100 copies, fully designed by the publisher, with an ISBN, catalogued and distributed via book fairs, online retailers, and bookshops. Selected artists receive 3 free copies and the option to purchase up to 20 additional copies at a 60% discount. Open to artists working primarily with photography in any style; supplementary media like drawing or writing may be incorporated as long as photography remains dominant. AI-generated work is not accepted. Submit 80–300 low-resolution JPGs via download link or a dummy/PDF with a work description by email to hello@kultbooks.com with 'open call' in the subject line. Results announced June 26, 2026; publication Spring 2027.
calls.summary: Free photobook open call from indie publisher Kult Books (Stockholm). Selected projects published in editions of 100 copies, fully designed.
prose: Kult Books is an independent publishing project based in Stockholm, founded and run by Finnish-Swedish visual artist, publisher, and book designer Janne Riikonen. The catalogue focuses on conceptual and documentary photography, with monographs and artists' books produced in close collaboration with each artist — the physical form of each book designed to carry the concept of the work. Lenscratch featured Kult Books in its Publishers Spotlight in 2023; the press has since opened a bookshop at its Stockholm studio and aims to publish six to eight titles a year.

The 100 Book Award is the press's recurring open call for new projects to enter the catalogue. One or two selected works are published as a limited edition of 100 copies, with full design by Janne Riikonen, an ISBN, and catalogue inclusion. Selected books are distributed at international book fairs, in bookshops, and through online retailers — meaning the prize is full publication rather than a contest-style award. There are no submission, design, or printing costs for the artist.

The selected artist(s) receive three complimentary copies of the printed book plus the option to purchase up to twenty additional copies at a 60% discount for personal sale. In exchange, artists are expected to attend design meetings, deliver print-ready retouched photographs, and provide written work descriptions and any relevant accompanying texts.

The call is open worldwide to artists working primarily with photography. All photographic styles are welcome, and complementary media such as drawing and writing may be incorporated as long as photography remains the dominant medium. AI-generated work is explicitly not accepted.

Submissions are sent by email to hello@kultbooks.com with the subject line 'open call', containing either a download link to 80–300 low-resolution JPGs or a dummy/PDF, alongside a written work description and any supporting texts. Deadline: June 14, 2026. Results announced June 26, 2026. Publication scheduled for Spring 2027.

calls.title: TOKAS International Creator Residency Program 2027
calls.description: Three-month residency in Tokyo run by Tokyo Arts and Space (TOKAS), the contemporary art programming arm of the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo (MOT). Open to international visual artists (photographers welcome), designers, and architects with at least five years of professional experience. Six positions across three periods: May–July 2027, September–November 2027, and January–March 2028. Each resident receives round-trip airfare, a single-room studio apartment at TOKAS Residency in Koto-ku, shared workspace, a per diem of 4,200 JPY/day (approximately €25/$28), and a 300,000 JPY (≈€1,800/$2,000) creative work fee. Two letters of recommendation required. Applicants must not be students at the time of residency; previous TOKAS participants may reapply only for a program they have not completed. Application via online form plus uploaded PDF application form and portfolio.
calls.summary: Three-month Tokyo residency. Airfare, accommodation, 4,200 JPY/day per diem, 300,000 JPY creative fee. Free to apply.
prose: Tokyo Arts and Space (TOKAS) is the contemporary-art programming arm of the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo (MOT), based in Koto-ku, Tokyo. Its residency programs run alongside the museum's exhibition and curatorial activity, and the International Creator Residency Program is its flagship invitation to non-Japanese practitioners working in visual art (including photography), film, design, and architecture.

The 2027 cycle offers six three-month residencies across three periods: May–July 2027, September–November 2027, and January–March 2028. Each resident is housed in a single-room studio apartment at TOKAS Residency, with access to shared studio and workspace. The program covers round-trip economy airfare, a daily per diem of 4,200 JPY (approximately €25), and a creative work fee of 300,000 JPY (approximately €1,800) intended to support research and production during the stay.

Eligibility is open to international artists with at least five years of professional practice. Applicants cannot be students at the time of the residency. Previous TOKAS participants are allowed to reapply, but only for a program they have not yet completed. Applications close June 16, 2026 at 18:00 Japan Standard Time. Inquiries through the dedicated contact form are accepted until June 7, 2026.

Submission is via an online form alongside an uploaded PDF Application Form, two letters of recommendation from referees versed in art and culture, and a portfolio. Selection is by the TOKAS jury, with results communicated by email; the residency itself begins from May 2027 for the first cohort.

calls.title: Magnetic 5 Residency Programme 2026
calls.description: Fifth cycle of Magnetic, the France-UK cross-Channel residency programme run by Fluxus Art Projects. Five tandem pairings link French regions with UK nations: Nouvelle-Aquitaine with Wysing Arts Centre (Cambridge), Hauts-de-France with Flax Art Studios (Belfast), Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur with Cove Park (Scotland), Brittany with Aberystwyth Arts Centre (Wales), and Île-de-France with Gasworks (London) — applications open in both directions. Each residency runs 2–3 months with a minimum monthly allowance of £2,100 / €2,500, accommodation, workspace access, and curatorial mentoring tailored to each host. Open to professional visual artists (photographers welcome) with prior exhibition history in recognized contemporary art venues, individuals only, who are French nationals or 5+ years France-resident, or British nationals or 5+ years UK-resident. PhD candidates eligible; other students not. The 2026 brief asks artists to engage with the social, environmental, geographical, historical, and artistic context of the host site. Submission via Google Forms with artistic proposal and motivational statement. Interviews 6–10 July; results 20 July 2026.
calls.summary: France–UK cross-Channel residency. 2-3 months, £2,100/€2,500 monthly. For visual artists resident in FR or UK only.
prose: Fluxus Art Projects is a UK-registered charity dedicated to supporting cultural exchange between France and the United Kingdom across the visual arts. Magnetic, now in its fifth iteration, is the foundation's flagship residency programme — a tandem structure pairing French regions with UK nations so that artists travel in both directions across the Channel as a single cohort.

The 2026 cycle offers residencies across five tandem pairings. From France, artists from Nouvelle-Aquitaine travel to Wysing Arts Centre near Cambridge; Hauts-de-France to Flax Art Studios in Belfast; Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur to Cove Park in Scotland; Brittany to Aberystwyth Arts Centre in Wales; and Île-de-France to Gasworks in London. The reverse pairings apply for UK-based artists travelling to French institutions in the same regions.

Each residency runs 2 to 3 months and provides a minimum monthly allowance of £2,100 (or €2,500), accommodation, workspace access, and curatorial mentoring. The 2026 brief frames the programme around societal and environmental issues, asking artists to engage with the geographical, historical, social, and artistic context of the host site. Eligibility is restricted to professional visual artists with exhibition history in recognized contemporary art venues, individuals only (no collectives or duos), French nationals or those resident in France for at least five years, and British nationals or those resident in the UK for at least five years. Students are not eligible, with PhD candidates as the exception.

Applications close at midnight on Tuesday 2 June 2026 via Google Forms, requiring an artistic proposal articulating the practice's relevance to the residency context and a motivational statement on why an international residency matters at this point in the applicant's career. Interviews are held 6–10 July; results are announced 20 July 2026.

calls.title: Southern Survey Biennial III
calls.description: Third edition of Project Row Houses' biennial survey of contemporary visual artists living and working in the 13-state Southern U.S. region (Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia). Selected artists are commissioned to create site-responsive installations in one of PRH's seven 550-square-foot shotgun-house galleries on Holman Street in Houston's Third Ward. Each selected artist receives a $5,000 stipend toward materials, artist fees, and creative labor; one participating artist additionally receives a $25,000 prize chosen by a guest juror. PRH covers travel and lodging during the installation week and the opening reception/community market in early October 2026. Application via SlideRoom: introductory statement, portfolio of 1–5 artworks, optional installation budget, and a written response to the question 'How would you characterize your identity as a Southerner?'. Exhibition on view October 2026 through February 2027. Past participating artists have included photographers and photo-based installation artists; previous $25,000 winner was Nico Brierre Aziz, selected by Kimberli Gant (Curator of Modern & Contemporary Art, Brooklyn Museum).
calls.summary: Biennial survey for visual artists in 13 Southern U.S. states. Installation in shotgun-house gallery, $5K stipend + $25K prize.
prose: Project Row Houses is a community-based arts and culture nonprofit founded in 1993 in Houston's Third Ward, occupying a row of restored shotgun houses on Holman Street. Its programming sits at the intersection of art, social practice, and Black cultural heritage in the U.S. South. The Southern Survey Biennial is PRH's recurring effort to spotlight contemporary visual artists rooted in the region and to commission new installation work that responds to the unique 550-square-foot shotgun-house gallery footprint.

The third edition is open to contemporary visual artists living and working in the thirteen Southern states colloquially known as 'The South': Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, and Virginia. Photographers and photo-based installation artists are welcome — Round 57, the previous Southern Survey Biennial, included photographers Violette Bule and Jamire Williams alongside multidisciplinary winner Nico Brierre Aziz, who received the $25,000 juror's prize selected by Kimberli Gant, Curator of Modern and Contemporary Art at the Brooklyn Museum.

Each selected artist receives a $5,000 stipend earmarked for materials, artist fees, and creative labor, plus travel and lodging during the installation week and the October opening weekend. One participating artist will additionally receive a $25,000 prize chosen by a guest juror (yet to be named). The exhibition runs from October 2026 through February 2027 and includes an opening reception and community market in early October.

Applications are submitted through SlideRoom. The application asks for an introductory statement, a portfolio of one to five artworks, an optional budget for an installation in one of the seven shotgun-house galleries, and a written response to the question: 'Project Row Houses uplifts artists who demonstrate commitment and deference to the Southern region of the United States. How would you characterize your identity as a Southerner?' Deadline: May 31, 2026. Contact: info@projectrowhouses.org.

calls.title: The Art of Experimentation — Symposium on Alternative Photography
calls.description: Free open call for speakers and presenters for The Art of Experimentation, a one-day symposium on alternative photography dedicated to women, non-binary, and trans artists, researchers, and practitioners. Held in person at Bristol Folk House Darkroom on August 1, 2026 (10am–3pm). Co-organized by Women Alternative Photography Group and Folk House Darkroom. Three submission categories: 10–15 minute artist talk or research paper, 10–15 minute performance, or 10–15 minute film screening. Speakers receive an equal split of all ticket-sale proceeds; programme also includes a photo walk around Bristol and an informal show-and-tell where presenters can share physical work. Particularly welcomes students and emerging to mid-career applicants; commitment to inclusivity across race, ability, and experience. International applicants welcome but no travel funding or visa sponsorship provided. Submit a title, abstract (max 250 words), artist bio (max 100 words), category selection, and up to three images/films/performance documentation via online form.
calls.summary: Symposium speaker call for women/nonbinary/trans alt-process photographers. Bristol, Aug 1, 2026. Free apply, revenue share.
prose: The Art of Experimentation is a one-day symposium on alternative photography co-organized by Women Alternative Photography Group and Bristol Folk House Darkroom. The 2026 edition runs in person on Saturday, August 1, 2026, 10am–3pm, at the Folk House Darkroom in central Bristol — a space dedicated to alternative and sustainable photographic processes.

The symposium is dedicated to women, non-binary, and trans artists, researchers, curators, and practitioners working with experimental and alternative photographic processes. The brief asks contributors to articulate how they use experimentation within different contexts — in practice, theory, or across different alternative photographic disciplines — and to help build community around the field. The organizers explicitly welcome students and emerging to mid-career practitioners, and applicants of all races, abilities, and experiences.

Three submission categories are open: a 10–15 minute presentation (artist talk or research paper), a 10–15 minute performance, or a 10–15 minute film screening. The programme also includes two social events designed to build networks: a photo walk around Bristol where participants can bring any camera, and an informal show-and-tell where presenters can share physical work with each other.

Application is free and made through an online form on the Women Alternative Photography Group site. Required materials: a title, a 250-word abstract, a 100-word artist bio, category selection, and up to three images, films, or performance documentation. Compensation is via revenue share — all proceeds from ticket sales are pooled and split equally among selected speakers. International applicants may apply but the organizers do not cover travel or provide visa sponsorship. Deadline: June 15, 2026. Contact: womenaltphotogroup@gmail.com.
jury: Elizabeth Ransom, Women Alternative Photography Group

calls.title: Eidolon Grant 2026
calls.description: Third edition of the Eidolon Grant from the Budapest-based Eidolon Centre for Everyday Photography, the only international platform dedicated to vernacular and everyday photography. €25,000 total prize pool distributed across two categories: (1) contemporary everyday photographic cultures (digital and social media imaging) and (2) everyday photographs of the past (19th-20th century vernacular archives). Number of winners determined by jury based on the applications received; payment in 3-4 installments. Open globally to artists, academics, researchers, enthusiasts, professionals, and collectors with no geographic restrictions; individual or group applications welcome. Application via Typeform with abstract (2,000 characters max), CV, project overview PDF (3 pages max), detailed project description PDF (10 pages max), and budget using the official Excel template. Submissions in English only. Call opens May 1, 2026; winners announced November 10, 2026.
calls.summary: €25,000 grant pool for research and projects on vernacular and everyday photography. Two categories: contemporary and historical.
jury: Axel Danielson & Maximilien Van Aertryck, Documentary filmmakers
Sam Mercer, Curator of Photography & Technology, The Photographers' Gallery
Róza Tekla Szilágyi, Director & Co-founder, Eidolon Centre
prose: The Eidolon Centre for Everyday Photography is a Budapest-based platform founded to focus exclusively on vernacular and everyday photography — the snapshot, the family album, the social media post, the institutional and amateur archive. The Centre positions these images as cultural artefacts that reveal social, political, and personal histories the canonical photographic tradition tends to overlook.

The Eidolon Grant is the Centre's flagship annual funding programme, now in its third edition. The 2026 cycle splits a €25,000 total pool across two parallel tracks: one focused on contemporary everyday photographic cultures (digital, mobile, and social media imaging) and one focused on everyday photographs of the past (19th- and 20th-century vernacular archives). Both individual researchers and collaborative teams can apply, with no geographic restrictions and no entry fee.

The 2026 jury combines academic, curatorial, and practitioner perspectives: Axel Danielson and Maximilien Van Aertryck (the Swedish documentary filmmakers behind the Films of the World project), photography curator and writer Catlin Langford, Sam Mercer (Curator of Photography & Technology at The Photographers' Gallery in London), the Italian photographer and filmmaker Alba Zari, and Róza Tekla Szilágyi, Director and Co-founder of the Eidolon Centre.

Applications are submitted in English through a dedicated Typeform — email submissions are not accepted. The form requires an abstract (max 2,000 characters), a project overview PDF (max 3 pages, 10 MB), a detailed project description PDF (max 10 pages, 10 MB), CV, and a completed budget using the official Excel template. The call opens May 1, 2026 and closes September 30, 2026 at 11:59 p.m.; winners are announced November 10, 2026 with payment in 3-4 installments tied to project scope and timeline.

calls.title: The Print Center 101st ANNUAL International Competition
calls.description: The Print Center's 101st edition of its long-running annual international competition for artists working with photography and/or printmaking. Open to local, national, and international artists; work must have been completed within the last three years. Up to five images or videos per submission. Selection produces 25 Semifinalists and 10 Finalists; three Finalists are given Solo Exhibitions at The Print Center (January-March 2027). Acquisition awards include the Philadelphia Museum of Art Collection Award and the Art Museum of West Virginia University Purchase Award via the Beth and Joe Hestick Acquisitions Fund. Additional cash prizes up to $1,000 and material awards from Awagami Paper. Jurors: Pepe Coronado (Director and Master Printer, Coronado printstudio, Austin) and Shana Lopes (Assistant Curator of Photography, SFMOMA). Notifications by September 11, 2026.
