jury: Pepe Coronado, Director and Master Printer, Coronado printstudio
Shana Lopes, Assistant Curator of Photography, SFMOMA
prose: The Print Center is a long-running Philadelphia nonprofit founded in 1915 that supports artists working with photography and printmaking. The Annual International Competition has run since 1923 and is one of the oldest competitions of its kind in the United States. The 101st edition continues the tradition of treating photography and printmaking as parallel critical practices rather than separate disciplines.

Eligibility is open to local, national, and international artists. Work submitted must have been completed within the last three years — pieces finished between June 2023 and June 2026. Each artist may submit one application of up to five images or videos.

Twenty-five Semifinalists and ten Finalists are selected. Three Finalists receive Solo Exhibitions at The Print Center between January and March 2027. The competition is notable for its acquisition awards: the Philadelphia Museum of Art Collection Award places winning work into PMA's permanent collection, and the Art Museum of West Virginia University Purchase Award acquires work through the Beth and Joe Hestick Acquisitions Fund. Additional cash prizes up to $1,000 and material awards from Awagami Paper are also awarded.

The 2026 jurors are Pepe Coronado, Director and Master Printer of Coronado printstudio in Austin, and Shana Lopes, Assistant Curator of Photography at the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art. Submissions go through SlideRoom; the entry fee is $45. The deadline is June 18, 2026 at 11:59pm ET; notifications by September 11, 2026.

calls.title: In Full View — Woman Made Gallery
calls.description: Open call from Woman Made Gallery (Chicago) for an exhibition exploring visibility, aging, identity, memory, and the legacy of a fully lived life. Open to women and nonbinary artists aged 65 and over, internationally. All media accepted, including photography. Juried by Jerri Zbiral. In-person exhibition at WMG, 1332 S. Halsted St., Chicago, October 10–November 7, 2026. Submission via EntryThingy: 1–3 artworks plus a $24.60 entry fee. Selected artists ship or hand-deliver work ready to exhibit.
calls.summary: Woman Made Gallery (Chicago) open call for women/nonbinary artists 65+. Juried by Jerri Zbiral. All media including photography.
prose: In Full View is the autumn exhibition at Woman Made Gallery, the Chicago feminist arts space founded in 1992 to champion women and nonbinary artists. The 2026 edition narrows eligibility deliberately: only artists aged 65 and over may apply. The brief is built around visibility — how older artists are seen, remembered, and represented — and around the texture of a fully lived life.

The exhibition is juried by Jerri Zbiral. Work is shown in person at the gallery's space at 1332 S. Halsted Street in Chicago from October 10 through November 7, 2026. Selected artists ship or hand-deliver finished work ready to install rather than producing in-house.

All media are welcome, photography included. Submissions are made through EntryThingy with one to three artworks per applicant. The entry fee is $24.60. WMG's standard terms apply to packaging, insurance, and return shipping.

The deadline is August 12, 2026. WMG has presented more than 475 exhibitions across three decades; In Full View sits squarely within their mission of putting underrepresented artists into a space where their work is genuinely seen.

calls.title: Feminism 250 — Woman Made America
calls.description: Open call from Woman Made Gallery (Chicago) for a group exhibition marking the United States' 250th anniversary year through feminist thought and activism. Themes include erasure, reclamation, intersectionality, activism, and feminist futures. Open to women and nonbinary artists at all career stages, internationally; all media accepted including photography, with the caveat that AI image-generation tools cannot be the primary creation method. Juried by the WMG Program Committee. In-person exhibition August 29–September 26, 2026 at WMG, 1332 S. Halsted St., Chicago. Submission via EntryThingy: 1–3 artworks plus a $30 entry fee.
calls.summary: Woman Made Gallery (Chicago) feminist group show marking the US 250th anniversary. Women/nb artists, all media including photography.
prose: Feminism 250: Woman Made America is Woman Made Gallery's contribution to the United States' 250th anniversary year, framed deliberately through a feminist lens. The exhibition asks where women and nonbinary artists locate themselves in that national history — what has been written in, what has been erased, and what is being reclaimed.

The brief gathers five throughlines: erasure, reclamation, intersectionality, activism, and feminist futures. Submissions are not limited to documentary or political work; the exhibition reads the theme broadly across approaches, from archival reworkings to staged portraiture to abstract gestures.

All media are eligible — photography sits alongside painting, sculpture, fiber, performance documentation — but generative AI cannot be the primary creation method. Submissions come through EntryThingy: one to three artworks, $30 fee. Juried by the WMG Program Committee.
The exhibition runs August 29 through September 26, 2026 in person at the gallery at 1332 S. Halsted Street, Chicago. The submission deadline is June 27, 2026.

calls.title: Brian Black Memorial Award 2026 — Adult Photo Competition
calls.description: Annual marine environmental photography award from Yachting Monthly magazine and Coppercoat, on the theme 'Our Inspiring Seas'. Open to UK residents only. Adult category awards camera equipment worth £750; separate junior category for ages 16 and under (equipment worth £500). Entries are a single image with a 300-word explanation of what, where, why, and how the photo was taken, plus a personal photo and a 100-word biography. Judges include circumnavigator Mike Golding, TV presenter/environmentalist Monty Halls, conservationist Dr Bob Brown, Sarah Brown (Brian Black's daughter), and the editorial teams of Yachting Monthly and Digital Camera World. Winners are published in Yachting Monthly and interviewed on the magazine's podcast; Yachting Monthly also donates £500 to Sea-Changers marine conservation charity. Submission via SurveyMonkey.
calls.summary: Yachting Monthly + Coppercoat marine environmental photo award on 'Our Inspiring Seas'. UK only. £750 camera equipment prize.
prose: The Brian Black Memorial Award is Yachting Monthly's annual marine environmental journalism and photography prize, run with sponsorship from Coppercoat. It is named for Brian Black, a sailor and journalist who covered the marine environment, and is administered with input from his daughter Sarah Brown alongside the magazine's editorial team.

The 2026 brief is 'Our Inspiring Seas' — work that captures encounters with marine wildlife or the wider marine environment in a way that reflects the theme's optimism rather than purely cataloging damage. The award sits alongside a parallel article competition and a separate junior photo category for entrants aged 16 and under.

Adult photo entries are a single image paired with a 300-word explanation covering what the photograph shows, where it was taken, why the entrant wanted to make it, and how the image was captured. Entrants also submit a personal photograph and a 100-word biography.

The judging panel pairs photography editors with marine specialists: circumnavigator Mike Golding, TV presenter and environmentalist Monty Halls, conservationist Dr Bob Brown, Sarah Brown, and the editorial teams of Yachting Monthly and Digital Camera World. The adult winner receives camera equipment worth £750; junior winner £500. Yachting Monthly also donates £500 to Sea-Changers, a marine conservation charity. Eligibility is restricted to UK residents. Entry is free, with a deadline of August 30, 2026.

calls.title: Humber Portrait Prize 2026
calls.description: Open call for contemporary portrait photography from Humberlands Photo Festival in Grimsby, UK. Spans the broad spectrum of portraiture, from formal commissioned portraits to spontaneous and personal images of friends and family. Open to photographers at all stages of their practice across two categories: open and young person. calls.summary: Free open call for the Humber Portrait Prize 2026 from Humberlands Photo Festival in Grimsby. Open and young person categories. Exhibition.
prose: The Humber Portrait Prize is the portrait photography competition of Humberlands, the photo festival based in Grimsby and the wider North East Lincolnshire coast. The 2026 edition runs as part of Humberlands 26, whose curatorial framework for the year is River — a frame the festival applies across its programme rather than a strict thematic requirement for prize submissions.

The brief itself is broad: contemporary portrait photography in its widest sense, from formal commissioned portraits through to spontaneous, personal images of friends and family. The prize is built around two parallel entry categories, an open category and a young person category, with selected work shown together as a single exhibition.

Selected photographs are exhibited at Grimbarians Studios, 87 Wharncliffe Road, in Grimsby Docks, during the festival period in late June 2026. The prize is presented as a curated selection rather than a single winner-take-all award, foregrounding the range of approaches photographers at different stages of their practice bring to portraiture.
Entry is free. Submission is made via a Google Form linked from humberlands.co.uk. Questions go to submissions@humberlands.co.uk. The deadline is June 5, 2026.

calls.title: Women Photograph + Leica Project Grants 2026

calls.summary: Three $10,000 grants from Women Photograph + Leica for women, nonbinary, trans, intersex documentary photographers. Free, international.
prose: Women Photograph is a non-profit founded in 2017 to elevate the work of women and nonbinary visual journalists. Its annual Project Grants, partnered with Leica, fund documentary photography projects from underrepresented practitioners across the discipline. The 2026 cycle awards three grants of $10,000 USD each, with applications opening May 20 and closing June 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET.

The grants are open to women, nonbinary, transgender, and intersex documentary photographers of any nationality, regardless of Women Photograph membership. Applications are submitted in English, though machine translation is accepted. Only one submission per applicant is permitted, and applicants must designate still photography as their primary medium; video and multimedia work may be referenced via links but is not the focus of the grant.

Funding is targeted at the hard costs of reporting: travel, fixers, equipment rental, photographer fees, and other production expenses tied to making new work. Books, exhibitions, workshops, and secondary outputs are explicitly outside the scope. Both new projects and ongoing long-term documentary projects are eligible, provided the applicant can demonstrate substantial existing work and a clear sense of what remains to be made.

Strong applications submit a story rather than a portfolio of single images, and reviewers look for engagement with the communities being documented beyond traditional journalistic distance. Any use of generative AI in submitted work must be disclosed clearly. Applications are made through Picter; there is no fee.

calls.title: Eamonn McCabe Bursary 2026

prose: The Eamonn McCabe Bursary is a £3,000 award administered by the Royal Photographic Society in partnership with the family of Eamonn McCabe and The Guardian, supporting a new body of photographic work on the theme of sporting endeavour. The bursary was established in 2024 in memory of the British photographer and picture editor Eamonn McCabe (1948–2022), who built his name shooting sport for The Observer in the late 1970s and 1980s before moving into wider editorial work, including a long tenure at The Guardian.

The theme is interpreted broadly. Professional sport is eligible, but the brief is explicit that projects engaging with grassroots and community sport are particularly welcome — including photographic work that addresses mental health, displaced communities, gender, disability, race, or other social issues through the lens of sport. Creative reinterpretations of the theme are encouraged.

Eligibility is open to photographers aged 30 or under at the time of application, internationally. Submitted work should be a new body of work suitable for publication and must not have been previously exhibited or published elsewhere. The winner receives the £3,000 cash bursary, mentoring from an industry specialist, and a solo exhibition.
There is no entry fee. The 2026 deadline is August 3 at 23:30 BST. Applications are made through the RPS's awards platform, where applicants submit a project proposal and supporting materials.

calls.title: LensCulture Street Photography Awards 2026

calls.title: Expand and Contract 2026 — American Documentary Photography

prose: Expand and Contract is the Los Angeles Center of Photography's recurring open-call series that uses contemporary themes to widen the conversation around photographic practice. The 2026 edition turns to American documentary photography, asking how America sees itself today — what it highlights, what it forgets, and what might be missing from the frame.

The juror is Dr. Rotem Rozental, LACP's Executive Director and Chief Curator. The selected works are presented in a virtual exhibition on LACP's website, running July 16 to October 16, 2026. The top three winners are also invited to show their work in an in-person component at LACP's DTLA gallery.

Prizes: 1st place receives $500 cash plus the in-person invitation; 2nd place $250 LACP gift card, a one-year LACP membership, and the in-person invitation; 3rd place $250 LACP gift card and the in-person invitation. Honorable mentions are placed in the online gallery for three months.

Submission is via Submittable. Fees are tiered: $25 for a single image up to $200 for 31–35 images. LACP members receive a 25% discount across all tiers. AI involvement beyond basic editing must be disclosed in the submission description; watermarks are not accepted. The deadline is June 16, 2026 at midnight PST; acceptances are announced June 30, 2026.

calls.title: The Illume Awards 2026
calls.description: Adventure and action sports photography awards, formerly Red Bull Illume, now operating as an independent contest with environmental NGO partners (Leave No Trace, World Bicycle Relief). Sixteen categories — eight sports (Adventure, Aerial, Bike, Climb, Skate, Snow, Surf, Trail) and eight themes (Close-Up, Emerging, Innovation, Lifestyle, Masterpiece, Playground, RAW, Spirit). Sixty international judges; 160 finalists are featured in the physical Illume Photobook and may be selected for the Illume Exhibit Tour. The overall winner is announced at a global awards ceremony in December 2026. Prizes from media partners include premium camera and storage gear (including Angelbird). Free to enter; open to all levels from amateur to professional. Since 2006 the contest has received nearly 250,000 submissions.
calls.summary: Adventure and action sports photography awards (formerly Red Bull Illume). Free entry, 16 categories, camera gear, photobook, exhibition tour.
prose: The Illume Awards is the new, independent continuation of what was Red Bull Illume — a long-running, high-profile competition focused on adventure and action sports photography. The 2026 edition is the first under the new branding, with an expanded environmental focus and partnerships with Leave No Trace and World Bicycle Relief.

There are sixteen categories total: eight sports — Adventure, Aerial, Bike, Climb, Skate, Snow, Surf, Trail — and eight themes — Close-Up, Emerging, Innovation, Lifestyle, Masterpiece, Playground, RAW, Spirit. Photographers can submit images to multiple categories. Sixty international judges review submissions.

160 finalists are featured in the physical Illume Photobook and may be selected for the Illume Exhibit Tour, which travels internationally. Prizes from media partners include premium camera and storage gear (including Angelbird). The overall winner is announced at a global awards ceremony in December 2026.

calls.description: Der Greif × Foundation Manuel Rivera-Ortiz open call for Les Rencontres d'Arles 2026, themed Read Against the Machine. Invites work that resists automated interpretation and reclaims the social act of looking — how meaning is shaped through conversation rather than algorithms. 12–16 selected artists join an intensive collective image-reading workshop on July 8; an additional cohort is invited to 1:1 Face-to-Face portfolio reviews on July 10. prose: Read Against the Machine is a Der Greif × Foundation Manuel Rivera-Ortiz collaboration for the 57th Rencontres d'Arles. The brief invites photographic work that resists automated interpretation and reclaims the social act of looking, asking what happens when meaning is shaped through conversation rather than algorithms.

The programme has two strands. 12–16 selected artists join a collaborative editing workshop on July 8 led by Der Greif's jury and MRO's Artistic Director Alejandro León Cannock — an intensive collective image-reading session. A separate cohort is invited to one-on-one Face-to-Face portfolio reviews on July 10 with Der Greif editors and an MRO guest reviewer.

All selected participants' work is included in a collective screening at the MRO Foundation during Arles, on July 10. The screening sits within the wider Rencontres programme and brings the workshop conversations into a public, communal viewing.

Submission is through Picter. The fee is voluntary, with a 15€ suggested donation; vouchers are available on request via voucher-special@dergreif.org. Applicants must already be attending Les Rencontres d'Arles — travel and accommodation are not covered. The deadline is June 14, 2026 at 11:59 PM CET, extended from June 7.

calls.title: Queer Quintessential 2026
calls.description: Der Greif's Pride Month 2026 open call, initiated by queer Program Curator Francesca Hummler. Invites LGBTQIA+ lens-based artists to explore queer life, identity, intimacy, and forms of community through photography and image-based practices. Welcomes work engaging with self-representation, chosen family, visibility, and the relationship between public and private space. Selected artists featured in an online exhibition on Der Greif's homepage and invited to join small-group Face-to-Face critique sessions, with opportunities for future collaborations through Der Greif Studio. Voluntary submission fee with 10€ suggested donation; 50% or 100% discount vouchers available on request. Open globally.
jury: Francesca Hummler, Queer Program Curator, Der Greif
calls.summary: Pride Month open call for LGBTQIA+ lens-based artists. Online exhibition + Face-to-Face critique. PWYC; deadline 15 June 2026.
prose: Queer Quintessential is Der Greif's Pride Month 2026 open call, initiated by the platform's queer Program Curator Francesca Hummler. The brief invites LGBTQIA+ lens-based artists to explore queer life, identity, intimacy, and forms of community through photography and image-based practices.

The call welcomes work engaging with self-representation, chosen family, visibility, and the relationship between public and private space. Submissions are evaluated on artistic quality, conceptual clarity, openness to dialogue and process, and engagement with themes of identity and community.

Selected artists are featured in an online exhibition on Der Greif's homepage and invited to join small-group Face-to-Face critique sessions — direct conversation rather than written feedback. Selection also brings visibility within Der Greif's international community and possibilities for future collaboration through Der Greif Studio.

Submission is through Picter. The fee is voluntary (Pay-What-You-Can) with a 10€ suggested donation; financial-assistance vouchers for 50% or 100% discount are available by emailing voucher-special-2@dergreif.org. Eligibility is open globally to LGBTQIA+ lens-based artists. The deadline is June 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM CET.

calls.title: PhotoVogue Global Open Call 2026 — Brave New Visions
calls.description: PhotoVogue's annual global open call from Vogue Italia, themed Brave New Visions: Creativity as Rebellion. Photographers, video makers, and multimedia artists worldwide invited to submit work that responds to the present through a distinct visual language. All genres welcome — fashion, documentary, portraiture, fine art, experimental. $12,000 total in three grants: $6,000 Outstanding Vision Grant, $4,000 Vision Grant, $2,000 Rising Voice Grant. Selected artists are presented at the next PhotoVogue Festival, published across Vogue's global editions, and offered virtual portfolio reviews. Open May 14 – September 11, 2026.
calls.summary: PhotoVogue's 2026 global open call. $12,000 in three grants, festival exhibition, Vogue publication. Free; deadline 11 September 2026.
prose: PhotoVogue is the global photography platform run by Vogue Italia under editorial direction Alessia Glaviano. The Global Open Call is the platform's annual flagship, and the 2026 cycle is themed Brave New Visions: Creativity as Rebellion. PhotoVogue frames the brief as a stance rather than a subject — it is asking for work where the way the artist sees is itself an act of resistance against visual indifference, not adherence to a specified theme.

Three grants split $12,000: the Outstanding Vision Grant of $6,000 for an artist expanding the boundaries of visual language; the Vision Grant of $4,000 for an artist with a strong and singular perspective; and the Rising Voice Grant of $2,000 for an emerging artist showing clarity, originality, and promise. Selected artists are presented at the next PhotoVogue Festival in Milan, with the possibility of publication across Vogue's global editions and an invitation to PhotoVogue's Virtual Portfolio Reviews.

The call welcomes photography, video, and multimedia projects across all genres — fashion, documentary, portraiture, fine art, and experimental practice. Submissions may include up to 15 images, an optional 60-second video trailer, or a combination for multimedia projects. Artists must be 18 or older; AI-generated work is not eligible.

Submissions are free and hosted on Picter, open May 14 through September 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM CET. Contact for the call is Daniel Rodríguez-Gordillo at Condé Nast (daniel.rodriguez-gordillo@condenast.es).

calls.title: BWP x Nikon Grant Fund 2026 — Quarter 2
calls.description: Second-quarter 2026 cycle of the Black Women Photographers x Nikon $50K Grant Fund — a year-long program supporting Black women photographers globally through four quarterly grant opportunities. The Q2 recipient receives a $2,500 USD unrestricted cash grant plus a Nikon Z6III with 24-70mm f/4 lens kit. Funding can support photography projects, production, travel, equipment, or other professional needs. BWP is a global membership community founded in 2020 by Polly Irungu, with members across 60+ countries and 35 U.S. states. To date, the program has awarded over $230,000 in financial grants plus $80,000 in camera equipment. Applications for Q2 close June 5, 2026.
calls.summary: Quarterly grant for Black women photographers worldwide. $2,500 cash + Nikon Z6III kit. Q2 2026 cycle.
prose: Black Women Photographers (BWP) is a global community founded in 2020 by Polly Irungu — a Kenyan-American photo editor — to combat the underrepresentation of Black women photographers in the industry. BWP's membership directory now spans more than 60 countries and 35 U.S. states. The BWP x Nikon Grant Fund is the organization's flagship support program, structured as four quarterly grant cycles running across 2026.

Each quarterly recipient receives a $2,500 USD unrestricted cash grant plus a Nikon Z6III with 24-70mm f/4 lens kit. The funds carry no project restrictions — past recipients have used them for production, travel, gear replacement, studio setup, and other professional needs. The Q2 2026 deadline is June 5.

Eligibility is for Black women photographers globally, including emerging, independent, and professional practitioners as well as visual storytellers and content creators. There is no application fee. To date, the program has distributed more than $230,000 in cash grants and $80,000 in Nikon mirrorless gear across previous cycles.

Applications are submitted via the BWP grant fund page. The program is run jointly with Nikon USA and is one of the most consistent direct-funding initiatives for Black women photographers in the field.

calls.title: 2026 Black & White Award
calls.description: The Independent Photographer's monthly themed competition cycle, this round dedicated to black and white photography in any genre — landscape, portrait, street, documentary, or abstract — emphasizing mastery of light, composition, and shadow. Total prize pool $2,700: 1st prize $1,000, 2nd $600, 3rd $400, plus seven $100 finalist prizes. Winners exhibited internationally at PBC Gallery London and featured to the platform's 965k+ Instagram and 200k+ Facebook followers. All entrants receive a free online portfolio. Judge: Monica Denevan. Submissions are tiered: $15 for 1 image, $30 for 3, $45 for 6. AI-generated work not accepted; photography-based submissions only (film, digital, smartphone). JPEG or PNG, minimum 1200px longest side, maximum 10MB.
calls.summary: Black & white photography competition. $2,700 prize pool, PBC Gallery London exhibition. Judge: Monica Denevan.
prose: The Independent Photographer (TIP) is a London-based online photography platform that runs themed monthly competitions and publishes editorial work, interviews, and book reviews. The 2026 Black & White Award is the platform's monochrome-themed cycle, focused on mastery of light, composition, and shadow across any genre — landscape, portrait, street, documentary, or abstract.

Total prize pool is $2,700: first place receives $1,000, second $600, third $400, and seven runners-up receive $100 each. Winners are exhibited at PBC Gallery in London and featured across The Independent Photographer's Instagram (965k+ followers) and Facebook (200k+) channels. All entrants receive a free online portfolio on the platform.

Selection is by Monica Denevan, the American fine-art photographer known for her striking monochrome work in Burma and beyond. TIP's broader jury roster has historically included names like Steve McCurry, Ed Kashi, Maggie Steber, Magdalena Herrera, and Fiona Shields — useful context for emerging entrants weighing this competition against others at similar price points.

Eligibility is open globally. Submissions are tiered: $15 for one image, $30 for three, $45 for six. JPEG or PNG, minimum 1200 pixels on one side, maximum 10MB per file. AI-generated work is not accepted — photography-based submissions only, with film, digital, and smartphone all welcome. The final deadline is May 31, 2026.

calls.title: Passage Art-Residency-Programme 2026
calls.description: Four-week residency in Wittenberg, Germany in October 2026 for two photographers or filmmakers. €5,000 grant per resident plus four-week accommodation; additional €1,000 childcare supplement if accompanied by a child. Run by Polygona Kunstverein e.V. as part of the KOBRA Cultural Network Wittenberg. Two themes to choose from: Ferropolis (the historic Zschornewitz coal power station — energy history and industrial transformation) or RFB (Research Library of Reformation Studies — knowledge production and visual representation in historical scientific texts). On-site support from Polygona staff plus topic-specific expert guidance. Residents develop an artistic project, conduct a one-day workshop for young people, give a public artist talk, and contribute to documentary filming over two days. National and international artists welcome (18+); students not eligible. Submit 10 final project photographs by December 31, 2026. Jury decision announced from June 20, 2026.
calls.summary: 4-week residency in Wittenberg, Germany. €5,000 grant + accommodation. Themes: Ferropolis power station or Reformation archive.
prose: The Passage Art-Residency-Programme is run by Polygona Kunstverein e.V., a Wittenberg-based art association, as part of the KOBRA Cultural Network Wittenberg (2025–2029). The 2026 cycle offers two four-week residency positions in October at Wittenberg in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany — open to photographers and filmmakers, with no upper age limit and no application fee.

Each resident receives a €5,000 grant plus four weeks of accommodation. An additional €1,000 childcare supplement is available for residents accompanied by a child — a relatively rare provision among comparable programs. Travel, local transport, materials, and living expenses beyond the grant are applicant-funded.

Applicants choose between two research contexts. Theme One is Ferropolis — the historic Zschornewitz coal power station, framed around energy history and post-industrial transformation. Theme Two is the Research Library of Reformation Studies (RFB), framed around knowledge production and visual representation in historical scientific texts. The thematic structure means the program is best suited to artists with an existing or readily adaptable interest in industrial heritage or archive-based practice.

The residency carries program obligations beyond studio work: a one-day workshop for young people, a public artist talk, and two days of contributing to documentary filming. Selected artists also submit 10 final project photographs by December 31, 2026. Applications close May 30, 2026; the jury decision is announced from June 20.

calls.title: CCI Fellowships 2026
calls.description: Sixth annual cycle of fellowships from the Green Family Foundation Caribbean Cultural Institute (CCI) at Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM). Three parallel tracks: CCI Artist Fellowship (residency at Bakehouse Art Complex Miami for up to two months, stipend, travel, $4,000 production budget); CCI Research Fellowship (hybrid in-person/remote over four months, travel and two-week Miami residency covered, research stipend, up to $1,000 in research expenses); and CCI + WOPHA Fellowship — the photography track, open to emerging and mid-career women and nonbinary photographers from the Caribbean or its diaspora. The CCI + WOPHA Fellowship runs September through November 2026, hybrid format, with September residency at El Espacio 23 in Miami; includes stipend, $4,000 production funds, round-trip airfare if not Miami-based, plus mentorship and collaboration with Green Space Miami and FIU-LACC. Photographic practice is defined broadly: cameras and cameraless work, automated/computational processes, augmented photography, and image collecting/archiving/circulation. International applicants must secure their own visas — PAMM cannot sponsor.
calls.summary: Three CCI fellowships at Pérez Art Museum Miami. WOPHA photography track for women & nonbinary Caribbean photographers.
prose: The Green Family Foundation Caribbean Cultural Institute (CCI) is the Caribbean-focused research and curatorial arm of Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM). The 2026 fellowships are the program's sixth annual cycle, run across three parallel tracks: CCI Artist Fellowship, CCI Research Fellowship, and CCI + WOPHA Fellowship — the photography-specific track operated jointly with Women Photographers International Archive (WOPHA).

The CCI + WOPHA Fellowship is reserved for emerging and mid-career women and nonbinary photographers from the Caribbean or its diaspora. The fellowship runs September through November 2026 in hybrid format, with the in-person residency component held at El Espacio 23 in Miami during September. Funding includes a stipend, up to $4,000 in production funds, and round-trip airfare for non-Miami-based fellows. Mentorship and collaboration opportunities extend through Green Space Miami and the FIU Latin American and Caribbean Center (FIU-LACC).

The brief's definition of photographic practice is deliberately expansive: image-making with or without cameras, automated and computational processes, augmented photography, and the collecting, archiving, and circulation of images. The framing fits both traditional photographic projects and research-led or post-photographic work.

All three CCI fellowships share a June 1, 2026 deadline (11:59 PM EDT) and require a 500-word cover letter, CV, 500-word artist statement, 1,000-word project proposal with budget and timeline, and a portfolio. Application is free. International applicants must secure their own visas — PAMM cannot sponsor.

calls.title: Photography+ Emerging Talent 2026

Open to BA and MA graduates, plus image-based artists within the first five years of their practice and/or graduation. Ten awardees featured in the next Photography+ issue; all 10 included in an evening projection at Kranj Foto Fest. A second selected artist receives a £200 printing voucher from Spectrum Photographic and an Instagram takeover. Funded by Photoworks, Spectrum Photographic, and Picter.

prose: Photoworks is the UK photography agency based in Brighton — a major commissioning, publishing, and development organization for photography in Britain. Photography+ is the agency's online magazine, and the Emerging Talent issue is its annual open-call edition dedicated to early-career image-makers. The 2026 cycle is open to BA and MA graduates and to image-based artists within the first five years of their practice and/or graduation.

Ten awardees are selected. All ten are featured in the next Photography+ issue and included in an evening projection at Kranj Foto Fest in Slovenia. Two additional awards are layered on top: one selected artist receives a one-year Photoworks membership plus curatorial and editorial mentoring; a second receives a £200 printing voucher from Spectrum Photographic and an Instagram takeover.

The 2026 jury is Emma Bowkett (Director of Photography, Financial Times), Louise Fedotov-Clements (Director, Photoworks), Fernanda Prado Verčič (Founding Director, Kranj Foto Fest), Maryam Wahid (Head of Programs and Outreach, Tasweer Photography Festival), and Amin Yousefi (Assistant Curator and Editor, Photography+). The panel mixes editorial, institutional, and festival-side perspectives — useful for emerging photographers thinking about where their work fits next.

Applications are made through Picter: up to 15 images from a single project plus a 200-word artist statement. Only one project per applicant. The call is free to enter. The deadline is June 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM. Program funding comes from Photoworks, Spectrum Photographic, and Picter.

calls.title: No Theme Open Call 2026
calls.description: Open theme — any subject matter or photographic medium (digital, film, alternative process). Opening reception August 7, 2026, 6–9 PM. Submission fee waivers available on request; fees support the gallery and a scholarship fund for printing and framing. Submissions reviewed blind. calls.summary: Open-theme show at Oakland Photo Workshop. 30–45 in-person + 10–20 online. Bay Area artists. Opening Aug 7, 2026.
prose: East Bay Photo Collective (EBPCO) is an Oakland-based photography nonprofit founded in 2017, operating the Oakland Photo Workshop gallery in Chinatown and a darkroom in downtown Oakland. The mission centers on access — facilities, education, and community for East Bay photographers, including those who are under-served or without a creative community elsewhere. The Oakland Photo Workshop gallery has shown over 200 local artists since opening in 2021.

The No Theme Open Call is EBPCO's annual open-theme exhibition — any subject, any photographic medium (digital, film, alternative process) — with one process restriction: generative AI is not accepted. The brief is deliberately broad to surface the range of Bay Area practice rather than steer toward a single mood or genre.

Selection structure: 30 to 45 pieces are chosen for the in-person gallery exhibition at Oakland Photo Workshop (312 8th St., Oakland), plus an additional 10 to 20 for the online exhibition. The opening reception is August 7, 2026, from 6 to 9 PM. Submissions are reviewed blind by volunteer jurors.

Eligibility is geographic: artists must be 18 or older and based in or around the Bay Area — this is a regional show by design. Submission is through Artwork Archive: up to 3 images for $35, or $20 for students and low-income artists. Fee waivers are available on request — emailing info@ebpco.org. Framed work cannot exceed 24 inches wide. The deadline was extended to May 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM.

calls.title: MUUS Collection Research Fellowship 2026
calls.description: Inaugural research fellowship from the MUUS Collection, a New York-area photography archive holding nearly half a million images from the archives of André de Dienes, Fred W. McDarrah, Larry Fink, Rosalind Fox Solomon, Deborah Turbeville, and Alfred Wertheimer. $20,000 grant to one curator or academic to spend time in the archives and the new MUUSEUM Research Portal developing an exhibition or publication concept. Travel costs to the archive fully covered as part of the grant. Mentorship from an advisory board of leading curators and directors. Grant runs November 2026–November 2027. Winner decided in October and announced at Paris Photo in November 2026. Open globally to curators and academics.
jury: Mark Sealy OBE, Executive Director, Autograph ABP
Sophie Wright, Executive Director, MUUS Collection
calls.summary: $20,000 grant for a curator or academic to develop an exhibition or publication using MUUS Collection's archives. Travel covered.
prose: The MUUS Collection is an American 20th-century photography collection based just outside Manhattan, holding nearly half a million images and supporting ephemera — contact sheets, personal papers, manuscripts, and publications. The current archives include the work of André de Dienes, Larry Fink, Fred W. McDarrah (the downtown New York scene, Dylan, Ginsberg, Warhol, and the Stonewall Uprising), Rosalind Fox Solomon, Deborah Turbeville, and Alfred Wertheimer.

The Research Fellowship is the Collection's inaugural grant program, launched in 2026. One $20,000 grant is awarded to a curator or academic for time in the physical archives and on the new MUUSEUM Research Portal, with the goal of producing an exhibition or publication concept drawn from the holdings. The grant covers travel to the archive in full, separately from the cash award.

The fellowship runs November 2026 through November 2027, with mentorship sessions across the year from the advisory board: Nathalie Herschdorfer (Director, Photo Elysée), Sarah Meister (Executive Director, Aperture), Paul Roth (Director, Image Centre), Mark Sealy OBE (Executive Director, Autograph ABP), and Sophie Wright (Executive Director, MUUS Collection).

Eligibility is restricted to curators and academics — this is a research grant, not an artist's fellowship. Applications open May 1 and close July 31, 2026. The winner is decided in October 2026 and announced publicly at Paris Photo in November.

calls.title: LUMINEX 4.0
calls.description: Fourth edition of LUMINEX, NOW Art's outdoor art and technology exhibition in Los Angeles. Open call for artists working at the intersection of art, light, and technology. Selected artists receive a $1,000 stipend plus production fees based on approved project. Free to apply.
calls.summary: Outdoor art and technology exhibition in Los Angeles. $1,000 stipend per artist plus production support based on approved project.
prose: LUMINEX is an outdoor art and technology exhibition staged in Los Angeles, produced by NOW Art — the LA-based public art organization. The 2026 cycle is the program's fourth edition (LUMINEX 4.0).

The brief is positioned at the intersection of art, light, and technology — projection, immersive installation, and light-based work made for public outdoor space rather than gallery interiors. The audience is the city itself.

The financial structure is two-part rather than a single award. Each selected artist receives a $1,000 stipend. The split lets the organization fund work at different scales without forcing a flat budget.
Eligibility is open. Application is free.
Submission is through the Fillout RFP at nowart.fillout.com/luminex4. The 2026 deadline is June 5 at 11:59 PM PST.

calls.title: SlowExposures 2026 — Photography of the Rural South
calls.description: 20th annual Main Exhibition of contemporary photography of the American South. Submissions must be made in 16 Southern US states (AL, AR, DE, FL, GA, KY, LA, MD, MS, NC, OK, SC, TN, TX, VA, WV). Up to 6 images. Selected work shown September 18–20, 2026 at the historic R.F. Strickland Building in Concord, GA, then travels to Cochran Gallery in LaGrange, GA. Jurors Dennis Kiel and Coco Conroy.
calls.summary: 20th SlowExposures festival's Main Exhibition. Photography made in 16 Southern US states. Concord, GA. Up to 6 images.
prose: SlowExposures is a long-running annual photography festival in Pike County, Georgia dedicated to images of the contemporary American South. Founded in 2003 and now in its 20th year, the festival anchors a weekend of exhibitions, talks, and the popular PopUp Tour in and around the small town of Concord.

The 2026 Main Exhibition is regionally focused: photographs must be made in one of sixteen Southern states — Alabama, Arkansas, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, or West Virginia. The brief invites work that captures the diversity, contradictions, and complexity of the South rather than a fixed theme.

Selected images — typically 70 to 90 prints — are displayed at the historic R.F. Strickland Building in downtown Concord during the festival weekend, September 18–20, 2026, then move on to a month-long run at the Cochran Gallery in LaGrange, Georgia.

Jurors for the 2026 edition are Dennis Kiel and Coco Conroy. The entry fee is $50 for up to six images and underwrites venue rental, juror expenses, receptions, publicity, and awards. All entrants — selected or not — are invited as honored guests to the private Soiree on Friday night at Split Oak Farm.

calls.title: Focus 2026 — Atlanta Photography Group
calls.description: Open-themed juried exhibition for APG members based in Georgia. Juror Anne Leighton Massoni, Executive Director of the Houston Center for Photography. 2 to 8 images per entry. calls.summary: APG's open-themed juried show. $1,000 MOCA GA purchase award + permanent collection. Members-only, Georgia artists.
prose: Atlanta Photography Group (APG) is a long-standing nonprofit photography organization in Atlanta, Georgia, with its own gallery on Piedmont Avenue. Focus is APG's open-themed juried members' exhibition, programmed annually to recognize work by Georgia photographers.

The 2026 juror is Anne Leighton Massoni, Executive Director of the Houston Center for Photography, who selects from across the open-themed submissions without a prescribed subject. Eligibility is restricted to APG members who are based in Georgia, and to artists whose work hasn't appeared in APG's Main or Maloof galleries within the past three years.

Selected work is exhibited July 21 through August 21, 2026 at the APG gallery at 1544 Piedmont Avenue NE, Atlanta, with an opening reception on July 23. The top award is the $1,000 APG / Museum of Contemporary Art of Georgia Purchase Award, with the winning work entering MOCA GA's permanent collection.

Entries accept 2 to 8 images. Fees scale by submission window: $35–$75 early (May 7–15), $40–$85 regular (May 16–31), $50–$95 late (June 1–5), with reduced student rates of $30–$70. The deadline is June 5, 2026 at midnight Eastern.

calls.title: Light on Cut Paper: Photography & Collage
calls.description: Third in a NOPA series exploring the intersection of photography and collage. Seeks artists who collage their own photographs, make photomontage, or use a collage-like process in composition or in the darkroom. Selected work exhibited June 10 – July 10, 2026 at the NOPA gallery in New Orleans. 60/40 sales split (artist/gallery). Juror Jan Kather.
calls.summary: Third in a NOPA series at the intersection of photography and collage. Photomontage, darkroom collage, hybrid composition. New Orleans.
prose: The New Orleans Photo Alliance (NOPA) is a long-running nonprofit photography organization in New Orleans, Louisiana that runs themed juried exhibitions, the Michael P. Smith Fund for documentary photography, and educational programs. "Light on Cut Paper: Photography & Collage" is the third call in a NOPA series focused on artwork at the intersection of photography and collage.

The brief is medium-specific: work by artists who collage their own photographs, make photomontage, or use a collage-like process — whether in the composition of photographs or in the darkroom itself. Applicants must submit a brief statement explaining how the work demonstrates this intersection rather than only sending images. NOPA states openness to any work where the artist feels the image speaks to this hybrid practice.

Selected work is exhibited June 10 through July 10, 2026 at the NOPA gallery. The gallery takes 40% commission on sales; artists receive 60%. All work must be delivered framed and ready to hang by June 5, 2026 — international shipping logistics are the artist's responsibility.

Juror is Jan Kather, with notifications sent May 18, 2026. The deadline is May 12, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. MDT. Entry fees: $25 for NOPA members, $35 for non-members; combined membership-plus-entry options are also available.

Eligibility is international; all ages welcome; NOPA membership is not required to apply. Image specs: 1 to 5 images per entry, JPEG/JPG, under 5MB, minimum 1200 pixels on the longest side. Digitally manipulated photographs are permitted; AI-generated photographs are not accepted.

calls.title: SHOTS Magazine #172 — The Human Figure
calls.description: Fall 2026 issue (#172) of the black & white photography quarterly, in print since 1986. Theme is the human figure — no need to be literal. Submit up to 8 grayscale images at 300ppi (color files converted to B&W upon receipt). Free for current/renewing subscribers; $25 for non-subscribers ($28 international). All processes, formats, and experience levels welcome. All submitting artists receive a complimentary copy of the issue. Initial selection by editor Elizabeth Flinsch.
calls.summary: B&W photography quarterly since 1986. Issue #172 themed The Human Figure. Up to 8 grayscale images. Free for subscribers.
prose: SHOTS Magazine is a black-and-white photography quarterly that has been in print since 1986 — long-running among indie B&W publications. The 2026 fall issue is #172, themed The Human Figure.
The brief leaves room: human figure does not need to be literal. The selection welcomes interpretations that bend or abstract the figure rather than restricting to traditional portraiture or nudes.

The publication is process-restricted: black-and-white only. Submitted color files are converted to grayscale on receipt — applicants should consider how their work translates rather than assume color information will carry.

All processes, formats, and experience levels are welcome. All submitting artists receive a complimentary copy of the issue regardless of selection — a small but meaningful gesture for a paid-subscription publication.

Initial selection is by editor Elizabeth Flinsch, with publisher Douglas Beasley involved. Submission is through the SHOTS website with up to 8 grayscale images at 300 ppi. Submission is free for current and renewing subscribers; $25 for non-subscribers ($28 international). The 2026 deadline is June 1.

calls.title: Collection 2026 - Decode Gallery
calls.description: Decode Gallery's open-theme exhibition — no themes, no limits. At least 26 images selected. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ultra Premium Luster paper, museum-quality framing and matting handled by the gallery. 50% commission on sales. Open worldwide to all skill levels. Exhibition August 1–29, 2026 in Tucson, AZ. Juror: Holly Hart, Decode Gallery founder.
jury: Holly Hart, Conceptual Fine Art Photographer & Decode Gallery Founder
calls.summary: Open-theme show — no themes, no limits. 26+ selected. Free pro printing on Epson + museum framing. Tucson, AZ.
prose: Decode Gallery is a Tucson, Arizona photography gallery founded by conceptual fine art photographer Holly Hart, who also serves as juror for the gallery's calls. "Collection 2026" is the gallery's open-theme exhibition — no themes, no subject restrictions, no limits beyond technical quality.

The selection structure is generous: at least 26 images are selected for the physical exhibition. What's unusual: the gallery covers all professional printing on Epson printers with Ultra Premium Luster paper, plus museum-quality framing in 22×22 inch white frames with precut white mats — the artist provides only the high-resolution JPEG. Prints are retained in the gallery's flat files for two years after the exhibition for further promotion and sales.

Sales terms split commission 50/50 between artist and gallery. Selected work is also promoted across Decode's website, social media, and editorial publications. The 2026 exhibition runs August 1 through 29 in Tucson.

Entry fee is $40 for up to 5 images. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers at all skill levels. The deadline is June 27, 2026; selected artists are notified within two weeks of the deadline.

calls.title: SE Center for Photography — The Art of Architecture
calls.description: Virtual juried exhibition seeking architectural photography in all forms — urban or rural, B&W or color, analog, digital or antique processes. Juror Michael Pannier (fine art photographer based in Greenville, SC) selects 35–40 images for the virtual gallery. Selected artists receive a portfolio review with the juror. 0% commission on sales. All photographers regardless of location, age, or skill level.
calls.summary: Virtual show on architectural photography — urban, rural, analog or digital. Juror: Michael Pannier. Portfolio review.
calls.verifyNote: Page calendar lists 2025 dates (4/20/25 to 8/30/25) but the URL and title say "Architectural Prospectus 26" — appears to be a stale-year typo on the org's site. Treat 2026-07-01 deadline as authoritative.
prose: The Southeast Center for Photography (SEC4P) is a Greenville, South Carolina photography organization (104 S Main St, Suite 841) that runs themed virtual juried exhibitions. "The Art of Architecture" is the center's open call for architectural photography in all forms — urban or rural, black-and-white or color, analog, digital, or antique processes.

The 2026 cycle is juried by Michael Pannier, a Greenville-based fine art photographer with thirty years' practice. Selection takes 35 to 40 images for an approximately one-month virtual gallery, with social media promotion across SEC4P's Facebook, Instagram, and X channels and an archived online slideshow plus video walkthrough. Selected artists also receive a portfolio review with the SEC4P director.
Entry fees: $35 for non-members for up to 5 images ($6 each additional, max 15), or $28 / $5 for SEC4P members. There is no sales commission.

Eligibility is open to all photographers regardless of location, age, or skill level. Work previously exhibited at SEC4P within the prior two years is ineligible. The 2026 deadline is July 1; results are announced July 15.

calls.title: Ethereal
calls.description: Seeking images that explore the intangible — works that evoke lightness, transience, and the space between what is seen and what is felt. Both traditional and experimental photographic processes welcome. Juror: John Horowitz, photographer and curator whose work resides in Purdue University's permanent collection. Exhibition June 5 – July 1, 2026 at A Photographer's Place in Raleigh, NC. Opening reception June 5, 7–9 PM.
calls.summary: Images that explore the intangible — lightness, transience, the space between seen and felt. Juror: John Horowitz.
prose: A Photographer's Place is a Raleigh, North Carolina photography gallery and printing studio. "Ethereal" is the gallery's themed call exploring the intangible — work that evokes lightness, transience, and the space between what is seen and what is felt. The brief is interpretive: both traditional and experimental photographic processes are welcome.

The exhibition runs June 5 through July 1, 2026, with an opening reception on June 5 from 7 to 9 PM. Selection is by John Horowitz, a working photographer and curator with work held in Purdue University's permanent collection.

Selected artists may optionally have their work printed at the gallery on the Canon ImagePROGRAF Pro-1100 (the gallery's in-house printer) for an additional fee — an unusually integrated offering for an open-call exhibition.

Entry fee is $35 for up to 5 images. Eligibility is open to photographers of all skill levels. Submissions are JPEGs at minimum 3,000 pixels on the longest side, color or black and white, with titles for each image. Submissions go through Smarter Entry. The 2026 deadline is May 22; juror selections announced May 25; work delivery June 3; exhibition opens June 5.

calls.title: Critical Mass 2026
calls.description: Photolucida's annual program connecting photographers with the international photography community. Submit 10 images for pre-screening; approximately 200 finalists are then reviewed by up to 200 photography professionals worldwide — curators, gallerists, publishers, editors, educators, and media. The Top 50 are announced each year, alongside book awards and exhibition opportunities. Past finalists have gained acquisitions, exhibitions, and publication features. Open to photographers at any career stage. AI-generated imagery is not accepted for the 2026 cycle.
jury: Alexa Becker, Photography Coach & Publishing Consultant, DGPh
Borbála Jász, Vice-Director, PH21 Gallery, Barcelona
Crista Dix, Executive Director, Griffin Museum of Photography
