prose: The Lucie Foundation Photo Book Prize is the foundation's annual award for photography in book form. Three categories carry cash prizes: Book of the Year ($3,000, awarded to the publisher), First Book ($2,000, awarded to the photographer), and Self-Published ($2,000, awarded to the photographer). The prize structure reflects how photo books actually get made — recognizing publishers for their craft, debut authors for theirs, and independents for going it alone.

Eligible work spans the full range of contemporary photo publishing: traditionally published books and zines, hand-made and limited editions, exhibition catalogues, photography combined with other media, multi-artist anthologies, and single-artist publications. Books must be published between September 2024 and September 2026 to qualify for the 2026 cycle. There is no submission limit per applicant.

Entry fees are $75 for publishers and $50 for photographers on the first submission, with 20% off subsequent category entries of the same book. Submissions require a completed form and a PDF of the book up to 60MB; individual JPG files used for evaluation must be 72 DPI and under 4MB each. Final deadline is September 15, 2026 (midnight ET); winners are announced in fall 2026.

The eleven-juror panel for 2026 includes photographers Martin Schoeller, Jamel Shabazz, Lele Saveri, and Paul Baldonado; editors Merve Arkunlar (212 Magazine) and Elizabeth Krist; and curators Eleni Mouzakiti, Yumi Goto, Emmanuel Iduma (Tender Photos), and Monica Aguilar Villamarin.

calls.title: Nes Artist Residency — Fall 2026

calls.summary: Residency in Skagaströnd, Iceland. 1-6 month stays. Private bedroom, shared studio. Artists and writers.
prose: Nes is a 1- to 6-month residency in Skagaströnd, a small fishing town on Iceland's north coast. The program is deliberately interdisciplinary: the same campus hosts visual artists, writers, musicians, dancers, and researchers, with discipline-specific spaces — a research library for writers, the BioPol dance studio, a ceramics workshop, and access to the local music school. Visual artists receive an individual workspace inside a shared open-plan studio.

The fall 2026 cycle covers September, October, and November; private bedrooms and shared common areas are included. Monthly cost is €850. The application fee is $15 and submissions go through SlideRoom; selection prioritizes "curiosity and experimentation" over conventional credentials. Nes does not currently offer scholarships or stipends — artists fund their own stay.

The location is remote: Skagaströnd has a population of about 500, and the residency draws on that isolation as part of its program. Past residents have used the time for self-directed projects, with optional artistic and cultural exchange built into the schedule.

calls.title: SCAN Tarragona — Talent Latent 2026
calls.description: International photography festival open call. Theme: Metamorphosis. Selected projects exhibited at the festival (Oct 16–Nov 29, 2026) and receive €500 fee. Open to photographers 18+ of any nationality.
calls.summary: International festival open call. Theme: Metamorphosis. €500 fee for selected projects. Exhibition Oct-Nov 2026.
prose: SCAN is the international photography festival organized by Tarragona City Council in Catalonia. Talent Latent is the festival's annual project-based open call, separate from the SCAN Full Contact Award which is structured around portfolio review. The 2026 Talent Latent theme is Metamorphosis.
Selected projects are exhibited at the festival, October 16 – November 29, 2026 — a six-week run. Each selected artist receives a €500 fee.
Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+ of any nationality. The Talent Latent track has no EU/UK restriction (unlike the Full Contact Award).
Submission is through JotForm with up to 20 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 12; results announced end of May 2026.

calls.title: Lobster Club Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: Weeklong summer residency (June 1–8) at Camp Singers in Delhi, New York — 88 acres with restored 1870s lodge. Group show in NYC opening June 10. All disciplines welcome. Simple application: photos of work and a brief about your plans.
calls.summary: Weeklong summer residency at Camp Singers in Delhi, New York — 88 acres with restored 1870s lodge. Group show in NYC.
prose: Lobster Club is a NYC-based artist initiative running a weeklong summer residency at Camp Singers in Delhi, New York — 88 acres in the Catskills with a restored 1870s lodge. The 2026 residency dates are June 1–8.
The residency is multidisciplinary — all disciplines are welcome.
After the residency, the work made culminates in a group show in New York City opening June 10, 2026.

The application is intentionally light: photos of work and a brief about plans for the residency. Submission is through Typeform with 5–10 images. Fee is $25. The 2026 deadline was March 23; results announced early April 2026.

calls.title: REBIRTH — Monart Curates
calls.description: Curated group exhibition in Bermondsey, London (May 14–19, 2026). Open to artists working in painting, photography, installation, textile, and video.
calls.summary: Curated group exhibition in Bermondsey, London. Painting, photography, installation, textile, and video.
prose: Monart Curates is an independent curatorial platform running pop-up exhibitions in London. REBIRTH is a curated group exhibition held in Bermondsey, central London, running May 14–19, 2026.

The exhibition is multidisciplinary: painting, photography, installation, textile, and video are all eligible. The brief is held under the REBIRTH theme but the curatorial register is open across approaches.
Selection is by Monica Mardare, independent curator. Single-curator selection.

Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through CuratorSpace with up to 2 works. Fee is £99 — a higher entry fee that reflects the production cost of the physical pop-up exhibition rather than a competition prize fund.
The 2026 deadline was April 15.

calls.title: Suboart Magazine — May & June 2026 Issues
calls.description: Independent print magazine based in Lisbon seeking emerging visual artists for in-depth interviews, Q&As, and features. Photography, painting, sculpture, textile art, collage, and illustration welcome. Artists receive a free PDF copy.
calls.summary: Independent Lisbon print magazine seeking emerging visual artists for in-depth interviews and features.
prose: Suboart Magazine is an independent print magazine based in Lisbon focused on emerging visual artists. The publication runs in-depth interviews, Q&As, and features rather than thematic group features — selected artists are profiled at length.
Eligibility is open to emerging visual artists 18+ across multiple disciplines: photography, painting, sculpture, textile art, collage, and illustration. AI-generated work is not accepted.
The fee structure is staged: free to submit, with a €30 fee charged only if accepted. Selected artists receive a free PDF copy of the issue.
Submission is by email with up to 6 images. The May & June 2026 issues deadline was April 6; selections announced late April 2026.

calls.title: Field Notes — Aurea Photogallery
calls.description: Exhibition seeking photographs as visual observations — moments collected while moving through the world. Landscapes, street photography, portraits, and everyday details. One-month online exhibition with catalogue and permanent archive.
calls.summary: Photographs as visual observations — moments collected while moving through the world. Online exhibition with catalogue.
prose: Aurea Photogallery is an online photography gallery that runs themed open calls on a recurring schedule. Field Notes is the gallery's call for photographs as visual observations — work made in the act of moving through the world rather than constructed in studio.
The brief is open across genres: landscapes, street photography, portraits, and everyday details all eligible. The unifying register is observational and on-the-go.
Selected work is shown in a one-month online exhibition with a catalogue, then retained in the gallery's permanent archive.

The fee structure is staged: free to submit, with a €30 fee charged only if accepted. Submission is through the gallery's website with up to 3 images. Eligibility is open globally. The 2026 deadline was March 31.

calls.title: The Eden Artists Now Award 2026
calls.description: Unrestricted $3,000 grant plus a four-week residency at The Elizabeth Foundation for the Arts in Midtown Manhattan. Open to visual artists demonstrating outstanding creativity and originality. Independent jury selection.
jury: Carmen Hermo, Curator of Contemporary Art, Museum of Fine Arts Boston
Elena Ketelsen González, Associate Curator, MoMA PS1
calls.summary: Unrestricted $3,000 grant plus four-week residency at The Elizabeth Foundation for the Arts in Manhattan.
prose: The Eden Arts Foundation is a New York-based arts nonprofit. The Eden Artists Now Award is its annual grant for visual artists. The 2026 cycle awards an unrestricted $3,000 grant plus a four-week residency at The Elizabeth Foundation for the Arts in Midtown Manhattan — a working studio environment in the city.
The grant is unrestricted: recipients aren't required to use the funds for a specific project or deliverable.

Selection is by an external jury independent of the foundation's leadership. The 2026 jury is Carmen Hermo (Curator of Contemporary Art, Museum of Fine Arts Boston) and Elena Ketelsen González (Associate Curator, MoMA PS1).
Eligibility is restricted to artists 25 and older. Selection criteria foreground creativity and originality.
Submission is by Google Form with 5–8 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 13; results announced June 15, 2026.

calls.title: Schloss Plüschow Artist-in-Residence 2026
calls.description: Five working scholarships for international visual artists. Three-month residency (October–December 2026) with €1,000/month stipend. On-site stay required at historic Schloss Plüschow in northern Germany.
calls.summary: Three-month residency in northern Germany (Oct-Dec 2026). €1,000/month stipend. Five visual artists selected.
prose: Mecklenburg Artists' House (Mecklenburgisches Künstlerhaus) operates from Schloss Plüschow, a Baroque manor house in the northern German village of Plüschow, near the Baltic coast. The annual artist-in-residence program selects five international visual artists for working scholarships at the Schloss.

The 2026 residency runs three months, October through December, with a €1,000 monthly stipend (€3,000 total). On-site stay is required for the full duration — this is a live-in residency, not a flexible-attendance program.

Eligibility is open to international visual artists across disciplines, photography included. Application requires four PDFs covering the artist's work, project, biography, and concept for the residency period.
Submission is through the Mecklenburgisches Künstlerhaus website. Application fee is €10. The 2026 deadline was May 3; results announced June 2026.

calls.title: Inspired by Classics — Golden Duck Gallery
calls.description: International open call for contemporary art engaging with classical art traditions. Study copies, homages, and modern interpretations welcome. Physical exhibition in Budapest, online exhibition in Vienna and New York. 3 artists exhibit free. €1,000 prize fund.
calls.summary: Contemporary art engaging with classical art traditions. Physical exhibition in Budapest, online in Vienna and New York.
prose: Golden Duck Gallery is a Budapest-based contemporary art gallery. Inspired by Classics is its international open call for contemporary art engaging with classical art traditions — study copies, homages, and modern interpretations of historical works.
Selection structure: a physical exhibition in Budapest plus online exhibitions in Vienna and New York. Three artists exhibit without fee — for the rest, a €100 fee is charged on acceptance.
Total prize fund is €1,000.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is by Google Form with up to 5 images. The fee structure is staged: free to submit. The 2026 deadline was March 29; results announced April 3, 2026.

calls.title: Life Framer — Black & White
calls.description: Monthly photography competition judged by Andrea Modica. All genres welcome, film or digital, new work or from the archive. Winners exhibited at international galleries in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles. $24,000 in total cash prizes across the year.
jury: Andrea Modica, Photographer & Professor of Photography, Drexel University
calls.summary: Monthly competition judged by Andrea Modica. Winners exhibited in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles. $24,000 annual prizes.
prose: Life Framer is a monthly photography competition platform with a rotating thematic schedule. The Black & White edition is the platform's monochrome cycle.

The Black & White juror is Andrea Modica, an American photographer, Guggenheim Fellow and Professor of Photography at Drexel University, celebrated for her intimate platinum contact prints from 8×10 negatives — bringing a perspective rooted in monochrome's expressive possibilities.

Selected winners are featured on Life Framer's site and are eligible for inclusion in the platform's annual physical exhibitions, which travel between partner galleries in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles. Top prize is $2,000; total annual cash prizing across all monthly cycles is $24,000.

AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the Life Framer website with up to 10 images, film or digital, new or from the archive. Fee is tiered $20–$100 by submission scale. This Black & White deadline is September 30, 2026; results announced mid-October 2026.

calls.title: Life Framer — Colors
calls.description: Monthly photography competition judged by Jimmy Marble. All genres welcome. Winners exhibited at international galleries in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles.
calls.summary: Monthly competition judged by Jimmy Marble. Winners exhibited in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles.
prose: Life Framer is a monthly photography competition platform with a rotating thematic schedule. Each month a different juror selects winners and shortlists. The Colors edition is themed around color as subject and structure — work where chromatic register is doing the heavy lifting rather than serving as a backdrop.
The 2026 Colors juror is Jimmy Marble, photographer and creative director whose own work is known for high-saturation editorial sensibility.

Selected winners are featured on Life Framer's site and are eligible for inclusion in the platform's annual physical exhibitions, which travel between partner galleries in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles. Total prize value is $2,000 across categories.

Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+. AI-generated work is not accepted. Submission is through the Life Framer website with up to 10 images. Fee is tiered $20–$100 by submission scale. The 2026 Colors deadline was April 30; results announced mid-May 2026.

calls.title: Life Framer — Portraits
calls.description: Monthly photography competition judged by Robin Hammond. All genres welcome. Winners exhibited at international galleries in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles.
jury: Robin Hammond, National Geographic Explorer & Documentary Photographer
calls.summary: Monthly competition judged by Robin Hammond. Winners exhibited in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles.
prose: Life Framer runs as a monthly themed photography competition with a different juror each round. The "Portraits" call is among the platform's most-entered themes, accepting all approaches to portrait photography — studio, street, environmental, conceptual, intimate. The 2026 cycle of this theme is judged by Robin Hammond, a National Geographic Explorer and documentary photographer whose work focuses on long-form social and human rights stories.

The main prize is $2,000, with additional category awards and inclusion in Life Framer's online archive. Selected work is exhibited at Life Framer's partner galleries in New York, Tokyo, Milan, and Arles — a touring physical presence that runs alongside the online platform.

Entry fees are tiered between $20 and $100 depending on the number of images submitted (up to 10 maximum per applicant). AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 or over.

The Portraits theme deadline is May 31, 2026, with results announced in mid-June. Other Life Framer themes follow on a rolling monthly schedule, each with a different jury and slightly different focus.

calls.title: BBA Photography Prize 2026
calls.description: International photography prize open to all levels and themes. Selected work exhibited at BBA Gallery in Berlin. First prize includes solo exhibition in 2027 and Artsy profile.
jury: Vishal Shah, Managing & Creative Director, BBA Gallery
Renata Kudlacek, Director & Curator, BBA Gallery
Cia Durante, Art Consultant, MA Photography, Royal College of Art
Alexander Jöchl, Director, Samurai Museum Berlin
Hannah Weber-Heidenfels, Fair Manager, Affordable Art Fair Germany
calls.summary: International photography prize. First prize: solo exhibition at BBA Gallery Berlin in 2027 and Artsy profile.
prose: BBA Gallery is a Berlin-based contemporary art gallery. The annual BBA Photography Prize is one of several BBA prizes across photography, painting, and sculpture. The 2026 prize is open to all levels and themes — no thematic restriction, no career-stage filter.

The first-place winner receives €1,000 plus a 2027 solo exhibition at BBA Gallery in Berlin and an Artsy profile — Artsy being the major online art marketplace. Selected work from the broader shortlist is exhibited at BBA Gallery.

The 2026 jury is built from gallery and institutional figures: Vishal Shah (Managing & Creative Director, BBA Gallery), Renata Kudlacek (Director & Curator, BBA Gallery), Cia Durante (art consultant, MA Photography, Royal College of Art), Klaus J.A. Mellenthin (photographer and filmmaker), Alexander Jöchl (Director, Samurai Museum Berlin), Hannah Weber-Heidenfels (Fair Manager, Affordable Art Fair Germany), Isabell Kohls, and Arne Anker.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the BBA Prizes platform with 5 images. Fee is €59. The 2026 deadline was March 30; results announced May 20, 2026.

calls.title: Arty Rat Magazine Open Call
calls.description: Independent art magazine inviting artists and photographers worldwide to submit contemporary visual work. Two artists selected for cover features. One artist receives free participation in group exhibition in Vienna.
calls.summary: Independent art magazine for contemporary visual work. Two cover features and one free group exhibition in Vienna.
prose: Arty Rat is an independent art magazine based in Vienna. The open call invites artists and photographers worldwide to submit contemporary visual work for the magazine.

Selection has multiple tiers: two artists are chosen for cover features, and one artist receives free participation in an Arty Rat group exhibition in Vienna — bypassing the standard exhibition entry fees.
Eligibility is open globally to artists 18+. The fee structure is staged: free to submit, with an €35–€100 fee charged only if accepted for publication.
Submission is by email with up to 6 images. The 2026 deadline was April 1.

calls.title: MSU Zagreb Artist Residency 2026
calls.description: One-month international artist residency (September 20 to October 20, 2026) within the Meeting Point project and L'Internationale's Museum of the Commons programme. Focus on climate crisis, shared resources, and the museum's relationship to local communities. Includes accommodation, €1,500 participation fee, up to €500 travel support, curatorial dialogue, and access to local community networks. Process-oriented, not production-focused.
calls.summary: One-month residency at Museum of Contemporary Art Zagreb. Focus on climate crisis and shared resources. €1,500 fee.
prose: The Museum of Contemporary Art Zagreb (MSU) runs an annual one-month international artist residency. The 2026 residency is part of the Meeting Point project and L'Internationale's Museum of the Commons programme — both pan-European institutional initiatives focused on the contemporary museum's social role.

The 2026 thematic focus: climate crisis, shared resources, and the museum's relationship to local communities. The residency is process-oriented rather than production-focused — outputs are not required to be finished works.

The residency runs September 20 – October 20, 2026 and includes accommodation, a €1,500 participation fee, up to €500 travel support, curatorial dialogue, and access to local community networks in Zagreb.
Eligibility is open. Submission is through Google Form with a portfolio. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 1; results announced April 15, 2026.

calls.title: Louvre Unbound Magazine — Volume 6 Open Call
calls.description: International contemporary art magazine seeking visual artists worldwide. Painting, photography, sculpture, digital art, mixed media, and more. Submit up to 6 artworks for consideration. Selected artists are featured in print and promoted across social media.
calls.summary: International contemporary art magazine. Submit up to 6 artworks. Featured in print and promoted across social media.
prose: Louvre Unbound is an international contemporary art magazine. Volume 6 is the magazine's call for submissions across visual disciplines: painting, photography, sculpture, digital art, mixed media, and more. The publication runs as a multidisciplinary print survey rather than a category-restricted journal.

Selected artists are featured in the printed magazine and promoted across the publication's social media channels. The fee structure is staged: free to submit, with a tiered $39–$139 fee charged only if work is accepted for publication.
Eligibility is open to artists 18+ globally. Submission is through Google Form with up to 6 artworks. The 2026 deadline was April 15.

calls.title: Musée du quai Branly Photography Award 2026
calls.org: Musée du quai Branly – Jacques Chirac
calls.description: Annual grant supporting non-European artists to create original photographic works for the museum's permanent collection. Three selected artists each receive €30,000 plus production support and travel to Paris.
calls.summary: Grant for non-European artists to create photographic works for the museum's permanent collection. €30,000 each.
prose: The Musée du quai Branly – Jacques Chirac is the major Paris museum dedicated to non-Western art and ethnography, located on the Seine. The annual Photography Award is the museum's commission program for original photographic works to enter its permanent collection.

Eligibility is restricted: open only to non-European artists. The structural premise inverts the usual flow — rather than European institutions collecting work from elsewhere, this program funds non-European photographers specifically.
Three artists are selected each cycle. Each receives €30,000 plus production support and travel to Paris.
The work made under the grant enters the museum's permanent collection — an acquisition rather than a fee.
Submission is through Picter with a project proposal. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 15; results announced July 30, 2026.

calls.title: Photographers Without Borders Revolutionary Storyteller Grant
calls.description: Three recipients worldwide receive $5,000 USD each for impact-driven photography projects focused on environment, land/water protection, decolonized conservation, queer ecology, and climate change.
calls.summary: Three $5,000 grants for impact-driven photography projects focused on environment and climate change.
prose: Photographers Without Borders (PWB) is an international nonprofit supporting impact-driven photography. The Revolutionary Storyteller Grant is the organization's annual grant program for projects with explicit environmental and social-justice framings.

The brief is thematically specific: projects focused on environment, land/water protection, decolonized conservation, queer ecology, and climate change. The framing is rooted in non-extractive, community-rooted approaches rather than traditional photojournalism.
Three recipients worldwide receive $5,000 USD each plus Adobe Creative Cloud subscription.
Selection is by photographers Eman Mohammed, Sophia Nasif, and Natalia Ortiz Mantilla.
Eligibility requires PWB membership. Submission is through the PWB website with up to 12 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 30.

calls.title: 10. Merck-Preis der Darmstädter Tage der Fotografie
calls.description: Festival seeking projects exploring 'unstable presence' through direct contact with reality. Finalists receive €500 production budget, travel reimbursement, and hotel accommodation.
calls.summary: Festival seeking projects exploring 'unstable presence' through direct contact with reality.
prose: Darmstädter Tage der Fotografie (Darmstadt Days of Photography) is a German photography festival held in Darmstadt. The Merck-Preis is the festival's main prize, sponsored by the pharmaceutical company Merck, which is headquartered in Darmstadt. The 2026 edition is the prize's 10th cycle.

The brief is conceptually specific: projects exploring 'unstable presence' through direct contact with reality. The framing favors documentary approaches that engage with the world rather than constructed or studio work.

Selection is by Robin Hinsch (photographer and professor), Sara-Lena Maierhofer (photographer and professor), Ute Noll (curator), Marcel Rauschkolb (curator), Kris Scholz (professor), and Gregor Schuster (photographer).
Finalists receive €500 production budget, travel reimbursement, and hotel accommodation during the festival.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through PhMuseum with up to 12 images. Fee is €25. The 2026 deadline was March 15; results announced April 20, 2026.

calls.title: On the Block - Street & Urban Photography
calls.description: Celebrates street and urban photography. Seeking unposed, unfiltered moments revealing quiet truths and vivid stories.
jury: Paris Chong, Gallery Director, Leica Gallery Los Angeles
calls.summary: Celebrating unposed, unfiltered street moments revealing quiet truths and vivid stories of urban life.
prose: On the Block is the Lucie Foundation's open call for street and urban photography. The Lucie Foundation runs the Lucie Awards, the International Photography Awards, and a wider program of grants and exhibitions. The 2026 edition is the second cycle of On the Block.

The brief is specific: unposed, unfiltered street and urban photography. The selection priority is moments revealing quiet truths and vivid stories — observational rather than constructed work. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Top prize is $1,000 plus inclusion in the exhibition.

The 2026 jury is Paris Chong (Gallery Director, Leica Gallery Los Angeles), Lynn Johnson (photojournalist and educator), Arturo Soto (photographer, writer, and educator), and Matt Stuart (Magnum-affiliated street photographer).
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the Lucie Foundation website, single image per entry. Fee is $20. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced April 2026.

calls.title: Temporary Storage
calls.description: Online photo-based exhibition exploring duration, process, and time as material. Open to photographers using photo-based practices.
calls.summary: Online photo-based exhibition exploring duration, process, and time as material.
prose: Container Media is an indie curatorial platform. The Temporary Storage open call is for photo-based work exploring duration, process, and time as material — work that engages with photography's relationship to time rather than the photograph as a single moment.
The brief is open to photographers using photo-based practices broadly. AI-generated work is accepted.
Selected work is shown in an online photo-based exhibition.
Submission is by email with unlimited images. Application is free. Eligibility is open globally. The 2026 deadline was March 15.

calls.title: Photo Laureate 2026
calls.description: Select one photographer to document Tampa Bay for one year. Winner receives solo exhibition at Florida Museum of Photographic Arts.
calls.summary: One photographer selected to document Tampa Bay for one year. Solo exhibition at Florida Museum of Photographic Arts.
prose: Photo Laureate is the annual program from Saint Petersburg Month of Photography (SPMoP) in Florida. The structural premise: one photographer is selected to document the Tampa Bay region across an entire year — a sustained, place-based commission rather than a single-image prize.
The selected Photo Laureate produces a body of work over the year that culminates in a solo exhibition at the Florida Museum of Photographic Arts (FMoPA) in Tampa.
Eligibility is restricted to US-based photographers. Application is free, submitted through the SPMoP website. The 2026 deadline was March 17; results announced May 2026.

calls.title: Solo Exhibition April 2026
calls.description: Monthly featured photographer showcase with global audience visibility. April 1-30, 2026 in La Jolla, CA.
jury: Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, Founder & Editor, All About Photo
calls.summary: Monthly featured photographer showcase with global audience visibility. April 2026 in La Jolla, CA.
prose: All About Photo runs a recurring Solo Exhibition program — a monthly featured photographer slot. The April 2026 cycle selects one photographer for a full-month online solo exhibition running April 1–30, 2026.

What's offered: a permanent gallery presence on the All About Photo platform, an exclusive interview, social media promotion, newsletter feature, international press coverage, and commission-free sales.
Selection is by Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, photographer and founder of All About Photo. Single-juror selection.

Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the All About Photo website with a cohesive project of 6–14 images. Fee is $45. The April 2026 cycle deadline was March 20; selection announced April 1, 2026.

calls.title: Discovery Art Fair Cologne - Art Fair Spot
calls.description: Get an exclusive art fair spot at the Discovery Art Fair in Cologne at the New & Abstract booth. Open to abstract and contemporary artists.
calls.summary: Exclusive art fair spot at Discovery Art Fair Cologne at the New & Abstract booth. Abstract and contemporary art.
prose: New & Abstract Gallery is a Berlin-based gallery focused on abstract and contemporary art. The 2026 open call selects artists for an exclusive art fair spot at the Discovery Art Fair Cologne — work shown at the gallery's booth during the fair rather than as a stand-alone presence.
Eligibility is restricted to abstract and contemporary artists.
Submission is through the gallery's website. Fee is €20. The 2026 deadline was March 18; results announced March 27, 2026.

calls.title: Seeing America
calls.description: Celebrating 250th Anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. Exhibition during Photography Month Sacramento.
calls.summary: Celebrating 250th Anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. Exhibition during Photography Month Sacramento.
prose: Viewpoint Photographic Art Center is a Sacramento, California photography gallery. The 2026 Seeing America exhibition is timed to the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence — the brief asks photographers to interpret America as it stands now, two and a half centuries on.
The exhibition runs during Photography Month Sacramento, the city's annual photography programming.
Selection is by Eric Lindberg, adventure travel photographer. Top prize is $400.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through EntryThingy with up to 4 images. Fee is tiered $30–$50. The 2026 deadline was March 18; results announced March 23, 2026.

calls.title: Organ Vida 14 - Happy Spiraling
calls.description: Open to photographers and visual artists. Winners receive €300 artist fee, mentorship, exhibition at Museum of Contemporary Art Zagreb (June 2026), with travel and accommodation covered.
calls.summary: Exhibition at Museum of Contemporary Art Zagreb. €300 artist fee, mentorship, travel and accommodation covered.
prose: Organ Vida is a Croatian photography festival held annually in Zagreb. The 2026 edition is the festival's 14th cycle, themed Happy Spiraling.
Selected photographers receive a €300 artist fee, mentorship, and exhibition at the Museum of Contemporary Art Zagreb (MSU) in June 2026. Travel and accommodation for selected artists are covered.
Eligibility is open to photographers and visual artists globally. Submission is through Picter with up to 25 images. Fee is €35. The 2026 deadline was March 18; results announced mid-April 2026.

calls.title: Innovate Grants - Winter $1,800 Grants
calls.description: Two $1,800 quarterly grants for visual artists and photographers. Twelve honorable mentions also featured.
calls.summary: Two $1,800 quarterly grants for visual artists and photographers. Twelve honorable mentions also featured.
prose: Innovate Artist Grants runs a recurring quarterly grant program for visual artists and photographers. Each cycle awards two $1,800 grants. The Winter 2026 cycle is one of four cycles per year — applicants who miss one cycle can apply to the next.
Twelve honorable mentions are also featured on the Innovate platform alongside the two main grantees.
Eligibility is open globally to visual artists and photographers. Submission is through Paperform. Fee is $35. The Winter 2026 deadline was March 19.

calls.title: Call for Artists 2026
calls.description: Building internationally acclaimed collection. Eight new locations available for diverse media including sculpture, wall-mounted art, and technology-based works.
calls.summary: Building internationally acclaimed collection at Tampa International Airport. Eight new locations available.
prose: Tampa International Airport runs an active art collection program. The 2026 Call for Artists is for permanent commissions across eight new locations within the airport's terminals — diverse media including sculpture, wall-mounted art, and technology-based works.
The commission scale is unusually high: individual commissions range from $200,000 to $1.2 million, depending on the location and scope of the work.
Eligibility is restricted to professional artists. Selected work enters the airport's permanent public collection, seen by millions of travelers annually.
Submission is through CaFÉ with up to 10 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 19; results announced June 2026.

calls.title: Dek Unu Magazine - Monthly Artist Feature
calls.description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist monthly in print and online. Easy email submissions process.
calls.summary: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist monthly in print and online.
prose: Dek Unu Magazine is an international not-for-profit photography journal that publishes monthly. The structural premise is unusual: each issue features one accomplished artist rather than a multi-photographer group format. Issues are published as both print and online paperback.

Eligibility is open across all fine art photography genres and techniques. Selection criteria pair technical excellence with artistic vision and conceptual intent — the magazine is looking for resolved, mature bodies of work. The Monthly Artist Feature is the magazine's rolling submission stream — applications can be made at any time, with editorial review on a continuing basis.
Submission is by email with 11 images. Application is free. Eligibility is open globally.

calls.title: this place is strange
calls.description: Virtual exhibition seeking the weird underbelly of place — folklore, rust belt decay, uncanny moments. Artists worldwide welcome.
jury: Morgan Laurens, Arts writer & Founder, Goblin Market
calls.summary: Virtual exhibition seeking the weird underbelly of place — folklore, rust belt decay, uncanny moments.
prose: midwest nice art is a curatorial platform running themed virtual exhibitions. this place is strange is the platform's open call for the weird underbelly of place — folklore, rust belt decay, uncanny moments. The brief asks for the off-key, ambient strangeness of specific places rather than picturesque or generic landscapes.
Selection is by Morgan Laurens, arts writer and founder of Goblin Market.
Selected work is shown in a virtual exhibition. Eligibility is open to artists worldwide.
Submission is by Google Form with up to 3 images. Fee is $5. The 2026 deadline was March 20; results announced March 27, 2026.

calls.title: The Narrative
calls.description: International open call welcoming all forms of two-dimensional images, traditional and non-conventional media, and alternative photographic processes. Exhibition May 1 - June 1, 2026.
calls.summary: International open call for all forms of two-dimensional images, traditional and non-conventional media.
prose: The Narrative is an international juried call from TCG Gallery (also operating as Château Gallery), open to all forms of two-dimensional image-making — traditional photography alongside non-conventional media and alternative photographic processes. The brief uses narrative as a connective theme rather than a strict subject restriction.
Selected work is shown in an online exhibition running May 1 – June 1, 2026. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Eligibility is open globally to artists 18+. Submission is through the gallery's website with up to 3 images. Fee is $15.
The 2026 deadline was April 20; results announced April 27, 2026.

calls.title: Bourse Laurent Troude 2026
calls.description: 8th edition of the photojournalism grant supporting photographers under 30 with a project on French territory. Subjects: political, cultural, social, or sports themes in a proximity photojournalism format. Prize: €8,000 from La SAIF and Libération, one-year Divergence Images subscription, exhibition/projection in spring 2027, and publication in Libération. Submit via WeTransfer.
calls.summary: Photojournalism grant for photographers under 30 with a project on French territory. €8,000 prize.
prose: Bourse Laurent Troude is a French photojournalism grant named after Laurent Troude, the Libération photographer. The 2026 edition is the grant's 8th cycle.

Eligibility is restricted to photographers under 30 with a proposed project on French territory. Subject matter is open across categories: political, cultural, social, or sports themes — but the methodological frame is specific: proximity photojournalism (a French tradition of close-engagement, on-the-ground reporting).
Prize package: €8,000 from La SAIF and Libération, a one-year Divergence Images subscription, exhibition/projection in spring 2027, and publication in Libération. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Submission is by email plus WeTransfer with 5–10 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 20; results announced April 2026.

calls.title: Multi-Exposed
calls.description: Explores time overlaps and memory through photography. Exhibition: April 18 - May 16, 2026 in Minneapolis, MN.
calls.summary: Exploring time overlaps and memory through photography. Exhibition in Minneapolis, MN.
prose: Praxis Photo Arts Center is a Minneapolis nonprofit gallery for fine art photography. Multi-Exposed is one of its themed juried exhibitions — focused on photography that engages with time overlaps and memory: multiple exposures (in-camera or in post), composite imagery, layered processes, and other approaches that visualize time as compounded.
Selected work is shown in a physical exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis, April 18 – May 16, 2026.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through Smarter Entry with up to 10 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 22; results announced April 7, 2026.

calls.title: Linkshouse Residency — Pier Arts Centre Orkney
calls.description: Month-long funded residency at Linkshouse in Birsay, Orkney, May 1–31, 2026. Partnership with Wilhelmina Barns-Graham Trust and Pier Arts Centre. Includes accommodation, £2,200 stipend, and travel bursary up to £250. On-site artist support and opportunity for future exhibitions with VAS. VAS membership required.
calls.summary: Month-long funded residency in Birsay, Orkney. Includes accommodation, £2,200 stipend, and travel bursary.
prose: The Linkshouse Residency is a month-long funded residency at Linkshouse in Birsay, on Orkney's west mainland — a small village by the Atlantic. The residency runs May 1–31, 2026 as a partnership between Visual Arts Scotland (VAS), the Wilhelmina Barns-Graham Trust, and the Pier Arts Centre (the Stromness contemporary art center).

The package includes accommodation at Linkshouse, a £2,200 stipend, and a travel bursary up to £250. On-site artist support is provided during the residency, with the opportunity to develop future exhibitions with VAS.
Eligibility requires VAS membership. Submission is by email with a single PDF containing 6 images. Application is free.
The 2026 deadline was March 15; results announced end of March 2026.

calls.title: Premio Mila 2026
calls.description: Supporting Italian or Italy-based artists under 40. Five finalists exhibited in Milan; winner receives €3,000 acquisition prize with work entering permanent collection.
jury: Andrea Elia Zanini, Curator, Fondo Malerba
Bernardo Follini, Curator, Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo
calls.summary: Supporting Italian or Italy-based artists under 40. Winner receives €3,000 acquisition prize for permanent collection.
prose: Premio Mila is the annual prize organized by Fondo Malerba (Malerba Fund), supporting Italian or Italy-based photographers and visual artists under 40. The structural premise is acquisition: the winner's work enters Malerba Fund's permanent collection.
Selection structure: five finalists are exhibited in Milan. From the five, one winner receives a €3,000 acquisition prize.

The 2026 jury draws from Italian curatorial institutions: Andrea Elia Zanini (Curator, Fondo Malerba), Caterina Angelucci (curator and journalist), Matteo Balduzzi (Curator, MUFOCO — the Museum of Contemporary Photography in Cinisello Balsamo), Marta Cereda (Artistic Director, Careof), Bernardo Follini (Curator, Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo), and Francesca Lazzarini (independent curator).

Eligibility is restricted to Italian or Italy-based artists under 40. Submission is by email plus WeTransfer with up to 15 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 22; results announced late April 2026.

calls.title: Foto Tallinn 2026 Art Fair
calls.description: Estonia's only international art fair dedicated to contemporary photography. September 18-20, 2026 at Kai Art Centre in Tallinn.
calls.summary: Estonia's only international art fair dedicated to contemporary photography. At Kai Art Centre in Tallinn.
prose: Foto Tallinn is Estonia's only international art fair dedicated to contemporary photography. The 2026 fair runs September 18–20 at Kai Art Centre in Tallinn — the contemporary art venue in the Noblessner harbor district.

The 2026 selection panel is built from international curators and gallerists: Anna Tellgren (curator), Jeppe Ugelvig (curator and writer), Margot Samel (gallerist), Sara Giuliattini (curator), and Lilian Hiob-Küttis (curator).
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the fair's website with at least 5 images. Fee is tiered €150–€250. The 2026 deadline was March 23; results announced late spring 2026.

calls.title: Whimsical
calls.description: Seeking work that surprises, delights, and transports viewers through playful storytelling, surreal elements, and unexpected juxtapositions.
calls.summary: Seeking work that surprises and delights through playful storytelling, surreal elements, and unexpected juxtapositions.
prose: A Photographer's Place is a Raleigh, North Carolina photography gallery and creative space. Whimsical is one of its themed juried exhibitions. The brief asks for work that surprises, delights, and transports viewers through playful storytelling, surreal elements, and unexpected juxtapositions — humor and strangeness as primary register.
Selection is by Stephen Fletcher.
Selected work is shown at A Photographer's Place in Raleigh.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through Smarter Entry with up to 5 images. Fee is $35. The 2026 deadline was March 24; results announced March 25, 2026.

calls.title: 10x10 Photobooks Research Grants Cycle 5
calls.description: Three $2,500 grants supporting research on photobooks from Africa and its diaspora.
jury: Amy Sall, Founding Editor, SUNU Journal
Diane Frankel, Chair, George Rickey Foundation
Mariama Attah, Curator, National Museums Liverpool
calls.summary: Three $2,500 grants supporting research on photobooks from Africa and its diaspora.
prose: 10x10 Photobooks is a US-based nonprofit dedicated to photobook scholarship, exhibitions, and publications. The Research Grants are the organization's annual program supporting photobook research projects. The 2026 cycle is the 5th edition, focused specifically on photobooks from Africa and its diaspora.
Three $2,500 grants are awarded each cycle. The grants fund research toward exhibitions, publications, or critical writing — not photobook production itself, but study of the photobook as a form.

Selection is by Amy Sall (Founding Editor, SUNU Journal), Diane Frankel (Chair, George Rickey Foundation), Mariama Attah (Curator, National Museums Liverpool), and Marjorie Ornston (Grants Director, 10x10 Photobooks).

Eligibility is open globally to applicants whose research engages with the cycle's geographic focus. Submission is by Google Form with a project proposal. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 23; results announced May 2026.

calls.title: Fast Forward: Analog Photography as a Third Space
calls.description: Analog-only submissions exploring how photography creates space for camaraderie and interaction. Darkroom prints and experimental work welcome.
jury: Rotem Rozental, Executive Director & Chief Curator, LACP
calls.summary: Analog-only submissions exploring how photography creates space for camaraderie and interaction.
prose: Fast Forward: Analog Photography as a Third Space is an exhibition open call from Los Angeles Center of Photography (LACP). The brief frames photography itself as a third space — a social and physical environment for camaraderie and interaction, alongside its function as image production.
The call is process-restricted: analog-only submissions. Darkroom prints and experimental work welcome. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Selection is by Aline Smithson (Founder & Editor, Lenscratch) and Rotem Rozental (Executive Director & Chief Curator, LACP).

Eligibility is restricted to analog photography work. Submission is through Submittable with up to 35 images. Fee is tiered $25–$200 by submission scale. The 2026 deadline was March 24; results announced March 27, 2026.

calls.title: The Magic of Light - Photography Open Call
calls.description: Film, digital, and alternative process photography including hybrid approaches. Exhibited in Los Angeles, CA.
jury: Ann M. Jastrab, Executive Director, Center for Photographic Art
calls.summary: Film, digital, and alternative process photography including hybrid approaches. Exhibition in Los Angeles.
prose: Art/Space 114 is a Los Angeles photography venue. The Magic of Light is one of its juried open calls — open to film, digital, and alternative process photography, including hybrid approaches.
AI-generated work is not accepted.
Selection structure: cash prizes plus a solo exhibition for the top winner. First $500, second $250, third $100. The first-place winner also receives a solo exhibition slot.
Selection is by Ann M. Jastrab, Executive Director of the Center for Photographic Art (Carmel-by-the-Sea, California).
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through EntryThingy with up to 15 images. Fee is $45. The 2026 deadline was March 28; results announced April 4, 2026.

calls.title: The Human Portrait
calls.description: Global online exhibit honoring portraiture in all its forms — documentary, fine art, street, conceptual, experimental, self-portraiture, and beyond. Seeking portraits that convey presence, emotion, tension, or quiet recognition. $20 for first image, $5 each additional, up to 20 images total. No AI-generated imagery.
calls.summary: Global online exhibit honoring portraiture in all forms — documentary, fine art, street, conceptual, and experimental.
prose: Photo Artfolio is an online photography platform that runs themed juried calls. The Human Portrait is the platform's portrait-themed cycle — open to portraiture in all its forms: documentary, fine art, street, conceptual, experimental, self-portraiture.
The brief looks for portraits that convey presence, emotion, tension, or quiet recognition. AI-generated imagery is not accepted.
Cash prizing: $500 (first), $350 (second), $150 (third). Selected work is shown in a global online exhibit.

Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the platform's website with up to 20 images. The fee is $20 for the first image, $5 each additional. The 2026 deadline was March 25; results announced April 15, 2026.

calls.title: BOTANICAL Photography Exhibit
calls.description: Beyond documentation — seeking character in a leaf, architecture in a seedpod. All styles and processes welcome. Santa Fe, NM.
jury: Holly Hart, Fine Art Photographer & Founder, Dusk Gallery
calls.summary: Beyond documentation — seeking character in a leaf, architecture in a seedpod. All styles welcome. Santa Fe, NM.
prose: Dusk Gallery is a Santa Fe, New Mexico photography gallery founded by fine art photographer Holly Hart, who also juries the gallery's calls. BOTANICAL is the gallery's call for plant-life photography that moves beyond pure documentation.
The brief is specific: character in a leaf, architecture in a seedpod, the formal qualities of plants seen as compositional subjects rather than botanical specimens. All styles and processes welcome.
Selection is by Holly Hart.
Selected work is shown in a physical exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the gallery's website with 5 or 10 images. Fee is $40–$45. The 2026 deadline was March 26; results announced April 9, 2026.

calls.title: Photographic Exploration Project: ENTANGLEMENT
calls.description: Explores intricate webs of connections from intimate relationships to global systems. Group exhibition at Loop Raum in Berlin, July 2026.
jury: Rüdiger Lange, Artistic Director, Loop – Raum für aktuelle Kunst
calls.summary: Exploring intricate webs of connections from intimate relationships to global systems. Group exhibition in Berlin.
prose: Photographic Exploration Project (PEP) is a Berlin-based photography platform founded by Bénédicte Blondeau. The 2026 themed open call ENTANGLEMENT asks photographers to engage with the intricate webs of connections that hold things together — from intimate relationships through ecological systems to global networks.
Selection is by Rüdiger Lange (Artistic Director, Loop – Raum für aktuelle Kunst, the Berlin contemporary art space) and Bénédicte Blondeau (PEP Founder & Curator).
Selected work is shown in a group exhibition at Loop Raum in Berlin in July 2026.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through JotForm with 1–10 images. Fee is tiered €5–€15 by submission scale. The 2026 deadline was March 31; exhibition opens July 2026.

calls.title: Portfolio 2026
calls.description: Juried exhibition featuring cohesive bodies of work. Juror: Natasha Egan (MoCP). Winner eligible for $4,000 High Museum purchase award.
jury: Natasha Egan, Executive Director, Museum of Contemporary Photography
calls.summary: Juried exhibition for cohesive bodies of work. Juror: Natasha Egan (MoCP). Winner eligible for $4,000 purchase award.
prose: Atlanta Photography Group (APG) is a nonprofit photography membership organization in Atlanta, Georgia. Portfolio 2026 is the organization's juried exhibition focused on cohesive bodies of work — full portfolios rather than single-image group shows.
Selection is by Natasha Egan, Executive Director of the Museum of Contemporary Photography (MoCP) in Chicago.

The award structure has two tiers. Selected portfolios are exhibited at APG. Beyond that, the winning portfolio is eligible for a $4,000 High Museum purchase award — the work itself is acquired into the High Museum of Art's collection.
Eligibility requires APG membership. Submission is by Dropbox with 10 or 20 images. Fee is tiered $75–$105. The 2026 deadline was March 27; results announced April 5, 2026.

calls.title: COLOR Photography Exhibit
calls.description: Exploring color as one of the most powerful storytelling tools. Bold, subtle, vibrant, or muted approaches welcome. Tucson, AZ.
calls.summary: Exploring color as one of the most powerful storytelling tools. Bold, subtle, vibrant, or muted. Tucson, AZ.
prose: Decode Gallery is a Tucson, Arizona photography gallery founded by conceptual fine art photographer Holly Hart, who also juries the gallery's open calls. COLOR is the gallery's call for work where color functions as a primary storytelling tool — bold, subtle, vibrant, or muted approaches all eligible.
Selection is by Holly Hart.

Selected work is shown in a physical exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson. The gallery's production model: gallery covers professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality framing, and custom matting for selected work.

Eligibility is open worldwide to all skill levels. Submission is through the gallery's website with 5 or 10 images. Fee is $40–$45. The 2026 deadline was March 28; results announced approximately April 11, 2026.

calls.title: Contemporary Trends in Beauty
calls.description: Handcrafted prints using alternative photographic processes. No AI-generated images; final print must be handmade. Juried by Diana H. Bloomfield and Christina Z. Anderson.
jury: Christina Z. Anderson, Alternative Processes Artist
calls.summary: Handcrafted prints using alternative photographic processes. Final print must be handmade. No AI-generated images.
prose: Contemporary Trends in Beauty: Alternative Processes is a juried call from L.A. Photo Curator (the platform run by Laurie Freitag), with co-curation by alternative process specialists. The brief is doubly restricted: handcrafted prints made through alternative photographic processes, and the final print must be handmade — not just a digital reproduction of an alt-process image.
AI-generated images are not accepted.
Selection is by Diana H. Bloomfield (visual storyteller) and Christina Z. Anderson (alternative processes artist) — both deeply rooted in the alt-process community.
Eligibility is restricted to alternative process work. Submission is by email in groups of 3 or 6 images. Fee is $25. The 2026 deadline was March 29.

calls.title: Centrale Festival Open Call 2026
calls.description: Seeking 16 artists under 30 specializing in photography and video art for exhibition in Fano, Italy (June 12-27, 2026). Festival manages curation and setup.
jury: Claudia Bigongiari, Managing Editor, Pellicola Magazine
calls.summary: Seeking 16 artists under 30 in photography and video art. Exhibition in Fano, Italy, June 2026.
prose: Centrale Festival is held annually in Fano, on the Adriatic coast in central Italy. The 2026 open call selects 16 artists under 30 specializing in photography and video art. The exhibition runs June 12–27, 2026.
The festival manages all curation and setup — selected artists provide the work; the festival handles its display.
Selection is by Claudia Bigongiari (Managing Editor, Pellicola Magazine), Lori Lako (visual artist), and Sara Poli (Director, Forno Project).
Eligibility is restricted to artists under 30. Submission is by email. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 29; results announced May 4, 2026.

calls.title: Abstract Visions
calls.description: Invites abstraction as a way of seeing, sensing, and surviving. Welcomes projects communicating through atmosphere, rhythm, colour, and form. Amsterdam.
calls.summary: Abstraction as a way of seeing, sensing, and surviving. Projects communicating through atmosphere, rhythm, and form.
prose: Artdoc Photography Magazine is the Amsterdam-based contemporary photography magazine. The Abstract Visions open call invites work that uses abstraction as a way of seeing, sensing, and surviving — abstraction as method rather than just style.

The brief favors projects communicating through atmosphere, rhythm, colour, and form rather than narrative or representation. The selection is interested in non-representational and process-driven work.
Selected work is featured in Artdoc Magazine. Eligibility requires Artdoc membership.
Submission is through the Artdoc website. Application is free for members. The 2026 deadline was March 30.

calls.title: The Process Room - Open Call for Workshops & Artworks
calls.description: Open call for workshops and artworks exploring alternative photographic processes. Presented in collaboration with Photobook Cafe.
calls.summary: Workshops and artworks exploring alternative photographic processes. With Photobook Cafe.
prose: Alternative Processes is a London-based platform focused on alternative photographic processes — cyanotype, salt prints, gum bichromate, lumen, photogram, wet plate, and other historical or non-standard techniques. The Process Room is an open call presented in collaboration with Photobook Cafe.

The call has a dual structure: it accepts both workshop proposals (for artists who teach alternative processes) and finished artworks (for artists who use them). Selected workshops run as part of The Process Room programming; selected artworks are exhibited.
Eligibility is open. Submission is through Google Form. Fee is pay-what-you-can. The 2026 deadline was March 31.

calls.title: Mini Artist Grant for Emerging & Mid-Career Artists
calls.description: Artist grant for emerging and mid-career artists working with found photography and alternative processes.
calls.summary: Grant for emerging and mid-career artists working with found photography and alternative processes.
prose: The Mini Artist Grant is a small recurring grant from Photo Trouvée Magazine, the platform focused on found and family photographs as artistic source material. The grant is restricted by practice area: artists working with found photography and alternative processes.

The award is $350 plus publication on the Photo Trouvée platform. The size is intentional — a mini grant that can fund a specific small expense (a printing run, a roll of film, a small material cost) rather than a major project.
Eligibility is open to emerging and mid-career artists. Submission is through JotForm with up to 5 images. Fee is $10. The 2026 deadline was March 31.

calls.title: Colour Calendar Event
calls.description: Annual event inviting artists to introduce colour into monochrome alternative processes — cyanotype, chemigram, anthotype, and more.
calls.summary: Annual event inviting artists to introduce colour into monochrome alternative processes — cyanotype, chemigram, anthotype.
prose: AlternativePhotography.com runs an annual Colour Calendar Event inviting artists to introduce colour into traditionally monochrome alternative processes. Eligible techniques include cyanotype, chemigram, anthotype, and others where color is normally restricted by chemistry.
The brief asks artists to push the chemistry — multi-toning cyanotypes, hand-coloring, layering processes, or building color into traditionally one-tone outputs.
AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility is restricted to alternative process work and requires AlternativePhotography.com membership.
Selection results in inclusion in the platform's published calendar. Submission is by email, single image. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 31.

calls.title: FotoSlovo Award 2026
calls.description: International competition across all genres. Prizes: €2,000 cash, iPhone, Limassol Biennale participation, exhibitions in Bucharest and Frejus, magazine feature, festival projections, free book production.
jury: Ali Besikci, Photographer & Founder of ZONE
Madara Ulme, Artistic Director, SNAP Collective
calls.summary: International competition. Prizes: €2,000 cash, exhibitions, Limassol Biennale, magazine feature, book production.
prose: FotoSlovo is a Bucharest-based photography platform founded by Laza Anna. The annual FotoSlovo Award is the platform's international competition, open across all photography genres. The 2026 prize package is unusually layered.

Top prize is €2,000 cash plus an iPhone, participation in the Limassol Biennale, exhibitions in Bucharest and Frejus, magazine feature, festival projections, and free book production. Each component reaches a different audience — the prize is a network of opportunities rather than a single payout.

The 2026 jury is built from international photography institutions and past winners: Whitney Cole (Director, Candela Gallery), Ali Besikci (photographer and founder of ZONE), Madara Ulme (Artistic Director, SNAP Collective), Souhayl A (FotoSlovo Awards 2024 winner), Arnis Balcus (Editor-in-Chief, FK Magazine), and Laza Anna (FotoSlovo Founder). AI-generated work is accommodated through a dedicated category.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the FotoSlovo website with 1–15 images. Fee is tiered €9–€42 by submission scale. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced May 2026.

calls.title: Ephemere Photobook Grant 2026
calls.description: Selected artist receives 100% production coverage for an eco-conscious monograph published in Japan, global distribution, and round-trip airfare to Tokyo for launch at Ephemere Photo Fest (October 2026).
calls.summary: 100% production coverage for an eco-conscious monograph published in Japan. Airfare to Tokyo for launch included.
prose: Ephemere is a Tokyo-based photography publisher and the organizer of Ephemere Photo Fest. The annual Photobook Grant funds production of one selected artist's photo monograph published in Japan.

The grant is unusually comprehensive: 100% production coverage for an eco-conscious monograph (printed on sustainable materials), global distribution, plus round-trip airfare to Tokyo for the book launch at Ephemere Photo Fest in October 2026.
Selection is by Anne Murayama (Curator and Director, Ephemere) and Jordan Reyes (Creative Partner, Ephemere).
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through Google Form with a book dummy. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced May 2026.

calls.title: 2026 Street Photo Award
calls.description: Monthly street photography competition. Submit candid moments from packed corners to stark geometry. Winner receives $1,000, exhibition at PBC Gallery London, and feature. Total prize pool $2,700. Judge: Gulnara Samoilova.
calls.summary: Monthly street photography competition. $1,000 winner prize, PBC Gallery London exhibition. $2,700 total pool.
prose: The Independent Photographer is a London photography platform that runs monthly themed competitions. The 2026 Street Photo Award is the platform's street-themed cycle.
The brief calls for candid moments: from packed corners to stark geometry. Subject is open inside the genre.

Top prize is $1,000 plus exhibition at PBC Gallery in London plus a feature on The Independent Photographer platform. Total prize pool is $2,700 across category placements. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Selection is by Gulnara Samoilova, photographer.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the platform's website with 1, 3, or 6 images. Fee is tiered $15–$40 by submission scale. The 2026 deadline was March 31.

calls.title: A Stranger's Face: Travel Portraits (KLPA)
calls.description: 18th edition seeking travel portraits of strangers. Forty shortlisted photographers featured in Malaysian exhibition (September 2026) and international partner festivals. Prizes: €2,000/€1,000/€500.
jury: Aisha Nazar, Picture Editor, National Geographic Traveller UK
calls.summary: 18th edition seeking travel portraits of strangers. Featured in Malaysian exhibition and international partner festivals.
prose: Kuala Lumpur Photo Awards (KLPA) is an annual photography prize from Malaysia. The 2026 edition is the award's 18th cycle. The 2026 brief is A Stranger's Face: Travel Portraits — work where the photographer encounters a stranger while traveling and the resulting portrait is the subject.
AI-generated work is not accepted.

Selection structure: forty shortlisted photographers are featured in a Malaysian exhibition (September 2026) and at international partner festivals. Cash prizes are €2,000 (first), €1,000 (second), €500 (third).

The 2026 jury is Aisha Nazar (Picture Editor, National Geographic Traveller UK), Michelle Sank (documentary photographer), Ivan Gabriel (curator and arts practitioner), Ng Hui Hsien (artist and curator), and She Escobar (photographer).
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through Picter with up to 10 images. Fee is tiered €15–€65 by submission scale. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced July 15, 2026.

calls.title: AAP Magazine #56 Shadows
calls.description: Mastering shadows in photography. Winners receive $1,000 cash, publication in AAP Magazine #56, and global recognition.
jury: Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, Founder & Editor, All About Photo
calls.summary: Mastering shadows in photography. $1,000 cash prize, publication, and global recognition.
prose: All About Photo Magazine (AAP Magazine) runs themed photography contests on a rolling schedule. Each issue is built around an open call. AAP Magazine #56 is the shadow-themed cycle — work engaging with shadow as subject, structure, or compositional element.
Selection is by Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, founder and editor of All About Photo. Single-juror selection.
The winner receives $1,000 cash and publication in AAP Magazine #56. Selected photographers are featured on the All About Photo platform.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the All About Photo website with up to 40 images. Fee is tiered $30–$35. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced May 30, 2026.

calls.title: Color, Culture, Continuum – An Asian American Mosaic
calls.org: Asian American Museum of Orange County
calls.description: Celebrates Asian American life through photography. Professional and amateur photographers welcome to submit work exploring identity, heritage, and community.
jury: Kim Chapin, Executive Director of Photography, LA Times
calls.summary: Celebrating Asian American life through photography — identity, heritage, and community.
prose: Color, Culture, Continuum — An Asian American Mosaic is an open call from the Asian American Museum of Orange County, California. The brief invites photography exploring Asian American identity, heritage, and community.

The 2026 jury combines journalism, photography, and community perspectives: Kim Chapin (Executive Director of Photography, LA Times), Gong Cheng (sports photojournalist), Hiroshi Watanabe (photographer), and Katherine Shen (art enthusiast).
Top prize is $2,500. Eligibility is restricted to Asian American photographers, professional and amateur.
Submission is through SmarterEntry with up to 3 images. Fee is $30. The 2026 deadline was March 31.

calls.title: Night Works
calls.description: Seeking images made after dark where night is not simply a setting but an active collaborator.
calls.summary: Seeking images made after dark where night is not simply a setting but an active collaborator.
prose: Decagon Gallery is an online photography gallery that runs themed juried calls. Night Works is the gallery's call for photography made after dark — work where night functions as an active collaborator rather than just a setting.

The framing distinguishes the call from generic 'night photography' competitions: the brief asks for images where the conditions of darkness shape what the photograph is about, not just what's visible.
Top prize is $500. Selected work is shown in an online exhibition on the gallery's site.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the gallery's website with 1–8 images. Fee is tiered $10–$25. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced April 15, 2026.

calls.title: Fall 2026 - Spring 2027 Solo Exhibitions
calls.org: SRO Photo Gallery, Texas Tech University
calls.description: Six to eight solo exhibitions plus four moving image exhibitions. All styles and techniques welcome. Lubbock, Texas.
calls.summary: Six to eight solo exhibitions plus four moving image exhibitions. All styles welcome. Lubbock, Texas.
prose: SRO Photo Gallery is the photography gallery within Texas Tech University's Landmark Arts program in Lubbock, Texas. The annual Solo Exhibitions open call selects programming for an academic year — six to eight solo exhibitions plus four moving image exhibitions across the Fall 2026 – Spring 2027 schedule.
Selected artists receive a full solo exhibition slot rather than inclusion in a group show — the structural premise is dedicated wall and time for each artist.
All styles, techniques, and subjects are welcome. Eligibility is open globally.
Submission is by email with 20 images representing the proposed exhibition. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was March 31; results announced early May 2026.

calls.title: Hasselblad Foundation Photo Book Grant 2026
calls.description: Two grants of SEK 100,000 (~$9,500 USD) each supporting development and publication of photographic books. Projects should be largely edited but not yet published.
calls.summary: Two grants of SEK 100,000 each supporting development and publication of photographic books.
prose: The Hasselblad Foundation Photo Book Grant supports the development and publication of photographic books. Two grants of SEK 100,000 each (approximately $9,500 USD) are awarded each cycle.

The grant is staged: projects should be largely edited but not yet published. The funding is structured to push books over the finishing line — editing is mostly done, what's needed is production funding.
AI-generated mockups in book dummies must be disclosed.
The 2026 jury is Jacob Birch (Spine Studio), Maryam Fanni (HDK-Valand, the Gothenburg art school), and the Hasselblad Foundation's own Andréas Hagström and Dragana Vujanovic Östlind.
Eligibility is restricted to professional photographers. Submission is through Picter with a digital book dummy. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 1; results announced June 2026.

calls.title: Grants in Photography 2026
calls.description: Five $3,000 grants for photographers in New York State (outside NYC region). Exhibition and publication in Contact Sheet.
calls.summary: Five $3,000 grants for photographers in New York State (outside NYC). Exhibition and publication in Contact Sheet.
prose: Light Work is a Syracuse, New York nonprofit photography organization with a long history of supporting photographers — its annual residency program has hosted hundreds of artists since 1976. The Grants in Photography are the organization's annual cash-grant program for New York State photographers.

Five $3,000 grants are awarded each cycle. Eligibility is restricted to photographers based in New York State outside the New York City metropolitan region — the program is structured to support photographers in the rest of the state rather than the dominant urban concentration.
Beyond cash, recipients are exhibited at Light Work and published in Contact Sheet, the organization's long-running journal.
Submission is through SlideRoom with 10–20 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 1.

calls.title: Portals: New Perspectives
calls.description: Exploring the visual and symbolic power of openings, thresholds, and transitions. Windows, doorways, mirrors, gates, archways, and frames within frames. Juror: Ann Jastrab.
jury: Ann M. Jastrab, Executive Director, Center for Photographic Art
calls.summary: Exploring openings, thresholds, and transitions — windows, doorways, mirrors, gates, frames within frames.
prose: Portals: New Perspectives is one of PhotoPlace Gallery's recurring juried calls. PhotoPlace Gallery is a photography gallery in Middlebury, Vermont, that programs themed exhibitions on a rolling schedule.

The brief is iconographic: openings, thresholds, and transitions. Windows, doorways, mirrors, gates, archways, and frames within frames. The selection is interested in how photographers use these architectural and visual structures to point beyond what they show.
Selection is by Ann M. Jastrab, Executive Director of the Center for Photographic Art (Carmel-by-the-Sea, California). Single-juror selection.
AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the gallery's website with 5+ images. Fee is $39. The 2026 deadline was April 6.

calls.title: CPA Artist Grants 2026
calls.description: Five $5,000 grants across five categories: emerging photographer, mid-career photographer, landscape photographer, LGBTQ+ photographer, and Monterey County resident.
jury: Gregory Harris, Curator of Photography, High Museum of Art
calls.summary: Five $5,000 grants: emerging, mid-career, landscape, LGBTQ+, and Monterey County resident photographers.
prose: The Center for Photographic Art (CPA) is a Carmel-by-the-Sea, California nonprofit photography institution. The CPA Artist Grants are its annual category-restricted grant program. The 2026 cycle awards five separate $5,000 grants in distinct categories: emerging photographer, mid-career photographer, landscape photographer, LGBTQ+ photographer, and Monterey County resident.
The five-category structure means applicants apply to a specific track — selection is within category rather than against the whole field.
Selection is by Diane Chung (Founder, CHUNG 24 GALLERY), Gregory Harris (Curator of Photography, High Museum of Art), and Frank Yamrus (fine art photographer).

Eligibility is open to photographers 18+, with the geographic and identity restrictions applying within specific categories rather than overall. Submission is through the CPA website with 10–20 images. Fee is $30. The 2026 deadline was April 7.

calls.title: Thoughts of Summer
calls.description: Celebrating summer — family, friends, vacations. Jurors: Lisa Woodward and Mia Dalglish (Pictura co-curators). Greenville, SC.
calls.summary: Celebrating summer — family, friends, vacations. Jurors: Pictura co-curators. Greenville, SC.
prose: The Southeast Center for Photography (SEC4P) is a Greenville, South Carolina photography gallery and education center that runs themed juried exhibitions on a regular schedule. Thoughts of Summer is the gallery's seasonal call — work engaging with summer as subject and feeling: family, friends, vacations, summer light.
Selection is by Lisa Woodward and Mia Dalglish, the co-curators of Pictura — the photography curatorial collaboration. Two-juror selection.
Selected work is shown in a physical group exhibition at SEC4P in Greenville. Eligibility is open globally.
Submission is through Smarter Entry with up to 25 images. Fee is $35. The 2026 deadline was April 19; results announced April 30, 2026.

calls.title: 2026 International Portfolio Competition
calls.description: NYC's longest-running cooperative gallery awarding three solo shows. Portfolio: 10-15 images with consistent theme. AI may assist but work must begin with real photographic image.
calls.summary: NYC's longest-running cooperative gallery awarding three solo shows. Portfolio of 10-15 images. AI assist OK.
prose: Soho Photo Gallery is a photographer-run cooperative gallery in New York, founded in 1971 by photojournalists. It bills itself as the longest-running cooperative photography gallery in the city. The 2026 International Portfolio Competition is the gallery's annual portfolio-based prize.
The award structure is unusual: three solo exhibitions are awarded — three winners each receive a dedicated solo show at the gallery, rather than a single grand prize plus group runners-up.
Submitted portfolios must be 10–15 images with a consistent theme. AI may assist, but work must begin with a real photographic image — the gallery accepts AI-touched but not fully AI-generated work.
Eligibility is open to photographers 18+ globally. Submission is through CaFÉ. Fee is $60. The 2026 deadline was April 3.

calls.title: THE PORTRAIT
calls.description: Explores depth and complexity of human subject. Juried by Elizabeth Flinsch. All lens-based practices welcome. Minneapolis, MN.
calls.summary: Exploring depth and complexity of the human subject. All lens-based practices welcome. Minneapolis, MN.
prose: Praxis Photo Arts Center is a Minneapolis nonprofit gallery for fine art photography. THE PORTRAIT is one of its themed juried exhibitions — built around the depth and complexity of the human subject.
Selection is by Elizabeth Flinsch, Editor of SHOTS Magazine — the long-running US fine art photography quarterly. Single-juror selection.
All lens-based practices are welcome. Selected work is shown in a physical group exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis.
Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+. Submission is through the gallery's website with up to 10 images. Fee is $35. The 2026 deadline was April 5; results announced April 16, 2026.

calls.title: Earthly Fabulations
calls.description: Earth Day 2026 call for lens-based artists deconstructing landscape photography tradition. Ephemeral online exhibition displayed one month.
jury: Caroline von Courten, Artistic Director, Der Greif
Francesca Hummler, Community Manager & Program Curator, Der Greif
Ilaria Sponda, Managing Editor & Project Manager, Der Greif
Carolina Semprucci, Graphic Designer & Assistant Editor, Der Greif
calls.summary: Earth Day call for lens-based artists deconstructing landscape photography tradition. Ephemeral online exhibition.
prose: Earthly Fabulations is Der Greif's Earth Day open call, themed around deconstructing the landscape photography tradition. The brief asks lens-based artists to interrogate how landscape has been seen, framed, and idealized — and what alternative ways of looking might surface.
Selected work is shown in an ephemeral online exhibition on Der Greif's platform — displayed for one month before being archived rather than featured permanently.
Eligibility is restricted to emerging artists. The fee is voluntary — €10 suggested but not required.

Selection is by Der Greif's editorial team: Caroline von Courten (Artistic Director), Francesca Hummler (Community Manager and Program Curator), Ilaria Sponda (Managing Editor and Project Manager), and Carolina Semprucci (Graphic Designer and Assistant Editor).
Submission is through Picter with 1–10 images. The 2026 deadline was April 8; selection announced April 22, 2026.

calls.title: Golden Turtle International Wildlife Festival 2026
calls.description: International wildlife photography competition in 12 categories: Animals in the Environment, Portrait of the Animal, Animal Behaviour, Microcosm, Underwater World, Art and Nature's Image, Landscape, Magic of Plants, Humans and Nature, Reserved Russia, Mobile Photography, and Youth (two age groups).
