Up to 20 photos per author. Professional jury of international wildlife photographers. Finalists exhibited in Moscow autumn 2026, published in festival album. No zoo photography except Humans and Nature category. No composites or montage. RAW files required from semifinalists.
jury: Andrey Kamenev, National Geographic Russia Photographer
Mario Suárez Porras, Canon Pro Master, Bird Photographer (Spain)
Fernando Faciole, National Geographic Explorer, Conservation Photographer (Brazil)
Anthony Ochieng, National Geographic Explorer, Wildlife Photographer (Kenya)
calls.summary: International wildlife competition in 12 categories. Finalists exhibited in Moscow, published in festival album.
prose: Golden Turtle International Wildlife Festival is an annual international wildlife photography competition based in Russia. The 2026 edition runs across 12 categories: Animals in the Environment, Portrait of the Animal, Animal Behaviour, Microcosm, Underwater World, Art and Nature's Image, Landscape, Magic of Plants, Humans and Nature, Reserved Russia, Mobile Photography, and Youth (with two age groups).

Technical and ethical rules are strict: no zoo photography (except in the Humans and Nature category), no composites or montage, no AI-generated work. RAW files are required from semifinalists for verification.
Top prize is $2,000. Finalists are exhibited in Moscow in autumn 2026 and published in the festival album.

The 2026 jury is built from international wildlife photographers: Andrey Kamenev (National Geographic Russia), Gheorghe Popa (Romania), Mario Suárez Porras (Canon Pro Master, Spain), Cynthia Bandurek (Argentina/Costa Rica), Fernando Faciole (National Geographic Explorer, Brazil), Francesco Pacienza (Italy), and Anthony Ochieng (National Geographic Explorer, Kenya).
Eligibility is open globally. Each photographer may submit up to 20 photos. Application is free, made through the Golden Turtle website. The 2026 deadline was April 7.

calls.title: Sarajevo Photography Festival 2026
calls.description: Opening week June 1-7, 2026. Grand Prix: €2,000 cash. Canon-sponsored professional awards. Eight competition categories. Total prizes ~€7,000.
jury: Simone Azzoni, Professor, Contemporary Art History
Teresa Freitas, Director, Lisbon Street Photo Fest
Timotej Letonja, Founder & Editor-in-Chief, Numéro Netherlands
Fernanda Prado Verčič, Director, Kranj Foto Fest
calls.summary: Opening week June 1-7. Grand Prix: €2,000. Canon-sponsored professional awards. Eight competition categories.
prose: Sarajevo Photography Festival is the international photography festival held annually in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina. The 2026 opening week runs June 1–7.

The festival's competition runs across eight categories. Total prize fund is approximately €7,000, with the Grand Prix awarding €2,000 cash. Canon sponsors a set of professional-tier awards within the program. AI-generated work is not accepted.

The 2026 jury draws from European photography festival directors and contemporary art figures: Simone Azzoni (Professor of Contemporary Art History, also Co-Founder of Grenze Festival), Marko Drobnjaković (documentary photographer), Teresa Freitas (Director, Lisbon Street Photo Fest), Šejla Kamerić (visual artist), Timotej Letonja (Founder & Editor-in-Chief, Numéro Netherlands), Coline Plançon (curator and coordinator, PhotoSaintGermain), Fernanda Prado Verčič (Director, Kranj Foto Fest), and Ionuț Trandafirescu (Director, Bucharest Photofest).
Eligibility is open to photographers 16+ globally. Submission is through the festival's website with 1–6 images. Fee is tiered €15–€30. The 2026 deadline was April 10.

calls.title: Framed: Black and White
calls.description: Juried black and white group show exploring classic, nostalgic and dynamic translation with diversity of contemporary voices. Portland, OR.
jury: Todd Johnson, Founder & Director, Black Box Gallery
calls.summary: Juried black and white group show. Classic, nostalgic, and dynamic monochrome with diverse contemporary voices. Portland, OR.
prose: Framed: Black and White is the black-and-white-themed cycle of Black Box Gallery's recurring juried exhibition program. Black Box Gallery is a Portland, Oregon photography gallery directed by Todd Johnson, who holds an MFA in Photography from the San Francisco Art Institute and acts as juror for the gallery's calls. The brief seeks classic, nostalgic, and dynamic monochrome work spanning the diversity of contemporary voices working in B&W today.

The selection structure follows the gallery's standard format: 26 photographs are chosen for the physical gallery exhibition, 50 additional for the online gallery annex, and all 76 selected works appear in a printed Blurb catalog.

The gallery covers all printing, matting, and framing for selected work — archival printing on Epson Premium Luster Photo paper. After the exhibition closes, prints stay in the gallery's flat files for two years of ongoing promotion.

Entry fee is $40 per submission of up to 5 photos. Submissions are by email — JPEG, max 1200 pixels longest side, 72 PPI, under 5MB. Eligibility is open worldwide. Sales terms: 50% gallery commission, photographer retains rights and may opt out of sale.
The 2026 deadline was April 10; juror decisions communicated approximately April 17–20, 2026.

calls.title: Hiding in Plain Sight
calls.org: Rhode Island Center for Photographic Arts
calls.description: Exploring the unseen and forgotten. Challenges myths and revalues overlooked subjects. Providence, RI.
calls.summary: Exploring the unseen and forgotten. Challenging myths and revaluing overlooked subjects. Providence, RI.
prose: Hiding in Plain Sight is one of the Rhode Island Center for Photographic Arts (RICPA)'s themed juried calls. RICPA is a Providence-based nonprofit photography gallery and educational center.

The brief is interpretive: photographers are asked to explore the unseen and forgotten — work that challenges myths and revalues overlooked subjects. The framing invites attention to what photography typically misses or treats as background.
Selection is by Lou Jones, photographer. Single-juror selection.
Cash prizes are $250 (first), $150 (second), $75 (third). Selected work is shown in a physical exhibition at RICPA.
Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+. Submission is through CaFÉ with 3–15 images. Fee is $35. The 2026 deadline was April 10.

calls.title: Queer Conscience 2026 Photography Exhibition
calls.description: 4th annual for LGBTQIA2+ community. Seeking work affirming our own truths and expressing resistance during Pride month. Mill Valley, CA.
jury: Conor Moynihan, Associate Curator, RISD Museum
Nathan Lomas, Gallery Manager, The Image Flow
calls.summary: 4th annual for LGBTQIA2+ community. Affirming truths and expressing resistance during Pride month. Mill Valley, CA.
prose: The Image Flow is a Marin County, California photography center based in San Anselmo. The Queer Conscience exhibition is its annual juried show timed to Pride month. The 2026 edition is the fourth cycle.

Eligibility is restricted to LGBTQIA2+ photographers based in the United States. The brief asks for work affirming our own truths and expressing resistance — the editorial register foregrounds political and personal assertion rather than simply visibility.
Selection is by Conor Moynihan (Associate Curator, RISD Museum) and Nathan Lomas (Gallery Manager, The Image Flow). The 2026 exhibition is timed to coincide with Pride month.
Submission is through ArtCall with up to 5 images. Fee is $40. The 2026 deadline was April 11; results announced April 17, 2026.

calls.title: PPA Photo Award 2026
calls.description: For emerging US photographers. Prize: $2,000 cash, interview, Lenscratch feature, virtual artist talk. Juror: Craig Krull, art dealer.
jury: Craig Krull, Founder, Craig Krull Gallery
calls.ai: AI editing OK, fully generated not accepted
calls.summary: For emerging US photographers. $2,000 prize, Lenscratch feature, virtual artist talk. Juror: Craig Krull.
prose: Pasadena Photography Arts (PPA) is a nonprofit photography organization based in Pasadena, California. The PPA Photo Award is its annual prize for emerging US photographers — career-stage rather than location restricted to Pasadena.
The 2026 juror is Craig Krull, founder of the Craig Krull Gallery in Santa Monica — an established LA-area gallery with a long photography program. Single-juror selection rather than panel.

The winner receives $2,000 cash plus an interview, a Lenscratch feature (Lenscratch is the long-running US fine-art photography platform), and a virtual artist talk with PPA. AI editing is acceptable; fully AI-generated work is not.
Eligibility is restricted to emerging US-based photographers 18+. Submission is through CaFÉ with 10–20 images. Fee is $42. The 2026 deadline was April 26; results announced August 21, 2026.

calls.title: XVI Concurso Internacional de Fotografía sobre Humanización Asistencial
calls.org: Hospital San Juan de Dios de León
calls.description: 16th edition of this international photography competition seeking images that reflect humanization, solidarity, and care in healthcare and everyday life. Photos can depict professional healthcare settings, family, personal, sports, or cultural environments where someone helps a person in need. Open to all adults. Up to 3 photographs per participant. Prizes: €600, €400, €200 plus a weekend stay.
calls.summary: Photography reflecting humanization, solidarity, and care in healthcare and everyday life. Prizes: €600/€400/€200.
prose: The Concurso Internacional de Fotografía sobre Humanización Asistencial is an international photography competition organized by Hospital San Juan de Dios de León, in Spain. The 2026 edition is the 16th cycle.

The brief is thematically narrow: photography reflecting humanization, solidarity, and care — in healthcare settings or in everyday life. Subjects can depict professional healthcare environments, family, personal, sports, or cultural settings where someone helps a person in need. The unifying thread is the act of care.
Cash prizes are €600, €400, and €200, plus a weekend hotel stay for the top winner. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Selection is by Secundino Pérez, Mauricio Peña, and Javier Casares — all photographers.
Eligibility is open globally to adults 18+. Submission is by email with up to 3 photographs per participant. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 13; results announced April 24, 2026.

calls.title: light
calls.description: Exploring light as key element. 47 images selected. Exhibition May 8 - June 18, 2026. Juror: Elizabeth Avedon. Johnson City, TX.
jury: Elizabeth Avedon, Curator & Photography Book Designer
calls.summary: Exploring light as key element. 47 images selected. Juror: Elizabeth Avedon. Exhibition in Johnson City, TX.
prose: A Smith Gallery is a photography gallery in Johnson City, Texas, that runs themed juried exhibitions on a recurring schedule. The 'light' call is the gallery's exhibition for work where light functions as the key element of the photograph — its presence, behavior, and quality as subject rather than as a technical condition.
Forty-seven images are selected for the physical exhibition at the gallery, running May 8 – June 18, 2026.
Selection is by Elizabeth Avedon, curator and photography book designer.

AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the gallery's website with unlimited images per applicant. Fee is $40. The 2026 deadline was April 13; results announced April 24, 2026.

calls.title: Sharing and Caring Cities: Portraits of Collective Urban Life
calls.description: 10th annual photography contest exploring shared urban spaces addressing inequality and climate change. Open to all photographers.
jury: Nikhil Anand, Professor of Anthropology, Penn
Matthew Neff, Director, Undergraduate Fine Arts, Weitzman School
Jennifer Whittaker, Research Scientist, CHOP Policy Lab
calls.summary: 10th annual contest exploring shared urban spaces addressing inequality and climate change.
prose: The Penn Institute for Urban Research (Penn IUR) runs an annual photography contest as part of its public program. The 2026 edition is the 10th cycle, themed Sharing and Caring Cities: Portraits of Collective Urban Life — work engaging with shared urban spaces and how cities address inequality and climate change.
The contest is academic-affiliated rather than a fine-art competition. The brief favors documentary observation of shared infrastructure, public space, and collective practices.
AI-generated work is not accepted.

Selection is by Penn faculty and researchers: Nikhil Anand (Professor of Anthropology), Amy Hillier (Associate Professor), Matthew Neff (Director, Undergraduate Fine Arts, Weitzman School), and Jennifer Whittaker (Research Scientist, CHOP Policy Lab). Top prize is $500.
Eligibility is open to all photographers globally. Submission is through Penn's Qualtrics form with 3 images. Application is free. The 2026 deadline was April 15.

calls.title: Portrait Awards 2026
calls.description: Fourth edition celebrating portrait as a space of presence, responsibility, and authorship amidst visual saturation. Barcelona.
jury: Burkhard Arnold, Gallery Director, in focus Galerie
Erin Hoyt, Executive Director, Filter Photo Festival
calls.summary: Fourth edition celebrating portrait as a space of presence and authorship amidst visual saturation. Barcelona.
prose: Dodho Magazine is a Barcelona-based contemporary photography magazine. The Portrait Awards is one of its themed annual competitions. The 2026 edition is the fourth cycle. The brief celebrates portrait as a space of presence, responsibility, and authorship amidst visual saturation — framing portraiture as a counter-practice to image overproduction.

The 2026 jury draws from the international photography ecosystem: Aline Smithson (Founder & Editor, Lenscratch), Burkhard Arnold (Gallery Director, in focus Galerie), Erin Hoyt (Executive Director, Filter Photo Festival), and Roger Ballen (photographer).
Selected work is published by Dodho Magazine.

Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through Dodho's website with 3, 6, or 12 images. Fee is tiered €30–€60 based on submission scale. The 2026 deadline was April 15; results announced May 1–3, 2026.

calls.title: ViewPoint Gallery International Photography Competition
calls.description: Twelve winners display professionally printed, matted, framed work for one month each from June 2026 to May 2027. Eastern Canada.
calls.summary: Twelve winners displayed professionally printed and framed for one month each, June 2026 to May 2027. Eastern Canada.
prose: ViewPoint Gallery is a photographer-run cooperative gallery in Halifax, Nova Scotia — Eastern Canada. The annual International Photography Competition selects work for the gallery's monthly featured wall.

The structure is unusual: twelve winners are selected, and each receives a one-month featured display from June 2026 through May 2027. Each winner gets the wall for the full month rather than a single group exhibition. Production is gallery-supplied: work is professionally printed, matted, and framed.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is by Google Form with 3 images. Fee is $25. The 2026 deadline was April 15; results announced May 8, 2026.

calls.title: The Cortona on The Move / BarTur Grant
calls.org: BarTur Photo Award / Cortona On The Move
calls.description: Supports photographers with ongoing projects. Honors visual storytellers who push the medium forward with clear authorship. Winners exhibited at Cortona On The Move festival. Note: Cortona On The Move and BarTur Photo Award have announced the conclusion of their collaboration after the first edition.
calls.summary: Supporting photographers with ongoing projects and clear authorship. Winners exhibited at Cortona On The Move festival.
prose: The Cortona on The Move / BarTur Grant was a $30,000 grant supporting professional photographers with ongoing projects, organized as a collaboration between Cortona On The Move (the Italian photography festival held annually in Cortona) and BarTur Photo Award.
The brief honored visual storytellers who push the medium forward with clear authorship. Winners were exhibited at Cortona On The Move festival.
Note: Cortona On The Move and BarTur Photo Award announced the conclusion of their collaboration after this first edition. The 2026 cycle was a one-time joint program.

Eligibility was restricted to professional photographers. Submission was through Picter. Fee was $25. AI-generated work was not accepted. The 2026 deadline was February 13; results announced July 2026.

calls.title: Montgomery Photo Festival 2026
calls.description: Eighth annual festival. Four categories: Color, Monochromatic, Alternative process, Manipulation. No theme; all work acceptable.
calls.summary: Eighth annual festival. Four categories: Color, Monochromatic, Alternative process, Manipulation. No theme.
prose: Montgomery Photo Festival is an annual photography festival held in Montgomery, Alabama. The 2026 edition is the festival's eighth cycle.

The structure runs across four process and approach categories: Color, Monochromatic, Alternative Process, and Manipulation. There is no thematic restriction — subject matter is open. Selection is by category type rather than by topic.
Selection is by Carol McCusker. Total prize pool is $3,500. Selected work is shown in the festival's exhibition program in Montgomery.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through ArtCall with up to 3 images. Fee is $35. The 2026 deadline was April 17; results announced May 22, 2026.

calls.title: LUMINOSITY - The Impact of Light
calls.org: New York Center for Photographic Arts
calls.description: Exploring light's presence, absence, and location. Winners receive $4,000 cash, online gallery feature, catalog publication. New York, NY.
jury: Crista Dix, Executive Director, Griffin Museum of Photography
calls.summary: Exploring light's presence, absence, and location. $4,000 cash prize, online gallery, catalogue. New York.
prose: The New York Center for Photographic Arts (NYC4PA) runs themed juried exhibitions on a recurring schedule. LUMINOSITY — The Impact of Light is the call for work engaging with light as primary subject — its presence, absence, and location.
Selection is by Crista Dix, Executive Director of the Griffin Museum of Photography in Winchester, Massachusetts. Single-juror selection.
Total prize pool is $4,000 cash. Selected work is featured in an online gallery and a published catalog.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through Smarter Entry with unlimited images per entrant. Fee is $40. The 2026 deadline was April 19; results announced approximately May 3–10, 2026.

calls.title: FMoPA International Photography Competition 2026
calls.description: International jury selection. Winning entries printed and exhibited June 16 - August 2, 2026 at Ybor City, Tampa.
jury: Jessica Jarl, Global Director of Exhibitions, Fotografiska
calls.summary: International jury selection. Winning entries printed and exhibited at Ybor City, Tampa, June-August 2026.
prose: The Florida Museum of Photographic Arts (FMoPA) is a Tampa-based museum dedicated to photography, located in Tampa's Ybor City Historic District. The annual International Photography Competition is the museum's flagship juried open call.

The 2026 edition runs across seven categories: People/Portraits, Places/Landscape, Nature/Science/Animals, Documentation/Photojournalism, Still Life, Abstract, and Conceptual. Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+.
Best in Competition receives $1,000 cash. Category winners receive goods and services rather than additional cash. Winning works are exhibited at FMoPA from June 16 to August 2, 2026.

The 2026 jury is built from international institutions: Jessica Jarl (Global Director of Exhibitions, Fotografiska), Hiromi Nakamura (Curator, Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Photography), Elena Paraskeva (photographer and art director), Bärbel Reinhard (photographer, curator and educator), and Kristen Roles (photographic artist and educator).
Submission is through Picter with up to 15 images. Fee is $10. The 2026 deadline was April 22; results announced May 13, 2026.

calls.title: CITY Photography Exhibit
calls.description: Capturing personal urban experience from quiet, unnoticed moments to the bustling energy of a metropolis. Santa Fe, NM.
jury: Holly Hart, Fine Art Photographer & Founder, Dusk Gallery
calls.summary: Capturing personal urban experience from quiet moments to bustling energy. Santa Fe, NM.
prose: Dusk Gallery is a Santa Fe, New Mexico photography gallery — a sister gallery to Decode Gallery in Tucson, both founded by fine art photographer Holly Hart. CITY is the gallery's call for work engaging with personal urban experience: quiet, unnoticed moments through the bustling energy of metropolitan life.
The brief is open in approach. Selection is by Holly Hart.

Selected work is shown in a physical exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe. The gallery's production model mirrors Decode's — the gallery typically covers professional printing and framing for selected work.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the gallery's website with 5 or 10 images. Fee is $40–$45. The 2026 deadline was April 16; results announced approximately April 30, 2026.

calls.title: Film Photo Award 2026
calls.description: Three grants of professional film and complimentary processing by Praus Productions. Open to emerging, established, and student photographers worldwide.
calls.summary: Three grants of professional film and processing by Praus Productions. US-based photographers only.
prose: The Film Photo Award is unusual in its prize structure: rather than cash, the award provides three grants of professional film stock and complimentary processing by Praus Productions, the Rochester-based film processing lab.

The grant supports photographers committing to extended film-based projects — the photographer brings the project, the award brings the materials. Selected work is also published on the Film Photo Award platform.
Eligibility is restricted to US-based photographers 18+. Open across career stages: emerging, established, and student photographers all eligible.
Submission is through CaFÉ with 1–15 images. Fee is tiered $25–$35. The 2026 deadline was April 26; results announced late May 2026.

calls.title: HOME Photography Exhibit
calls.description: Home as feeling, memory, sanctuary. Exploring domesticity, heritage, shelter, identity through diverse styles. Tucson, AZ.
calls.summary: Home as feeling, memory, sanctuary. Exploring domesticity, heritage, shelter, and identity. Tucson, AZ.
prose: Decode Gallery is a Tucson, Arizona photography gallery founded by conceptual fine art photographer Holly Hart, who also juries the gallery's open calls. HOME is the gallery's call for work engaging with the multifaceted nature of home — as feeling, memory, sanctuary, physical space, heritage, or identity.
The brief invites domestic spaces, loved ones, landscapes, or personal belonging. The thematic framing is broader than literal residence — what counts as home is left to the photographer.

Selection structure: at least 26 images selected for exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson, June 6–27, 2026. The gallery covers production: complimentary professional printing on Epson printers with Ilford Pearl paper, museum-quality 22×22 white framing, and custom matting.

Eligibility is open worldwide to all skill levels. Submission is through the gallery's website with 5 or 10 images. Fee is $40–$45. The 2026 deadline was April 18; results announced approximately May 2, 2026.

calls.title: Masterclasses Program 2026/2027
calls.description: Online masterclasses led by Aaron Schuman, Charlie Engman, Erik Kessels, Salvatore Vitale, and Vasantha Yoganathan.
calls.summary: Online masterclasses by Aaron Schuman, Charlie Engman, Erik Kessels, Salvatore Vitale, and Vasantha Yoganathan.
prose: PhMuseum is a photography-focused educational platform offering online masterclasses, mentorship programs, and competitions. The 2026/2027 Masterclasses Program runs five distinct online masterclasses from October 2026 through May 2027 — an eight-month structured cohort program with a different focus and instructor for each track.

The five masterclasses for 2026/2027: CRITICAE — Documentary Photography, led by Aaron Schuman (photographer and writer). IDEA — Conceptual Thinking, led by Charlie Engman (photographer). CURAE — Artistic Development, led by Erik Kessels (curator and publisher, who has worked across major photobook projects). MEDIAE — Transmedia Storytelling, led by Salvatore Vitale (photographer and editor). FOLIO — Photobook Making, led jointly by Vasantha Yogananthan (photographer) and Cécile Poimbœuf-Koizumi (publisher).

Each masterclass operates as a separate cohort with its own application — applicants choose one track. The format is online and structured around cohort-based learning with selected practitioners working alongside the lead instructor across the program duration.

Specific fees and participant numbers are not published on the program landing page; applicants need to consult the linked masterclass pages for current details. Early-bird and scholarship applications close April 30, 2026; regular applications close May 28, 2026.

calls.title: FOTOFILMIC OPEN 2026
calls.description: Open exhibition featuring contemporary film-based photography. Honourable mentions: Mauro Curti, Melissa Renwick, Sasha Arutyunova, Will Warasila, Scott Offen, Jonah Reenders. Exhibition May 2–31, 2026 at FOTOFILMIC, Bowen Island, BC.
jury: Christopher McCall, Curator, former Director of Pier 24 Photography

prose: World Cyanotype Day is an annual celebration of the cyanotype process — a 19th-century alternative photographic technique that uses iron-based salts and UV light to produce prints in distinctive shades of blue. The event was founded in 2015 by AlternativePhotography.com (itself established in 1999) and runs each year on the last Saturday of September. The 2026 cycle covers September 26 through October 2.

Submissions are free and open to anyone working with the process. Each year carries a theme — 2025's was "Cultivating Community," with the 2026 theme to be announced in spring. The format is single-image submissions: 1080px on the longest side, under 2MB, JPEG only (no PNG, TIFF, or HEIC), with filenames structured as "Name Surname, Title, Country.jpg." No nudes; submissions must follow the year's theme.
Selected work is shown across AlternativePhotography.com's gallery, Facebook, Instagram, Pinterest, BlueSky, and YouTube channels. There is no cash prize.

The event references Anna Atkins — the first woman to illustrate a photography book, using cyanotypes — as part of its lineage. AlternativePhotography.com is a non-profit, runs the event without sponsor backing, and maintains a substantial educational resource library on cyanotype chemistry, paper preparation, and exposure techniques.

prose: World Anthotype Day is an annual celebration of the anthotype process — a 19th-century photographic technique that uses plant-based emulsions and sunlight to make images. The event runs from August 1 through the last Saturday in October each year, with submissions free and open to anyone working with the process. The 2026 cycle closes October 31.

Entries require three components: a written description of the process used (including the plant material, exposure time, and any layering), the final anthotype image at 2,500 pixels minimum, and a photograph of the source plant taken before processing. Each non-member submits a single print, made within the prior twelve months. Files go via WeTransfer, Dropbox, or Google Drive to anthotype@alternativephotography.com.

Submissions are split between Professional and Non-Professional tracks across 11 categories: Advertising, Analog/Film, Architectural, Editorial, Event, Fine Art, Nature, People, Sports, Photography Book, and Special Category. Total prize pool is $60,000 across the program.

Top awards: International Photographer of the Year (Professional, $10,000) and Discovery of the Year (Non-Professional, $5,000). Each Professional Category winner receives $1,000 cash plus a $500 travel allowance; each Non-Professional Category winner receives $500 plus $500 travel. Beyond cash, IPA category winners receive an IPA Trophy, two tickets to the IPA Awards Gala, inclusion in the Best of Show exhibition, screening at House of Lucie Galleries worldwide, publication in the IPA Annual Book, and press coverage to the program's 130,000+ member network.

The 2026 jury includes Anne Morin (curator at diChroma Photography), Caroline Metcalfe (Photography Director), Giovanna Calvenzi (photo editor and curator), Kirk McKoy (photojournalist), Michael Pritchard (Director-General of the Royal Photographic Society), Paris Chong (Leica Gallery LA), and others. Entry fees are tiered between $20 and $40 depending on category and submission tier. The 2026 deadline is June 30; results announced October 2026.

calls.title: London Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: International photography awards across 13 categories including Architecture, Fine Art, Nature, Minimalist, Fashion, and Black & White. Separate professional and amateur/student divisions.

calls.summary: International awards across 13 categories. Separate professional and amateur/student divisions.
prose: London Photography Awards is an international photography competition run by International Awards Associate, the same group that operates several other geographically-titled photography awards. The 2026 edition runs across 13 categories: Architecture, Fine Art, Nature, Minimalist, Fashion, Black & White, and others.
The structure is split: separate professional and amateur/student divisions, with the same categories on each side. Top prize is $3,000.

The 2026 jury is large — over 20 photographers, art directors, and educators across multiple countries, ranging from independent practitioners to ambassadors and creative agency directors. Submissions are reviewed across the full jury rather than category-by-category.

Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+. Submission is through the awards website with 1–8 images per entry. Fee is tiered $25–$50. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced May 15, 2026.

calls.title: Photo Journalism Prize 2026
calls.description: International award honoring editorial and documentary photography. 11 categories including Conflict, Daily Life, Documentary, Human Rights, and News. Founded by Hossein Farmani, creator of the Lucie Awards.

calls.summary: International award for editorial and documentary photography. 11 categories including Conflict and Human Rights.
prose: The Photo Journalism Prize is an international award honoring editorial and documentary photography. It was founded by Hossein Farmani, the same publisher who created the Lucie Awards.

The 2026 edition runs across 11 categories including Conflict, Daily Life, Documentary, Human Rights, and News. Total prize fund is €9,000: first €5,000, second €3,000, third €1,000. AI-generated work is not accepted.

The jury is built from working photojournalists and major-publication photo editors: James Nachtwey, Steve McCurry, Paolo Pellegrin, and Ron Haviv (co-founder of the VII Foundation) on the photographer side; Alex Pollack (Director of Photography, National Geographic), Sarah Gilbert and Jim Powell (Photo Editors, The Guardian), Pia Peterson Haggarty (Photo Director, Lonely Planet), and Natasha Egan (Executive Director, MoCP) on the editorial side, alongside curators, professors, and visual editors.

Eligibility is open globally to photographers 18+. Submission is through the prize website with 1–10 images per entry. Fee is tiered €20–€25. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced June 15, 2026.

calls.title: Gomma Black and White Photo Award 2026
calls.description: International black-and-white photography competition for project-based work. Submit 8–24 B&W images from any medium. All genres welcome. Winners published in a dedicated book. 3rd edition.
calls.summary: Project-based B&W competition. Submit 8-24 images. Winners published in a dedicated book. 3rd edition.
prose: Gomma Publishing is an independent photobook publisher specializing in black-and-white photography. The Gomma Black and White Photo Award is the publisher's annual project-based competition. The 2026 edition is the award's third cycle.

The brief is process-restricted but genre-open: project-based black-and-white photography of any kind, sourced from any medium (film, digital, hybrid). All genres welcome — documentary, fine art, conceptual. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Each application includes 8–24 black-and-white images forming a coherent project. Single-image submissions are not eligible — the award is structured around bodies of work.
Winners are published in a dedicated Gomma book. Cash prize is €500.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through Submittable. Fee is €29. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced December 2026.

calls.title: Landskrona Foto & Breadfield Dummy Award 2026
calls.description: International photobook dummy competition. Submit an unpublished photobook dummy as PDF. Winner receives full publication by Breadfield Press and Landskrona Foto in 2027 including design, printing, and distribution.
jury: Raquel Villar-Pérez, Independent Curator of Photography
Tommaso Parrillo, Publisher & Art Director, Witty Books
calls.summary: Photobook dummy competition. Winner receives full publication by Breadfield Press in 2027.
prose: Landskrona Foto is a Swedish photography institution that runs an annual festival in Landskrona — a small port town on the Öresund. Breadfield Press is a Malmö-based independent photobook publisher. The Dummy Award is a joint project — a photobook dummy competition with a full publication outcome.

The brief is straightforward: submit an unpublished photobook dummy. The winning project is published in 2027 as a Breadfield Press / Landskrona Foto co-edition, with design, printing, and distribution all covered by the partnership. The publication is the prize — there's no cash component.

The 2026 jury is Raquel Villar-Pérez (independent curator of photography), Greger Ulf Nilson (creative director), Jenny Lindhe (curator and artist), Mandy Barker (photographer), and Tommaso Parrillo (publisher and art director, Witty Books).
Eligibility is open globally to artists 18+. Submission is through Picter as a single PDF dummy. Fee is €30. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced September 4, 2026.

calls.title: International Aerial Photographer of the Year 2026
calls.org: International Aerial Photographer of the Year
calls.description: Competition celebrating aerial photography from all platforms — drones, planes, helicopters, hot air balloons, mountains, and skyscrapers. Images must be aerial perspective, shot since January 2021.
calls.summary: Celebrating aerial photography from all platforms — drones, planes, helicopters, mountains, and skyscrapers.
prose: International Aerial Photographer of the Year (ILPOTY) is a competition focused on aerial photography across all capture platforms — drones, planes, helicopters, hot air balloons, and even high-vantage-point work from mountains and skyscrapers. The eligibility criterion is the perspective of the image, not the equipment used to make it.
Submitted work must be aerial perspective and shot since January 2021 — recency restricted. AI-generated work is not accepted.
Top prize is $10,000. Submission is unlimited — entrants can submit as many images as they want for a single $22 entry fee, which is unusual for the competition format.
The 2026 jury is chaired by Peter Eastway, with Tom Hegen (the German photographer best known for aerial views of industrial landscapes), Isabella Tabacchi, and drone photographer Joanna Steidle.
Eligibility is open globally. Submission is through the awards' Secure Platform portal. The 2026 deadline was April 30; results announced July 2026.

calls.title: ReA! Art Fair 2026
calls.description: Open call for emerging visual artists including photographers for a contemporary art fair at Fabbrica del Vapore, Milan, October 22–25, 2026. All visual art accepted. 50 artists selected; no additional exhibiting costs.
calls.summary: Contemporary art fair at Fabbrica del Vapore, Milan. 50 emerging artists selected. No exhibiting costs.
prose: ReA! Art Fair is a Milan contemporary art fair focused on emerging artists. The 2026 edition runs October 22–25 at Fabbrica del Vapore, the city's converted industrial cultural complex.

Fifty artists are selected through the open call. The fair is multidisciplinary — all visual art is accepted, including photography. Selected artists exhibit without additional booth or production costs beyond the application fee.

Eligibility is restricted to emerging artists. The €1,500 prize is awarded to one of the selected artists. The 2026 jury is five curators: Milena Zanetti, Valeria Conti, Vittoria Martinotti, Erica Massaccesi, and Maria Myasnikova.
Application is via the fair's website with a portfolio PDF. The fee is €55. The 2026 deadline was May 6; results announced June 15, 2026.

calls.title: Prix Virginia 2026
calls.description: International photography prize exclusively for professional women photographers. Submit 12–18 cohesive photographs plus CV and artistic statement. Photos must not have been previously exhibited in France. Winner announced November 2026.
jury: Anna Planas, Artistic Director, Paris Photo
calls.summary: International photography prize exclusively for professional women photographers. Submit 12-18 cohesive photographs.
prose: Prix Virginia is a French international photography prize awarded to professional women photographers. It is organized by Association Sylvia S., based in Paris, with a single €10,000 grant going to the winner.

The 2026 jury is built from major European photography institutions: Damarice Amao (Centre Pompidou), Anna Planas (Artistic Director, Paris Photo), Fiona Rogers (Curator, V&A), and Pauline Vermare (Curator, Brooklyn Museum).
Eligibility is restricted to professional women photographers internationally. Submitted photographs must not have been previously exhibited in France.
The application requires 12–18 cohesive photographs from a single body of work, plus CV and artistic statement. Submission is through Award Force. Application is free.
The 2026 deadline was May 7; the winner was announced in November 2026.

calls.title: MonoVisions Black & White Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: International black-and-white photography competition across 12 categories including Abstract, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscape, and Street. Open to all skill levels.
calls.summary: International B&W competition across 12 categories including Abstract, Architecture, Fine Art, and Street.
prose: MonoVisions Black & White Photography Awards is run by MonoVisions Magazine, an online photography publication operating since 2016 with a focus on black-and-white work. The 2026 cycle is one of multiple international monochrome competitions, distinguished by its deeper category-tiered structure and large jury panel.

Submissions are accepted in two sections — Single photos or Series (maximum 8 photos per series) — across twelve subject categories: Abstract, Architecture, Conceptual, Fine Art, Landscapes, Nature and Wildlife, Nude, People, Photojournalism, Portrait, Street Photography, and Travel.

The cash prize pool is $5,000, distributed across two top awards: Series of the Year ($3,000) and Photo of the Year ($2,000). Category winners and honorable mentions receive downloadable badges and certificates of achievement — recognition rather than additional cash.

The 2026 jury comprises 14 international judges: Cyrille Druart, Vera Saldivar de Lira, Arkadiusz Kubisiak, David Rathbone, Dr Nenad Nikolic, Agata Benhacoun, Michael Koster, Tatiana Kurnosova, Zhou HanShun, Monika K. Adler, Timurtas Onan, Keivan Cadinouche, and Philip Flip Collier — bringing together photographers and artists across multiple geographies.

Entry fees: $30 per series submission, $25 per single photo. Eligibility is open to professionals and amateurs at any skill level worldwide; both traditional and digital black-and-white photography are accepted. The 2026 deadline is May 17; winners announced July 26.

calls.title: Nature Photographer of the Year 2026
calls.description: International nature photography competition with 12 categories for individual images, a young photographers category (ages 10–17, free entry), and the Fred Hazelhoff Award for portfolios (€17.50). Award ceremony November 14, 2026.
calls.summary: International nature competition with 12 categories plus young photographers and portfolio awards.
prose: Nature Photographer of the Year (NPOTY) is an international nature photography competition organized by the Nature Talks Foundation (Stichting Nature Talks) in the Netherlands. The 2026 cycle is the contest's 11th consecutive year. Winners are announced at the Nature Talks Photo Festival on November 14, 2026.

The total prize pool is €25,000. The overall winner receives €3,000 in cash plus an additional €1,000 portfolio cash prize. Most category winners receive €500. The C11 category winner receives a photography weekend in Drenthe (Netherlands), and the C13 Youth winner (under 18) receives €250 in products.

Submissions are accepted across 13 categories total, including a free Youth category for photographers under 18 and a separate portfolio award. Photos can be from the current year or previous years — there is no recency restriction on submissions.
The 2025 contest received 24,781 entries from 96 countries, giving a sense of scale.

Eligibility is open to professional and non-professional photographers of all ages worldwide. AI-generated work is not accepted. Registration is free, but most categories carry a paid entry fee (€34 for the main contest, €17.50 for the Fred Hazelhoff portfolio award; the Youth category is free). The 2026 contest opens April 7 and closes June 2 at 23:59 CEST.

calls.title: HIPA Photography Award 2026
calls.org: Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum
calls.description: Major international photography award with 2026 theme 'Family.' Categories include Family, Dreams Through AI, Sports Photography, Portfolio, and General. Free entry, open to all photographers 18+.
calls.summary: Major international award. 2026 theme: Family. Free entry. Categories include Dreams Through AI and Sports.
prose: The Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum International Photography Award (HIPA) is one of the largest photography prizes in the world by total prize pool. Named after Sheikh Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, the 2026 cycle is HIPA's 15th season. Total prize pool: $1,000,000 USD across all categories.

The 2026 main theme is "Family." Submissions are accepted across multiple categories: Family ($40K/$30K/$20K for 1st/2nd/3rd), Dreams Through AI ($40K/$30K/$20K), Sports Photography ($40K/$30K/$20K), Portfolio/Story-Telling ($50K/$40K/$30K), General Color ($40K/$30K/$20K), and General Black & White ($40K/$30K/$20K). The Grand Prize Winner from any category receives an additional $200,000.

Special Awards add further prize money: Photography Appreciation ($100,000), Content Creator ($50,000), and Photographer of the Year ($80,000). AI-generated images are only accepted in the dedicated Dreams Through AI category and are excluded from all other categories.

There is no entry fee. Eligibility is open globally to photographers aged 18 and over. The judging process runs in four stages with typically nine judges; jurors remain anonymous until the season concludes — an unusual policy intended to keep selection insulated from external pressure.
Winners grant HIPA perpetual worldwide publication and promotional rights to winning photographs. The 2026 deadline is May 31 at 11:59 PM UAE local time.

calls.title: Natural Landscape Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: Competition celebrating realistic landscape and nature photography. No AI or compositing allowed. RAW file checks for finalists. Multiple categories from grand scenics to intimate abstracts.
calls.summary: Celebrating realistic landscape photography. No AI or compositing. RAW file checks for finalists.
prose: The Natural Landscape Photography Awards (NLPA) was founded in 2021 by photographers Tim Parkin, Matt Payne, Rajesh Jyothiswaran, and Alex Nail. The 2026 cycle is the 6th edition. The competition was set up specifically as a response to the increasing prevalence of compositing and heavy manipulation in landscape photography contests — NLPA positions itself as the prize for landscape work that represents the natural world truthfully.

Post-processing rules are unusually strict. Editing tools like Photoshop are permitted "when used sensitively" to enhance the viewer's experience, but compositing and substantive manipulations that mislead viewers about the natural scene are excluded. AI-generated images are not accepted. Finalists must provide RAW files for verification — a check that has become a defining feature of the award.

The 2026 cycle is judged by Anna Morgan, Albert Dros, Wayne Suggs, Mark Littlejohn, and Eric Bennett. The judging panel rotates each year. Categories cover grand scenic landscapes, intimate landscapes, abstracts, and other formats specific to the natural world.

Submissions accept 1 to 18 images. Eligibility is open globally to photographers worldwide. The 2026 deadline is May 31, with results announced September 15. Total prize pool is approximately $5,000 across categories; specific entry fees are tiered and listed on the awards site.

calls.title: Queer Nature Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: Free-entry photography award celebrating LGBTQ+ diversity through nature photography. Theme: Queer Nature (non-human). Submit via WeTransfer. Prizes include exhibitions and publication.
calls.summary: Free-entry award celebrating LGBTQ+ diversity through nature photography. Prizes include exhibitions.
jury: Christine Wilkinson, Wildlife Ecologist & Science Communicator
Charlotte Vermeulen, Storyteller & Emeritus Biologist, ARTIS Amsterdam Zoo
Noah Baars, Founder, Narwhal Rainbow Alliance
prose: The Queer Nature Photography Awards is administered by the Narwhal Rainbow Alliance, an Amsterdam-based organization at the intersection of LGBTQ+ advocacy and natural science communication. The 2026 cycle is the second edition. The brief is unusual: photographs of non-human nature documenting same-sex behaviors, gender fluidity, rainbow families, and other forms of biological diversity that challenge binary norms.

The premise is grounded in scientific literature: same-sex pairings, gender plasticity, and non-binary reproduction are documented across hundreds of species, from clownfish to bonobos, and the awards aim to surface that visual evidence in popular form rather than only academic publication.
First place receives €1,500. The top 10 photos are exhibited at the awards event, with the top 3 announced during the ceremony. There is no entry fee.

The 2026 jury comprises Christine Wilkinson (wildlife ecologist and National Geographic Explorer), Charlotte Vermeulen (emeritus biologist at ARTIS Amsterdam Zoo), Erin Ranney (wildlife cinematographer with credits at Nat Geo, Disney+, BBC), Noah Baars (Narwhal Rainbow Alliance founder), Nova West (filmmaker/photographer), and Laura Pennafort (BBC/Nat Geo cinematographer).

Eligibility is open to everyone — professional photographers, passionate amateurs, students. There is no LGBTQ+ identity requirement for the photographer. Each participant submits a maximum of 3 photos via WeTransfer to info@narwhalrainbowalliance.com, with an explanatory paragraph describing the work's relevance to queer nature. The 2026 deadline was extended to June 10; results announced late July.

calls.title: The Shape of a Moment
calls.description: International call exploring photography's ability to capture fleeting moments. Gold Award winner receives a solo exhibition. Exhibitions in Argentina and Los Angeles. Juror: Gary Hershorn (Reuters).
calls.ai: AI editing OK, fully generated not accepted
calls.summary: Capturing fleeting moments. Gold Award winner receives solo exhibition. Juror: Gary Hershorn (Reuters).
prose: Exposure Photo Gallery is a photography gallery operating across two continents — its primary venue at Urquiza 739 in Río Tercero, Córdoba, Argentina, with a secondary venue in Buena Park, California (Exposure Los Angeles). "The Shape of a Moment" is the gallery's open call exploring photography's capacity to capture instants that reveal something essential through light, emotion, and time.

The Gold Award winner receives $500 cash and a solo exhibition at the Argentina gallery. Silver and Bronze awards recognize artistic quality without cash; ten Honorable Mentions appear as printed works in the physical exhibition; further selections are shown digitally. Special recognitions are reserved for photographers based in Córdoba Province. All recognized artists receive digital diplomas, and selected works are reproduced in an official exhibition book (print-on-demand).
The 2026 cycle is juried by Gary Hershorn, a 29-year Reuters editor and Getty Images contributor who has covered 17 Olympic Games and is the author of New York Celestial.

Entry fees are tiered by image count: $5 for 1 photo, $10 for 3, $15 for 6, $20 for 12. Unlimited submissions are permitted per applicant. AI-edited work is accepted; fully AI-generated work is not. Submissions are JPEG, max 2,000 pixels on the longest side. The 2026 deadline is June 30 at 11:59 PM PST; results announced August 3.

calls.title: Chromatic Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: International color photography competition across 20 categories including Aerial, Architecture, Fine Art, Landscape, Nature, Portrait, and Street. Separate Professional and Amateur divisions.
calls.summary: International color competition across 20 categories. Separate Professional and Amateur divisions.
prose: Chromatic Photography Awards is the color counterpart to several long-running monochrome competitions — entries must be in color, and black-and-white work is explicitly excluded. The 2026 cycle is the awards' 8th edition. Submissions are open to professionals and amateurs worldwide, with no age restriction stated on the official information page.

Entries can be made in 20 categories: Abstract, Architecture, Cityscapes, Conceptual, Culture, Environmental, Fashion and Beauty, Fine Art, Landscapes, Nature, Nudes, People, Photojournalism, Photomanipulation, Portrait, Sports, Still Life, Street, Travel, and Wildlife and Animal. Category winners receive Gold, Silver, or Bronze medals. The Professional and Amateur top winners receive $2,000 and $1,000 respectively, plus inclusion in the awards' Official Book. Honorable mentions receive certificates and badges.

Entry fees follow a tiered structure: $17 amateur / $22 professional per entry at the early deadline (July 19, 2026), rising to $22 amateur / $27 professional at final deadline (October 25, 2026). Winners are announced December 20, 2026.

The jury is composed of magazine editors, gallery curators, professional agents, and other industry-side professionals — names rotate per edition and are listed on the awards site. The competition does not state an AI policy on its information page, so applicants making AI-assisted work should email organizers before entering.

calls.title: PX3 Prix de la Photographie Paris 2026
calls.description: One of Europe's most prestigious photography awards. Categories include Analog, Architecture, Book, Fine Art, Nature, Portraiture, Press, and Advertising. Winners exhibited in Paris and internationally.
calls.summary: One of Europe's most prestigious awards. Categories from Analog to Advertising. Exhibited in Paris.
prose: PX3 (Prix de la Photographie Paris) is an international photography competition based in Paris, awarding work across eight categories: Analog, Architecture, Book, Fine Art, Nature, Portraiture, Press, and Advertising. The structure separates traditional editorial categories (Press, Portraiture) from medium-specific tracks (Analog, Book), giving applicants flexibility in how they position a series.
The main prize is €5,000, with category and subcategory recognitions stacking on top. Winners are exhibited at PX3's annual Paris showcase and featured in the prize's annual book and online archive.

The 2026 jury includes James Wellford (National Geographic), Steve McCurry (photographer), and Samuel Nja Kwa (Forbes Afrique), with the full jury list published on px3.fr. Entry fees range from €20 to €50 depending on category and submission tier. Eligibility is open to photographers 18 and over worldwide. The deadline is June 17, 2026; AI policy is not stated on the public submission page, so applicants making AI-assisted work should email organizers before entering.

calls.title: Camera Clara Photo Award 2026
calls.description: Award dedicated exclusively to photographers using large-format cameras. Rewards unpublished work presented as a coherent series of 10 images. Winner receives prize money plus exhibition production.
jury: Joséphine de Bodinat Moreno, Founder, Prix Camera Clara
Dominique de Font-Reaulx, President of the Jury
Héloïse Conésa, Curator, National Library of France
Marc Donnadieu, Art Critic & Independent Curator

Fabien Simode, Art Critic & Director, Maisons-Alfort Media Libraries
calls.summary: Exclusively for large-format camera photographers. Unpublished series of 10 images. Prize money + exhibition.
prose: Camera Clara is a French photography prize dedicated specifically to large-format photography. Founded in 2012 by Joséphine de Bodinat Moreno, it rewards an unpublished body of work made with a large-format camera, presented as a coherent series of 10 images. The €8,000 prize is paid by Joséphine de Bodinat Moreno and includes exhibition production support for the winner.

Submissions are free of charge. The award accepts only large-format work and excludes AI-generated images. Selection criteria emphasize coherence both in form and content, treating the series as the unit of evaluation rather than individual images — applicants are reviewed on whether the body of work holds together, not on whether any single image stands out.

The 2026 jury is unusually senior for a niche prize: Dominique de Font-Reaulx (Jury President), Aurélie Chauffert-Yvart (Artistic Director), Héloïse Conésa (Curator at the National Library of France), Marc Donnadieu (art critic and independent curator), Anne Lacoste (Director of the Institute for Photography of Hauts-de-France), Chantal Nedjib (communications consultant), Guillaume Piens (art historian and founder of Culture Squad Communication), Michel Poivert (Professor of Art History at Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne), and Fabien Simode (art critic and director of Maisons-Alfort Media Libraries), alongside founder Joséphine de Bodinat Moreno.
The 2026 deadline is midnight July 31; the jury meets during September 2026 to designate the winner. Applications are made through prixcameraclara.plateformecandidature.com.

calls.title: Tokyo International Foto Award 2026
calls.description: International photography competition introducing photographers to the creative community in Tokyo. Categories include Advertising, Architecture, Editorial, Fine Art, Nature, People, and Portfolio. Winners exhibited in Tokyo.
jury: Prof. William Snyder, Rochester Institute of Technology
calls.summary: International competition introducing photographers to Tokyo's creative community. Winners exhibited in Tokyo.
prose: Tokyo International Foto Awards (TIFA) is an annual photography competition that culminates in a winners' exhibition in Tokyo. The 2026 cycle is open to photographers aged 18 and over worldwide, with seven submission categories: Advertising, Architecture, Editorial, Fine Art, Nature, People, and Portfolio. Series entries accept 2 to 10 images sharing a common theme.

The main prize is €3,000 in cash, with category winners and honorable mentions receiving recognition badges and inclusion in TIFA's annual archive. Selected work is exhibited in Tokyo as part of a winners' showcase; specific gala details are published after results.

Submissions are reviewed by a six-member jury that includes Hideko Kataoka (photo editor and curator), Mariama Attah (curator), Kenro Izu (photographer), Susan Baraz (Lucie Foundation Co-Chair), Professor William Snyder (Rochester Institute of Technology), and Alfie Goodrich (Japanorama).

Entry fees are tiered between €15 and €50 depending on category and submission type. AI-generated work is accepted in a dedicated AI-Generated Images subcategory. The 2026 deadline is August 1, with results announced in September.

Special guest Estevan Oriol (The Oriol Vision category); jury announced 15 days before selection. Event September 25–27, 2026, during Milano Fashion Week. Official sponsor: Nikon Italia.

prose: Milano Photo Awards is an Italian photography contest and exhibition run by TheStreetSoup, with Nikon Italia as official sponsor. The 2026 edition runs September 25–27 at Via Maurizio Gonzaga 7 in Milan, scheduled to coincide with Milano Fashion Week. The exhibition format is a 4×3 meter Samsung LED wall for digital display of selected work, with the top three winners in each category also receiving printed and framed prints. The 2026 edition includes a tribute to Sebastião Salgado.

The total prize pool is €30,000 in cash plus Nikon hardware. There are eight competition categories: Street Photography, Portrait & Identity, Wildlife & Nature, Movement & Sport, Human Landscape, Documentary & Social Vision, Conceptual & Fine Art, and Fashion & Style. AI-generated work is not accepted.

Entry follows a tiered structure with separate access levels: Exhibition Open (€20, 2 photos, €500 first prize plus a Nikon backpack and printing), Exhibition Room 1 (€50, 5 photos, €1,000 first prize plus printing and gala access), Exhibition Room 2 (€80, 8–10 photos, €1,500 first prize plus printing and gala access), and the Oriol Vision Award (€50, 5 photos), curated separately by guest judge Estevan Oriol.
