calls.title: Seen / Unseen
calls.description: Photography exhibition exploring the visible and the implied — works that engage with what is shown, suggested, or hidden. Online curated exhibition with published catalog, social media and newsletter promotion, certificate of participation, and digital badge. First place receives a solo webpage exhibition. Open to photographers worldwide aged 18+. $1,000 total cash awards.
jury: Ann M. Jastrab, Executive Director, Center for Photographic Art
calls.summary: Online photography exhibition on the visible and the implied. Juror Ann M. Jastrab. $1,000 total awards.
prose: Decagon Gallery is an online curatorial platform that runs themed photography exhibitions with published catalogs and social distribution. "Seen / Unseen" is the gallery's open call for work that engages with the relationship between what is shown and what is implied — exploring presence, absence, suggestion, concealment, and the visual languages that point at things without quite revealing them.

The selection structure is online-first. Selected photographers are featured in a curated online exhibition with a published catalog distributed through Decagon's mailing list and social channels. All accepted artists receive a certificate of participation and a digital badge for portfolio use. The first-place winner additionally receives a solo webpage exhibition on the gallery site.
Cash awards total $1,000 across the top placements. The 2026 cycle is juried by Ann M. Jastrab. Eligibility is open to photographers worldwide aged 18 and over.
Entry fee is $25 per submission of up to 8 images. The 2026 deadline is July 8, with results announced July 21.

calls.title: Manifest Season 23 Photo-Solo Exhibit Proposals
calls.description: Open call for solo exhibition proposals at Manifest Creative Research Gallery during the 2026/27 season, coinciding with the FotoFocus Biennial in Cincinnati. Approximately one-third of seasonal programming is dedicated to solo exhibitions of original lens-based work. Each exhibiting artist receives a $100 honorarium plus a $1,000 Grand Jury Award for one jury-selected work. Open internationally to artists working in traditional or non-traditional photographic media.
calls.summary: Solo lens-based exhibition proposals at Manifest Gallery during the 2026/27 FotoFocus Biennial. $1,000 Grand Jury Award.
prose: Manifest Creative Research Gallery is a Cincinnati, Ohio nonprofit gallery (2727 Woodburn Ave, East Walnut Hills) founded in 2005. Manifest runs a year-round seasonal exhibition program with about one-third of programming dedicated to solo exhibitions; the photo-solo track specifically calls for lens-based bodies of work for solo presentation.

Season 23 (2026/27) is timed to coincide with FotoFocus Biennial, the regional Cincinnati photography festival running September 25 through October 23, 2026. Solo exhibitors thus benefit from the heightened visitor traffic and curatorial attention the biennial brings.

Each exhibiting artist receives a $100 cash honorarium. Beyond the honorarium, one work across the entire seasonal exhibition period receives a $1,000 Grand Jury Award. Selected solo exhibitors receive a free season publication, insurance coverage while on gallery premises, and presentation in Manifest's roughly 2,000-square-foot space with 11.5-foot walls and museum-grade track lighting.

Selection is layered: most group exhibits are juried by an anonymous panel of professional and academic advisors who pass recommendations to the gallery's curators for final selection. Eligibility is open globally — anyone can submit a proposal, with the gallery looking for a consistent and very strong body of work.
Application fee is $50 (non-refundable). The 2026 deadline is June 1, with notifications sent in early August.

calls.title: Solstice Magazine Issue 72 — Editorial Submissions
calls.description: Submit fashion and editorial photography for publication in Issue 72 of Solstice Magazine, a London-based fashion publication. First-round deadline May 18; second-round June 18 if space remains. Issue release June 21, 2026. Editorials must be unpublished. Send via PDF, Dropbox, or WeTransfer.
calls.summary: Fashion and editorial photography for Issue 72 of this London fashion magazine. Issue releases June 21, 2026.
prose: Solstice Magazine is a London-based independently-run fashion and beauty publication that publishes both digital and print editorials. Issue 72 publishes June 21, 2026.

Submission requirements are unusually specific. Fashion editorials must include at least 5 different outfit changes; beauty editorials at least 5 different hair/makeup looks. Each outfit or look must be represented by at least 3 finished, retouched photographs. All work must be high-resolution (minimum 3,000 pixels on the shortest side, 300 DPI), unpublished, exclusive to Solstice, and written in English.

The fee structure is unusual and worth understanding before submitting. Standard submissions are free, but Solstice imposes penalty fees: USD $280 for editorials with fewer than 5 outfits (if quality justifies an exception), USD $380 if a single brand appears in more than 2 outfits, USD $30 for credit amendment errors, USD $220 cancellation fee after a 48-hour acceptance window, and USD $280 for deletion of published work. The model pushes much of the production discipline onto the photographer.

Selected photographers and stylists receive publication credit and digital tear-sheets for their portfolios. Solstice does not provide complimentary print copies and does not pay photographers for submissions.

Eligibility: models must be 18 or over; pornographic or graphic violent content is not accepted. The first-round deadline is 11:59 PM EDT on May 18, 2026; if space remains, a second round runs through June 18.

calls.title: Photoworks Guest Issue 4 — Rituals
calls.description: Fourth edition of Photoworks Guest, a community photo zine published by Photoworks SF in San Francisco. Theme: Rituals — exploring the relationship between rituals and photography. Examples include daily commutes, ceremonies, holiday traditions, cooking, or anything you do every day. Selected work appears in the print magazine; longer features with interviews are also available for projects that fit the theme.
calls.summary: Community photo zine from Photoworks SF. Theme: Rituals. Free print publication, 1–3 images per submission.
prose: Photoworks SF is a San Francisco community photography center offering film developing, custom printing, framing, and educational programs. Photoworks Guest is the center's recurring zine series, with each issue centered on a theme drawn from open-call submissions. Issue 4 is themed "Rituals" — exploring the relationship between rituals and photography.

The brief is unusually accessible: rituals interpreted broadly. Examples cited include daily commutes, ceremonies, holiday traditions, cooking, or anything done with regularity. The framing favors small everyday gestures over high-ceremony moments.

Selected photographers appear in the printed Photoworks Guest zine. Longer features with photographer interviews are also available for projects that fit the theme more substantively — a two-tier publication structure where some submissions get full feature treatment and others appear as single-image contributions.
Submission is free of charge. Each photographer submits 1 to 3 images via Google Form. Eligibility is open globally — Photoworks Guest accepts submissions beyond their San Francisco community.
The Issue 4 deadline is May 15, 2026; publication in June 2026.

calls.title: Łódź Photo-Match 2026 Portfolio Review
calls.description: Two-day portfolio review at Fotofestiwal in Łódź, June 19–20, 2026. Twenty selected photographers each get up to four one-on-one meetings with European curators, editors, and gallery directors based on a matching process. Day 1 features public presentations; Day 2 holds private reviews at Alfred Biedermann's Palace. Open internationally, including artistic duos. Physical attendance required. Reviewers from Spain, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, UK, Finland, Netherlands, Sweden, Austria, and Chile.
calls.summary: Free two-day portfolio review at Fotofestiwal Łódź. Twenty photographers meet 20 European curators.
prose: Łódź Photo-Match is the portfolio review program of Fotofestiwal, the major Polish photography festival in Łódź. The 2026 Photo-Match runs June 19–20, 2026 across two venues: Day 1 at Art_Inkubator and Day 2 at Alfred Biedermann's Palace.

The structure is matched-meeting rather than open networking. Twenty selected photographers are paired with 20 European curators, editors, and gallery directors based on a matching process. Each selected photographer receives up to four one-on-one meetings on Day 2. Day 1 features public presentations.

Reviewers come from across Europe — Spain, Italy, Lithuania, Poland, UK, Finland, Netherlands, Sweden, Austria — plus Chile. The 2026 reviewer panel includes curators Anna Surroca, Irene Monteagudo, Arianna Rinaldo, Kristyna Müller, Witek Orski, photo editor Emma Bowkett, and Fotofestiwal Director Tomasz Gutkowski.

The program is free of charge and co-financed by the European Union's Creative Europe program with support from multiple cultural institutions across Europe. Eligibility is open to photographers of any nationality, including artistic duos. Multiple project submissions are allowed, and past applicants may resubmit without restriction.

Selection is anonymous: 3 Fotofestiwal collective members evaluate applications using only the images and project descriptions, without identifying information. Submissions accept 10 photographs in JPG/PNG format (max 10 MB total) submitted via Google Form and email to portfolio@fotofestiwal.com. The 2026 deadline is May 15, 2026; selected artists announced by May 19. Physical attendance in Łódź is required.

calls.title: No-Type Monograph No. 01
calls.description: Open call from No-Type, an independent Chicago photography publisher, for the inaugural artist monograph. The selected photographer receives a fully-funded monograph dedicated entirely to their work — editing, design, printing, and marketing all covered, plus 20% of the printed edition. A shortlist of six artists will be interviewed on No-Type's website, and all applicants are considered for inclusion in an Editor's Choice issue of the magazine. Open to lens-based projects of any subject, genre, or process; submissions must be a cohesive body of work ready for book form.
calls.summary: Fully-funded monograph publication from independent Chicago photo publisher No-Type. Shortlist gets website interviews.
prose: No-Type is a Chicago-based independent photography publisher. Monograph No. 01 is the publisher's inaugural monograph publishing program — an open call for lens-based artists to submit a cohesive photographic project for development into a full artist monograph.

The brief is open: photographic projects of any subject, genre, or process, presented as a cohesive and ambitious body of work ready to be developed into book form. Selection prioritizes work that has the structural depth to sustain a full monograph rather than a strong serial portfolio.

One artist is selected. The selected artist receives full monograph publication by No-Type, with all production costs covered — editing, design, printing, and marketing — plus 20% of the total edition to sell and distribute at the artist's discretion. The selected artist also receives consideration for additional features in the magazine and across No-Type's digital platforms.
Six finalists are selected for published interviews on the No-Type site. All submitting artists are also considered for inclusion in an Editor's Choice issue of the magazine.
Eligibility is open to lens-based artists. Submission fee is $20. Submissions go through Typeform; the deadline is May 31, 2026, with the shortlist announced June 8 and final selection June 15.

calls.title: Photo Shoot 2026
calls.description: Open call from Black Box Gallery in Portland, OR. 26 photographs selected for in-gallery exhibition (July 1–25, 2026); 50 additional photographs included in an online gallery annex. All 76 selected works featured in a printed Blurb catalog. Free printing, matting, and framing for selected works. 50% commission to gallery on sales. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide. Juried by Todd Johnson (founder/director of Black Box Gallery, MFA San Francisco Art Institute).
jury: Todd Johnson, Founder & Director, Black Box Gallery
calls.summary: Black Box Gallery Portland open theme show. 26 prints exhibited + 50 online + Blurb catalog. Free framing.
prose: Photo Shoot is Black Box Gallery's open-theme themed exhibition — the gallery's catch-all call where any photographic style or genre is welcome. Black Box is a Portland, Oregon photography gallery directed by Todd Johnson, who holds an MFA in Photography from the San Francisco Art Institute and serves as juror for the gallery's calls.

The selection structure is two-part: 26 photographs are chosen for the physical gallery exhibition, with 50 additional photographs included in an online gallery annex. All 76 selected works are reproduced in a printed Blurb catalog.

What's unusual: the gallery covers all printing, matting, and framing for selected work. Archival printing is on Epson Premium Luster Photo paper. After the exhibition closes, prints are retained in the gallery's flat files for further promotion.

Entry fee is $40 per submission of up to 5 photos. Submissions are JPEG, max 1200 pixels, 72 PPI, under 5MB. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Sales terms: 50% gallery commission, photographer retains all rights. The exhibition runs July 1–25, 2026; the submission deadline was extended to June 16, 2026.

calls.title: SCAN Tarragona — Full Contact Award 2026
calls.description: Open call from SCAN, the international photography festival organized by Tarragona City Council. 12 projects selected for Full Contact, a professional meeting space at Teatret del Port in El Serrallo, Tarragona on October 17, 2026. From these 12, one artist receives the Full Contact Award: a solo exhibition in 2027 as part of SCAN's official program plus €900 fee for exhibition and communication rights. Open to EU and UK residents of legal age. Submit any photo series that tells a story, on any subject. Maximum 16 photographs from a single series.
calls.summary: Free open call from SCAN Tarragona. 12 projects to Full Contact meeting; winner gets 2027 solo show + €900.
prose: SCAN is the international photography festival organized by Tarragona City Council, in Catalonia. Full Contact is its portfolio review and professional meeting day, held inside the festival program. The 2026 edition takes place October 17 at Teatret del Port in El Serrallo, Tarragona's historic fishing quarter.

Twelve projects are selected for Full Contact. Each selected artist gets a table to present work to 20+ art-world professionals — curators, editors, gallerists, festival directors. Selected participation is fully covered: opening-night accommodation at the official hotel, formal invitations to SCAN and Full Contact opening events, the welcome dinner on Friday October 16, and a professional lunch on Saturday October 17.

From the twelve, one artist receives the Full Contact Award: a solo exhibition in 2027 as part of SCAN's official program plus €900 (taxes included) for exhibition and communication rights. SCAN provides advisory support within available resources to develop the show.

Eligibility is restricted to legal-age residents of any European Union country or the United Kingdom. Submissions are accepted in Catalan, Spanish, and English. Any photo series that tells a story is eligible — open subject. Selection criteria foreground conceptual strength, distinctive voice, aesthetic coherence, and narrative construction.

Each application includes biography, project title, a 300-word project description, up to 16 JPG photographs (minimum 2,000px on the shortest side, ZIP under 30 MB), and an optional supplementary PDF. The 2026 jury is Ada Sbriccoli and Arola Valls Bofill — both independent curators, researchers, and lecturers. The decision is final. Application is free; deadline May 10, 2026, 11:59 PM.

calls.title: Transforming Landscapes — 20/20 Photo Festival 2026
calls.description: International juried exhibition for analog photographers exploring how American landscapes have evolved over 250 years — physical, technological, societal, political, scientific, and artistic. Open exclusively to work made with analog photographic methods including film types (color negative, black-and-white, slide, instant) and formats (35mm, 120, 4×5 large format, 110, 126). Selected works exhibited at Cherry Street Pier during the 20/20 Photo Festival in Philadelphia, September 10–13, 2026. Juried by photographer Andrew Piccone.
calls.summary: Analog-only juried festival exhibition exploring 250 years of American landscapes. Cherry Street Pier, Philadelphia. Juror: Andrew Piccone.
prose: The 20/20 Photo Festival is a Philadelphia photography festival held at Cherry Street Pier on the Delaware River. The 2026 cycle is themed "Transforming Landscapes," tied to the United States' 250th anniversary year — the brief invites work that engages with the evolution of the American landscape across physical terrain, technological change, social and political shifts, scientific knowledge, and artistic expression.

The competition is restricted to analog photography. Eligible film types include color negative, black-and-white, slide, and instant film. Eligible formats include 35mm, 120 medium format, 4×5 large format, 110, and 126. Digital capture is not accepted; the festival positions itself specifically as an exhibition for film-based work.

Cash prizes: $500 first place, $250 second, $150 third. Honorable Mentions receive a selection of local Philadelphia photography goods. Selected work is exhibited at Cherry Street Pier during the festival, September 10–13, 2026, with a feature spotlight at the festival's photo book fair on September 12.

The 2026 cycle is juried by Andrew Piccone, a Philadelphia-based photographer. Submissions are made through Google Form. Eligibility is open internationally to photographers working in analog processes. The 2026 cycle accepts submissions May 1 through June 1, extended to June 8.

calls.title: Lens Work: Trees and Water
calls.description: Juried group exhibition exploring trees and water as subjects in contemporary photography — dynamic and diverse imagery, including 'magical and poetic pictures' celebrating visual composition and contemporary photographic technique. Selected work shown in physical gallery and online annex; included in printed catalog. Free printing, matting, and framing for accepted artists. 50/50 sales commission. Exhibition August 1–25, 2026 in Portland, OR. Juror: Todd Johnson, Black Box Gallery founder. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers.
calls.summary: Black Box Gallery juried exhibition exploring trees and water. Free printing/framing. Portland, OR. Juror: Todd Johnson.
jury: Todd Johnson, Founder, Black Box Gallery
prose: Black Box Gallery is a Portland, Oregon photography gallery directed by Todd Johnson, who holds an MFA in Photography from the San Francisco Art Institute and serves as juror for the gallery's calls. "Lens Work: Trees and Water" is the gallery's themed call for 2026, focused on contemporary photography of trees and water — both as separate subjects and in combination.

The selection structure is two-part: 26 photographs are chosen for the physical gallery exhibition, with 50 additional photographs included in an online gallery annex. All 76 selected works are reproduced in a purchasable catalog.

What's unusual: the gallery covers all printing, matting, and framing for selected work. Prints are displayed in 18×24 inch black frames with white mats. After the exhibition closes, prints are retained in the gallery's flat files for two years for future promotion and sales.

Entry fee is $40 per submission of up to 5 photos. Eligibility is open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Sales terms: 50% gallery commission, photographer retains copyright and approves all sales. The exhibition runs August 1–25, 2026; submission deadline is July 10, 2026.

calls.title: The Midnight Garden
calls.description: Four-day NYC pop-up exhibition curated by Jessica Libor (founder/director of Era Contemporary). Theme centers on cultivation, transformation, and unseen processes of growth — both in nature and within ourselves — exploring blooming, decay, renewal, and the balance between control and wildness. Open to U.S.-based visual artists in all 2D and 3D media including photography. Exhibition August 20–23, 2026 at 61 Atlantic Ave, Brooklyn. Selected artists featured in New Visionary Magazine and listed on Artsy through Warnes Contemporary gallery.
calls.summary: NYC pop-up curated by Jessica Libor on cultivation, transformation, and growth. Magazine feature + Artsy listing via Warnes Contemporary.
jury: Jessica Libor, Founder & Director, Era Contemporary
prose: Visionary Art Collective (VAC) is an artist-led platform that runs themed exhibitions and publishes New Visionary Magazine. "The Midnight Garden" is a four-day NYC pop-up exhibition curated by Jessica Libor, the Philadelphia-based artist and founder of Era Contemporary.

The brief centers on cultivation, transformation, and unseen processes of growth — both in nature and within ourselves — exploring the garden as a metaphor for creative practice, cycles of renewal, and the duality between control and wildness. The themes invite both literal botanical work and conceptual interpretation.

The exhibition runs August 20–23, 2026 at 61 Atlantic Ave, a ground-level gallery in Brooklyn. A virtual component runs alongside the physical pop-up for 4 to 6 weeks on the VAC website. Selected artists are also featured in New Visionary Magazine and listed on Artsy through Warnes Contemporary gallery — meaning selection produces both physical exhibition placement and ongoing online representation.

Eligibility is open to U.S.-based visual artists at all career levels. Accepted media span both 2D and 3D: painting, drawing, photography, digital, prints, fiber art, collage, mixed media, sculpture, ceramics, and installation. Film and video are excluded.
Entry fees are tiered by submission size: $25 for 1–2 images, $30 for 3–4, $35 for 5–6. The 2026 deadline is May 31.

calls.title: 2nd Street Photo Festival 2026
calls.description: International street photography open call for the 2nd edition, hosted at the Athens School of Fine Arts. Submit 1–3 high-resolution photographs (minimum 4000 px on the long side, JPG or TIFF) via WeTransfer or cloud service to contest@streetphotofestival.gr, accompanied by a Word document with contact info, country, Instagram and website. Selected photographers contribute €50 toward festival expenses. Selected works exhibited at Athens School of Fine Arts December 12–20, 2026. All selected photographers receive a Certificate of Participation and Achievement.
calls.summary: Street photography call for Athens festival exhibition Dec 12–20. Free entry; €400/€300/€200 prizes; €50 if selected.
prose: The Street Photo Festival Athens is a Greek street photography festival, with the 2026 edition the festival's 2nd. The festival is hosted at the Athens School of Fine Arts, with the open-call exhibition running December 12 through 20, 2026.

The submission model is free to apply, contribute-only-on-selection: the call accepts entries at no cost, but selected photographers contribute €50 toward festival expenses (printing, installation, hosting). Cash prizes: €400 first place, €300 second, €200 third. All selected photographers receive a Certificate of Participation and Achievement.

The 2026 jury comprises Aude Delannoy Dib (French street photographer based in the UAE), Brad Jones (NYC-based street photographer), and Eleni Mouzakiti (curator and photographer, Artistic Director of House of Lucie Athens) — three perspectives spanning continents and roles.

Eligibility is open internationally. Each photographer submits 1 to 3 original photographs in high resolution: minimum 4000 pixels on the long side, in JPG or TIFF at 240–300 dpi. Submissions go via WeTransfer or cloud service to contest@streetphotofestival.gr, with a Word document containing contact information, country, Instagram, and website. Festival retains the right to use selected images for festival promotion (with photographer credit). The 2026 deadline is May 31.

calls.title: XXIV Eurostars Grand Marina Photography Award — Josep Juanpere 2026
calls.description: 24th edition of this international photography prize organized by Hotusa Group in Barcelona. 2026 theme: Barcelona, World Capital of Architecture, marking the city's UNESCO designation. Submit up to three photographic triptychs that form a cohesive visual narrative on the city's architectural identity. Named in memory of architect Josep Juanpere (1953–2025), designer of Hotel Grand Marina. First prize: €5,000 + trophy. Second prize: €3,000 + trophy. Eight finalists receive trophies and free stays at Eurostars hotels.
calls.summary: 24th edition. Theme: Barcelona, World Capital of Architecture. €5,000 first prize. Submit photographic triptychs.

calls.title: Wassaic Project 2027 Artist Residency
calls.description: 2–4 week residency at the Wassaic Project in the foothills of the Berkshires, two hours north of NYC. Summer sessions (3–4 weeks, June–September) take place in the Luther Barn studio building; winter sessions (2–4 weeks, January–March) in Maxon Mills. Open to individual artists, collaborative teams, and groups in any medium — photography eligible alongside painting, sculpture, installation, sound, video, and writing. Includes private bedroom in shared house, dedicated studio space (200–300 sq ft summer; ~100 sq ft winter), access to print shop and wood shop, studio visits with critics, and group programming. calls.summary: 1–4 week summer or winter residency in upstate NY. Photography eligible. Sliding-scale fee $0–$900; private bedroom + studio.

prose: The Wassaic Project is a rural artist residency in the foothills of the Berkshires, two hours north of New York City in the small Hudson Valley hamlet of Wassaic. The 2027 program offers two seasonal tracks: summer sessions (3 to 4 weeks, June through September) in the Luther Barn studio building, and winter sessions (2 to 4 weeks, January through March) in the historic Maxon Mills.

Residents receive a private bedroom in a shared house with common spaces, a dedicated studio (200–300 square feet in summer; approximately 100 square feet in winter), 24-hour studio access, and use of the campus print shop and wood shop. Programming includes studio visits with visiting critics and curators, group critiques, and one-on-one studio visits.

Eligibility is unusually broad: individual artists, collaborative teams, groups of two or more, and family-residency applicants are all welcome. Media accepted include photography alongside painting, sculpture, installation, sound, video, and writing.

Cost is on a need-blind sliding scale from $0 to $900 per session, covering most program costs. The application fee is $25 (waivable for financial hardship). Selection is by a panel including the three Wassaic Project Co-Directors (Eve Biddle, Bowie Zunino, Jeff Barnett-Winsby), the Director of Artistic Programming (Will Hutnick), and the Assistant Director of Exhibitions and Residency (Danielle Klebes). The 2027 cycle deadline is July 1, 2026; notifications by early October.

calls.title: RAK Art Festival 2027 — Lost in Translation
calls.description: 14th edition of the Ras Al Khaimah Art Festival, organized by the Sheikh Saud bin Saqr Al Qasimi Foundation for Policy Research at the Al Jazeera Al Hamra Heritage Village in the UAE. Theme: Lost in Translation — exploring displacement, migration, cultural adaptation, and the search for belonging across linguistic and cultural boundaries. Open to international artists across four categories: Emerging Artists, Established Artists, Filmmakers, and Students (ages 6–19). All nationalities welcome. Photography eligible alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, installation, video art, and short film. Submit up to four artworks across two mediums maximum, with a 100-word artist statement and 200-word biography. Grand Jury Prize: AED 12,000 + trophy. Photography category prizes: AED 6,000 (1st) and AED 4,000 (2nd). Notifications: July 30, 2026; festival opens January 22, 2027.
calls.location: Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates
calls.summary: 14th edition Ras Al Khaimah Art Festival in UAE. Free entry. AED 12,000 Grand Jury Prize + AED 4,000–6,000 photography category prizes.
jury: Faisal Alrais, Emirati Conceptual Artist & Photographer
Rose-Marie Ferré, Associate Professor of Art History, Sorbonne University
prose: The RAK Art Festival is held annually at the Al Jazeera Al Hamra Heritage Village in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates — a restored coastal village that serves as the festival's permanent venue. The 2027 edition marks the festival's 14th year (founded 2013), organized by the Sheikh Saud bin Saqr Al Qasimi Foundation for Policy Research.

The 2027 theme is "Lost in Translation," exploring displacement, migration, cultural adaptation, and the search for belonging across linguistic and cultural boundaries. The brief draws on the experience of being in between languages, cultures, and identities.

The festival accepts work across four eligibility categories: Emerging Artists, Established Artists (minimum two solo exhibitions), Filmmakers, and Students aged 6 to 19. Eligible media include photography, painting and drawing, sculpture and installation, video art, and short films. Each applicant submits up to four artworks total, with no more than two per medium across no more than two mediums.

Cash awards are denominated in UAE dirham. The Grand Jury Prize is AED 12,000 plus a trophy. Photography, Painting, and Drawing category awards are AED 6,000 (1st) and AED 4,000 (2nd). Sculpture/Installation, Video Art, and short film categories carry AED 6,000 awards. Best Student Artwork prizes are AED 2,000 per age category. Submission is free of charge. Selection is overseen by curator Sharon Toval and Festival Director Suqrat Bin Bisher. The 2026 deadline is June 5; results announced July 30, 2026; festival opens January 22, 2027.

calls.title: FiiLTHY GLO Issue 5 — SONDER
calls.description: Independent zine for the strange and unusual seeking work for Issue 5 — SONDER, exploring the intricately layered, sparsely noticed connections that intertwine us across society. Photography accepted alongside painting, collage, mixed media, digital art, sculpture, comic strips, prose, and short stories. Submit 1–5 original works related to the theme. Visual works should be cleanly presented (well-lit, minimal background); writing capped at 900 words per piece. Files named ArtistName_Title_Year. Submit via Google Form linked on the submissions page.
calls.summary: Indie zine for the strange and unusual. Issue 5 theme: SONDER. Photography accepted. Free, worldwide.
prose: FiiLTHY GLO is an independent zine for work in the strange and unusual register, drawing from across visual art and writing. Issue 5 is themed "SONDER" — the constructed word for the realization that every passerby is living a life as vivid and complex as one's own. The brief asks for work that engages with the layered, sparsely noticed connections that intertwine people across society.

Submissions are interdisciplinary: photography is accepted alongside painting, collage, mixed media, digital art, sculpture, comic strips, prose, opinion writing, and short stories. Each artist may submit 1 to 5 original works. Visual works should be cleanly presented — well-lit, minimal background clutter. Writing is capped at 900 words per piece, submitted as PDF.

Filenames follow the format ArtistName_Title_Year. Submissions are made via a Google Form linked on the FiiLTHY GLO submissions page. There is no submission fee, and AI-generated work is not accepted. Eligibility requires applicants to be 18 years or older and to submit original work only.

The Issue 5 deadline is June 20, 2026. The zine does not publicly specify what selected contributors receive — applicants should email the zine directly to confirm contributor copies, payment, and other compensation details before submitting.

calls.title: Stanley Greene Foundation Emerging Photographers Grant 2026–2027
calls.description: Annual grant from the Stanley Greene Foundation providing a $10,000 award to emerging visual storytellers at the beginning of their careers to develop impactful visual narratives. The program places particular emphasis on photographers from underserved and diverse communities, expanding access to resources and opportunities to bring their stories to life. Award disbursed in two parts: $8,000 upon award and $2,000 upon submission of final materials. Application requires biography (max 1,500 characters), project description (max 2,000 characters), project proposal (max 3,000 characters), and up to 25 images (72 dpi JPG, minimum 1,500 pixels long dimension, sRGB). Submissions reviewed by three Foundation board members in two rounds. Recipients must provide 15 final digital images and a report detailing fund usage; these materials become part of the Foundation's collection. Open to applicants 18+; current students not eligible (graduating before announcement may apply). Honoring the legacy of war photographer and Noor Images co-founder Stanley Greene.
calls.summary: $10,000 grant for emerging visual storytellers, with emphasis on underserved and diverse communities. Honors Stanley Greene's legacy.
jury: Three members of the Stanley Greene Foundation Board of Directors
prose: The Stanley Greene Foundation Emerging Photographers Grant honors war photographer Stanley Greene, a co-founder of Noor Images who covered conflict zones from Chechnya through West Africa. The Foundation administers the grant in his name, with explicit emphasis on supporting visual storytellers from underserved and diverse communities at the beginning of their careers.

The grant is $10,000, paid in two installments: $8,000 upon award and $2,000 upon completion of the project, contingent on submission of 15 final digital images and a written report detailing how the funds were used. The completion materials become part of the Foundation's archive. The two-stage payment is designed to ensure projects are actually carried through.

Eligibility requires applicants to be 18 or older and not currently enrolled as students at the time of submission, though those graduating before the decision date may apply. One proposal per person; collaborators are accepted. AI-generated imagery is not permitted in the work samples.

Applications are made through Picter and require a biography (up to 1,500 characters), project description (up to 2,000 characters), project proposal (up to 3,000 characters), and up to 25 images at 72 dpi JPG, sRGB, minimum 1,500 pixels on the long dimension. Selection is by a three-member jury drawn from the Stanley Greene Foundation Board, which meets twice — first for finalists, then for the final decision. Applications open May 1, 2026 and close July 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM EDT. Winners announced August 10, 2026.

calls.title: Quinn Emanuel Los Angeles Artist-in-Residence 2026
calls.description: Four-month studio residency at Quinn Emanuel's Los Angeles office for emerging and mid-career artists working in any discipline, including photography. The selected artist receives $5,000 per month for four months ($20,000 total) plus an art materials allowance of up to $1,500. The residency runs September–December 2026, followed by a one-month exhibition. The studio is located within the Quinn Emanuel LA office with 24/7 keycard access, parking, and full firm support. At least one work from the residency will be incorporated into the firm's permanent collection. Open to artists living in greater Los Angeles only; international applicants accepted if they secure their own visas. Preference given to underrepresented artists in early/mid-career stages. Submit a CV, an 8–10 image PDF portfolio, and a project proposal (one PDF, max 20MB) by 11:59pm PST May 14, 2026.
calls.summary: $20,000 + $1,500 materials. 4-month studio residency at Quinn Emanuel LA office. Open to all media including photography. Greater LA only.
jury: John Quinn, Founding Partner, Quinn Emanuel
prose: Quinn Emanuel is a major U.S. litigation law firm with 32 international offices. The Quinn Emanuel Artist-in-Residence program is run by the firm's Los Angeles office, with selection committee appointed by curator Alexis Hyde and firm name partner John Quinn — making this an unusually large and well-funded artist residency hosted by a corporate entity rather than an arts organization.

The 2026 residency is four months long, running September through December 2026, followed by a one-month exhibition. Each artist receives $5,000 per month for four months ($20,000 total cash) plus an art materials allowance of up to $1,500. The studio is located within the firm's LA office with 24/7 keycard access, parking included, and full firm support during the residency.

At least one work from the residency is incorporated into the firm's permanent collection. The structure is unusual: the firm's collection becomes the long-term home for residency-produced work, with sales opportunities also available through the post-residency exhibition.

Eligibility is restricted to artists living in greater Los Angeles. International artists are welcome but must secure their own visas. Preference is given to underrepresented artists in early-to-mid career stages, working in any discipline (photography, painting, sculpture, video, mixed media). No formal education requirement.
Application is free. Submissions consist of a CV, an 8–10 image PDF portfolio, and a project proposal — combined as a single PDF up to 20MB. The 2026 deadline is May 14 at 11:59 PM PST.

calls.title: Fundación Botín Art Grants 2026/2027
calls.description: Six annual visual arts grants of €23,000 each to support a research project or training in the visual arts. Photography is explicitly included alongside drawing, film/video/new media, mixed-media, painting, sculpture, and craft. Grants run for nine months and cover living expenses, travel, accommodation, studio rental, equipment, and production costs, plus medical insurance for recipients travelling outside their country of residence. One grant prioritizes Spanish artists or Spain residents (5+ years) under age 30 relocating abroad. Applications open to individual artists of any nationality; project must involve practical artistic work, not theoretical study. Online registration is followed by postal submission of up to 40 single-sided A4 pages including ID, CV (3 pages max), project description (10 pages max), and graphic documentation. Applications must be postmarked by Friday, May 8, 2026 (received until May 22 if postmarked by deadline). Results announced before July 17, 2026. Public exhibition at Centro Botín; possible acquisitions for the Foundation's Collection.
calls.summary: Six €23,000 nine-month research grants for international visual artists, photography included. Postal application postmarked by May 8.
prose: Fundación Botín was established in 1964 by Marcelino Botín Sanz de Sautuola and Carmen Yllera. The Visual Arts Grant program has run since 1993 and has supported more than 200 artists. Many former grantees are now internationally established.

The 2026/2027 edition awards six grants of €23,000 each. Funds cover living expenses, travel, equipment, studio rental, and production costs. Medical insurance is included for grantees who need to relocate internationally for the project. Payment runs in tranches: 45% upfront, 25% after the first trimester, 25% after the second, 5% on final report submission. The grant period is nine months.

Eligibility is open to artists of any nationality. One of the six grants is reserved for Spanish citizens or Spain residents (5+ years) under age 30 who are relocating abroad for their project. Projects must involve artistic creation and production, not theoretical research.

What's offered beyond the funding: public exhibition of resulting work at Centro Botín in Santander as part of Itinerarios — the program's annual exhibition, now in its 27th edition. Works may be acquired by Fundación Botín's Art Advisory Committee. Centro Botín retains first-show rights — works exhibit there before any other public presentation. Career tracking and ongoing support continues post-grant.

Applications combine an online registration form and a printed dossier sent by postal mail: ID copy, CV (max 3 pages), project title and 100-word summary, full project description (max 10 pages), graphic documentation on single-sided A4 color prints. Final report due November 12, 2027.
The 2026/2027 deadline is May 8, 2026 (postmark date); physical receipt accepted through May 22 if postmarked by May 8. Results announced before July 17, 2026.

calls.title: 24th DongGang International Photo Festival 2026 Open Call
calls.description: Open call for the 24th DongGang International Photo Festival, held July 17 – October 11, 2026 in Yeongwol, South Korea. Theme: 'The Silence that Shapes' — exploring how humans interpret nature and what we project onto landscapes versus what nature actually reveals. 15–20 artists are selected by the festival's curatorial team, including one 'Artist of the Year' who receives a solo exhibition with production support and travel/accommodation to attend the opening. Other selected artists receive outdoor exhibition space, production assistance, and inclusion in the festival catalog and press. Open to individual artists and collectives worldwide. Submit 8–12 images (JPEG or TIFF, minimum 4000 px on long side) plus CV and an artist statement under 400 words by email or WeTransfer. Notification by June 10, 2026.
calls.summary: 24th DIPF Yeongwol, South Korea. Theme: The Silence that Shapes. 15–20 artists selected. Artist of the Year solo show + travel.
prose: The DongGang International Photo Festival (DIPF) is held annually in Yeongwol, a town in South Korea's Gangwon Special Self-Governing Province along the DongGang River. The 2026 edition is the festival's 24th — DIPF is among the longer-running photography festivals in East Asia.

The 2026 dates run July 17 through October 11. The theme is "The Silence that Shapes" — the brief asks how humans interpret nature and what meaning we project onto landscapes versus the inherent silence of natural spaces. The framing favors work that engages with landscape, environment, and human perception rather than purely portrait or documentary.

Fifteen to twenty artists or collectives are selected from the open call. One is named "Artist of the Year" and receives a solo exhibition with production support, plus travel and accommodation funded by the festival. Other selected artists are exhibited in the main, outdoor, or screening venues with all production and printing handled by the organizers, plus inclusion in the festival catalog, website, and ongoing press coverage.

There is no entry fee. Eligibility is open globally to artists and collectives. Submissions are 8 to 12 photographs in JPEG or TIFF format at minimum 4,000 pixels on the long side, plus CV/biography, an artist statement under 400 characters, and contact information. Selection is by the festival's curatorial team. The 2026 deadline is June 1; results announced by June 10.

calls.title: Inner Landscapes
calls.description: Open call for Mental Health Awareness Month inviting lens-based artists to reflect on mental health and its relationship to everyday life. Considers how internal experiences are shaped by social, cultural, and environmental conditions and expressed through image-making. Welcomes work engaging with care, fatigue, stability, imbalance, support systems, and personal coping strategies. Selected works featured in a one-month online exhibition on Der Greif's homepage (May 15 – June 15, 2026), plus participation in small-group online critique sessions through Der Greif's Face-to-Face program. Selected artists may also be invited to submit their portfolio to Der Greif Studio. Voluntary €5 or €10 donation; financial assistance available on request.
calls.summary: Mental health theme. One-month online exhibition at Der Greif + roundtable critique session with peers. Voluntary fee, vouchers available.
prose: Inner Landscapes is a thematic open call from Der Greif, the Augsburg-based photography platform and print magazine, programmed for Mental Health Awareness Month. The theme asks lens-based artists to reflect on mental health and its relationship to everyday life — how internal experiences are shaped by social, cultural, and environmental conditions and how those experiences are expressed through image-making.

Concrete subjects encouraged: care, fatigue, stability, imbalance, support systems, personal coping strategies. Selection criteria favor artistic quality, conceptual clarity, openness to dialogue, and engagement with identity and community.

Selected works are featured in a one-month online exhibition on Der Greif's homepage running May 15 – June 15, 2026. Selected artists also participate in small-group online critique sessions through Der Greif's Face-to-Face program — peers plus Der Greif facilitators rather than a one-way jury verdict. Selection may also lead to an invitation to submit a portfolio to Der Greif Studio for sales and commission opportunities.

Eligibility is open globally with no experience-level restriction. Submissions are made through Picter, up to 10 images. The fee is voluntary — €5 or €10 suggested. Financial assistance is available on request: applicants in financial hardship can email voucher-special-2@dergreif.org for a 50–100% discount code.
The 2026 deadline is May 10.

calls.title: Drone Photo Awards 2026
calls.description: International aerial photography contest run by Siena Awards (sister event to Siena International Photo Awards). Nine categories: seven single-shot themes (Wedding, Nature, People, Urban, Animals, Abstract, Sport), Videos, and Series (5–9 images). Drone Photographer of the Year receives the Pangea Prize crystal trophy, €500 worth of photography equipment, and €400 toward Siena travel for the Awards Ceremony weekend. Selected work shown in the "Above Us Only Sky" group exhibition. Awards ceremony at Teatro dei Rinnovati on October 10, 2026 during the Siena Awards Festival.
calls.summary: Aerial photography contest. 9 categories, free entry. €500 gear + Pangea trophy + Siena exhibition. Ceremony Oct 10.
prose: The Drone Photo Awards is an annual international aerial photography contest run by Siena Awards, the umbrella organization that also runs the Siena International Photo Awards (SIPA) and Creative Photo Awards. The contest is held alongside the wider Siena Awards Festival in Siena, Italy.

Submissions are accepted across nine categories. Seven cover single-shot themes: Wedding, Nature, People, Urban, Animals, Abstract, and Sport. Two additional categories are Videos and Series (5 to 9 images). All categories require aerial-perspective work — drone, aircraft, or other non-ground vantage. AI-generated images are not accepted.

The overall Drone Photographer of the Year receives the Pangea Prize crystal trophy, €500 worth of photography equipment, and €400 toward travel to the Siena Awards Ceremony weekend. Selected work from across categories is exhibited in the "Above Us Only Sky" group exhibition at the festival, with the awards ceremony held at the historic Teatro dei Rinnovati on October 10, 2026.
Entry is free of charge. Eligibility is open globally. Submissions go through Siena Awards' contest portal at sienawards.com. The 2026 deadline was extended to June 15.

calls.title: F/262 Photography Awards 2026
calls.description: Single-image international photography awards from the inaugural F/262 Festival in Caldas da Rainha, Portugal (a UNESCO Creative City). Four award tracks: F/262 Photography Award (Gold/Silver/Bronze), ZÉ Creative Award, NextGen Award (emerging photographers), and the Thematic Award 'Moldar as Margens / Shaping Shores' tied to the festival's 2026 Water focus. Selected work is exhibited as outdoor public installations across the city during the festival (May 16 – September 13, 2026) and featured in the festival programme, press, and digital platforms. Ami Vitale, National Geographic Explorer & Nikon Ambassador
Daria Bonera, Founder & Director, DB Agency
Jacqueline Tobin, Author & Former Editor-in-Chief, Rangefinder
Carine Van Gerven, Founder, Lens op de Mens Festival
Matthew Jordan Smith, Nikon & KoyLab Ambassador

calls.summary: Single-image awards from the inaugural F/262 Festival in Caldas da Rainha, Portugal. Public outdoor installations + 2028 solo show.
prose: F/262 is the inaugural international photography festival of Caldas da Rainha, a UNESCO Creative City in Portugal — the festival's name combines the photographic 'F' (Focus, F-Stop, Family, Fun, Friendship, Freedom) with the city's area code, 262. The 2026 edition runs May 16 – September 13, with the year's curatorial focus on Water as ecological, cultural, and symbolic element. The festival is produced by Associação F/SOS – Fotografia, Solidariedade e Obras Sociais.

The Photography Awards run as a single-image competition across four parallel tracks. The main F/262 Photography Award gives Gold, Silver, and Bronze. The ZÉ Award is a Creative Award for unconventional approaches. The NextGen Award is reserved for emerging photographers. The Thematic Award 'Moldar as Margens / Shaping Shores' ties to the 2026 Water focus.

Selected work is shown as outdoor public installations across Caldas da Rainha during the festival run, with each selected photographer receiving a 50×70 cm fine-art print on Fuji paper, festival programme inclusion, and press/digital visibility. Gold takes a 2028 solo exhibition plus a €500 KOYLAB voucher, BlackRapid Sport X, Outex Camera Pro Kit, and 1-year SmartAlbums bundle. Silver and Bronze receive €400 and €300 vouchers respectively plus gear and software. Other category winners receive €250 vouchers and accessories.

Selection is by an independent international jury of photographers, editors, curators, and cultural leaders, including National Geographic and Pulitzer-winning practitioners. Judging is blind, on narrative strength, visual impact, originality, technical/conceptual coherence, and contemporary relevance.

Submission is through the festival website. Entry fee is €15 per image with no quantity limit; series are not accepted (each image is judged separately). Single Photos covers four thematic categories: Streets (the urban thoroughfare and its life), People (urban figures and portraiture), Spaces (the city as architectural and photographic subject), and Creative (images that challenge perceptions of the urban). Projects & Portfolios is for series-based work. A dedicated free track is open to photographers under 35.

prose: MVA Gallery — Modern Visual Arts — is a gallery at 35 E. Elizabeth Avenue in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, showing painting, printmaking, photography, sculpture, and more. The Essence of a Woman is its national themed exhibition for fall 2026.

The brief asks artists to explore in art the essence of a woman — her physical, psychological, and spiritual characteristics. That can mean a simple portrait of a woman in tranquil repose or a complex image of her actively performing personal and professional roles; she can reveal vulnerability or strength. Environmental portraits showing an individual in her surroundings are explicitly welcomed.
Accepted media span painting, watercolor, printmaking, mixed media, digital, pastel, encaustic, sculpture, fiber, drawing, and photography.

The exhibition runs October 10 through November 7, 2026 at the gallery. Original work in any visual medium is welcome, including photography, printmaking, painting, sculpture, fibre art, ceramics, mixed media and digital art, and the exhibition seeks a diverse range of voices, perspectives and techniques. Eligible artists must be a US military veteran of any branch, active duty, reserve or National Guard, a military family member, or a civilian artist whose work addresses military or veteran themes; entrants must reside in the continental US. Up to three pieces may be submitted and all three may be selected. Two-dimensional work must be framed and wired for hanging (no sawtooth hangers). Accepted work is dropped off October 26–27 or shipped to arrive by October 26, with an artists' reception on November 14. Accepted images are also shown in a concurrent online exhibit.
calls.summary: First veteran art exhibition at a Frederick, MD non-profit gallery — open to veterans, military families and service-themed work.

calls.title: 51st Juried Annual Exhibition
calls.description: The Miller Art Museum in Sturgeon Bay opens its 51st Juried Annual, the Door County institution’s long-running survey of two-dimensional work by artists living in Wisconsin. It is open to artists 18 and over at every career stage, from emerging to established professional, and accepts original hangable 2D work in any media made within the past two years — photography very much included; the 2026 prospectus cover pairs Nika McKagen’s silver gelatin print with an oil painting. A panel of jurors reviews projected digital entries, and $1,950 in cash awards is presented at the opening reception on September 18: the Gerhard Miller Award of Excellence ($500), three Special Merit Awards ($250 each), three Juror’s Choice Awards ($200 each) and the Bonnie Hartmann Award for Outstanding Creativity ($100). calls.title: Día de Muertos 2026 — Remembering Is Resistance
calls.description: For its 2026 Día de Muertos exhibition, Recordar es Resistir / Remembering Is Resistance, Longmont’s Firehouse Art Center pairs artists with community members affected by US immigration policy so that each work carries a real story, told safely and anonymously. Selected artists meet their partner between August 24 and October 1 and translate that person’s words and experience into a piece for the Main Gallery, where the show sits as both reflection and provocation. Accepted mediums include photography, digital art, painting, drawing, collage, mixed media, text-based work, sculpture, installation, fibre and touchable or interactive work. The centre asks for practices that confront, reflect on or challenge political realities, global or deeply personal, and states plainly that credentials matter less than passion and messaging. Applicants send a single PDF holding a 200-word bio, a 200-word statement and five images. There is no entry fee. The call is addressed to artists in the Longmont area aged 18 and over, and work is hand-delivered on October 5 and 6. Community members need no paperwork and are compensated for their time; translators are provided for anyone who prefers to apply or work in another language. The Firehouse waives its commission entirely and splits any sale equally between artist and community member. The exhibition runs October 9 to November 1, 2026, opening with a reception on October 9.
calls.summary: Longmont art centre pairs artists with community members affected by immigration policy. Free to enter, sales split 50/50.

calls.title: Lines & Layers

prose: Inspection Pit is a not-for-profit contemporary art space in West Sussex, housed in a converted barn that once served as a garage for vintage cars — the sunken inspection pit in its floor gave the organisation its name. It sits beside a working farm near the South Downs and presents three exhibitions a year, one of which is reserved for its artist resident.

The 2027 residency runs from 30 January to 27 February 2027. The selected artist stays on site for up to one month in private accommodation, free of charge, with a dedicated studio for independent work and a bicycle available for use in the local area. A £500 bursary is paid at the start of the residency to help with personal expenses. The artist provides their own food and studio materials and covers travel, transportation and day-to-day living costs.

Approximately six months after the residency ends, the resident may be invited to present a body of work in a solo exhibition at the space. This is a real pathway rather than a nominal one: the 2025 resident Danilo Zocatelli, who completed an MA in Photography at the Royal College of Art, showed his photography and video project VIADO at Inspection Pit in May 2026.

The call is worded openly, for "artists" across the visual and creative arts, without naming individual media. Photographers should read that as an invitation rather than a hedge: the space gave Zocatelli his solo show, and its 2023 exhibition SAHAR was made with Sirkhane Darkroom, the photography workshop working with children in southeast Turkey. No age or residence restriction is published, and there is no application fee.

To apply, download the application form from the residency page and email it, with a 150-word artist statement, a digital portfolio of up to six images, and two character references, to inspectionpit.uk@gmail.com. The deadline is 5 August 2026. Artists selected for interview are notified by 21 August 2026, interviews take place on 1 September, and the 2027 resident is notified by 4 September 2026.

calls.title: SALTPRINT Volume 01 — From Where You Stand
calls.description: First volume of SALTPRINT, an independent print photography zine and archive founded, edited and designed single-handedly by photographer and designer Petra Zegnal in Zagreb, and published every two months from open calls for photographs made across Europe. The theme From Where You Stand is about point of view — literal, emotional, political, personal or poetic: a window, a street, a daily walk, a workplace, a corner of Europe. The editor is looking for images that feel observed rather than forced, and states plainly that this is not about finding the most dramatic location. Submit one photograph, taken anywhere in Europe though you need not live there; digital or film, black and white or colour, street, documentary, landscape or portrait, shot on a camera or a phone. Selection is on connection to the theme, visual strength, atmosphere and originality rather than technical perfection, and beginners, students, self-taught and previously unpublished photographers are explicitly welcome. Three featured photographers per volume are also invited to a short written interview and receive a print copy; other selected photographers receive a digital copy. Free to enter, no payment for Volume 01, and photographers keep full copyright. Deadline 13 September 23:59 CET, selections by 30 September, publication October 2026.

calls.title: Fotograf Zone Festival — International Open Call
calls.description: Open call for photographic projects to be exhibited on poster panels in the busy concourse of Můstek metro station at Wenceslas Square in central Prague, during the 16th Fotograf Zone Festival, running 1–11 October 2026 under the title Wild Kin. Four projects are selected; the festival covers all costs for production, printing, installation and photodocumentation of the exhibition. Work should relate loosely to the festival theme, which asks how we perceive others — both human and non-human — and where the boundaries between humans, animals, environments and technologies lie. The exhibition space consists of sixteen vitrines measuring 147 × 75 cm, four of which are given to the selected artists. Entry is by email with three PDFs: a CV and short bio of up to 500 characters, a portfolio of previous work up to 10 MB, and a project description of up to 1,500 characters with images, also up to 10 MB, each file labelled Surname_Name plus document type. There is no limit on how many projects one author may submit, but the participation fee applies per project, and it is paid by bank transfer to the organisers rather than by card. The international jury is Lucie Černá, a Czech curator, editor and founder of untitled, an independent publishing house and platform for photography and visual art; Karina Golisová, a Slovak photographer working in documentary practices who studied at AFAD Bratislava and FAMU; Lovro Japundžić, a Zagreb-based curator whose work explores the interplay between performance and visual art; and Amelie Rose Schüle, director of Photoforum Pasquart in Biel/Bienne since 2023. Fotograf Zone has connected photography communities from Prague outward since 2002 as a magazine, gallery and international festival.
jury: Lucie Černá, curator, editor and founder, untitled
Amelie Rose Schüle, Director, Photoforum Pasquart

All work must be for sale, with a 50/50 split between artist and ArtCentre; artist cheques are issued 4 December 2026. Hand-delivered work is due 19 October, shipped work between 12 and 19 October.

calls.title: 2026 Call for Curators
